title: LSU president tries to leverage current chaos into antitrust exemption
summary: The college sports ecosystem welcomes the current chaos in part, because it justifies the ongoing effort to get an antitrust exemption from Congress.
full_text: The college sports ecosystem welcomes the current chaos in part, because it justifies the ongoing effort to get an antitrust exemption from Congress. Which, in turn, will allow the programs to partially pick the pockets of players and/or limit their freedom to hopscotch from school to school, like coaches do. That's the hidden benefit of the Brendan Sorsby controversy or the ongoing tug of war between LSU and the SEC over former NFL players returning to school. To no surprise, the statement issued on Friday by LSU president Wade Rousse includes an overt effort to parlay his school's predicament into real progress as to the bigger-picture effort to secure the exemption. "LSU respects the judicial process and the court's decision," Rousse saud. "Our responsibility is to support our programs while complying with the law and the rules governing our conference. We will carefully review the court's order and continue to work constructively with the SEC and NCAA as this matter moves forward. College football does not deserve this kind of ambiguity in eligibility standards, this is just another illustration that congress needs to pass a version of the Protect College Sports Act." Beyond making a push for a Congressional solution to the instability that the system has created, Rousse seems to be setting up an avenue for backing down and not adding former NFL players to the roster in advance of Saturday's season opener before Clemson. While coach Lane Kiffin may not care at all about the long-term relationship between LSU and the SEC, Rousse does. And in the cost-benefit analysis of creating possible irreparable harm to the relationship with the other members of its conference via the eleventh-hour addition of two players, Rousse may very well decide it's just not worth it. One way or the other, we'll have an answer today.
author: Mike Florio

title: The Athletic finally publishes its internal review of Dianna Russini
summary: It took much longer than expected.
full_text: It took much longer than expected. In the end, it didn't say much (if anything) that was unexpected. The Athletic has posted its internal review of former NFL Insider Dianna Russini's reporting, following her resignation in the wake of the revelation of her relationship with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. "Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic ’s standards," writes Mike Semel, who conducted the probe. "Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed." Semel cites the standard The Athletic believes Russini violated: “When reporting and writing stories we do not have an agenda and it is important that our readers understand that. If our readers question our adherence to that basic tenet of journalism, our credibility will be at stake. To maintain the highest form of authority we should avoid even the appearance of a conflict of interest and reveal those sources or affiliations that may put into question our ability to be credible.” Complicating the problem for Russini was the company's conclusion that she did not handle the situation in an ideal manner, once the first images of Russini with Vrabel at a resort in Arizona were published. "[W]hen first confronted with the photos by The New York Post ," Semel explains, "Russini waited two days before telling her editors and managers. She then told a story to explain the photos that did not align with facts, raising issues of trust." Semel nevertheless found few irregularities or issues that will require the attachment of an editor's note: (1) a video regarding a 2025 training-camp fight in which Vrabel "comes out as somewhat heroic" for his role in breaking it up; and (2) a blurb in a column regarding the Titans' decision to go for two in a specific game. As to the accuracy of her reporting on matters involving Vrabel, Semel cited this quote from Russini in 2023, before the Titans fired Vrabel: “Angry Tennessee Titans fans can stop hoping owner Amy Adams Strunk fires Vrabel. It’s not happening. Based on multiple conversations with high-ranking Titans officials, the franchise strongly and collectively believes it has the right coach for long-term success.” The report apparently concludes all matters between The Athletic and Russini. And it likewise concludes the story — unless and until Russini tells her version of it. If she hopes to make the biggest splash and cause the most potential chaos, Tuesday, September 8 (the night before the Patriots-Seahawks regular-season opener), continues to be the ideal date for her next move.
author: Mike Florio

title: North Carolina G.M. Michael Lombardi resigns
summary: Michael Lombardi, the longtime advisor to Bill Belichick who was recently placed on leave as North Carolina's general manager, has resigned.
full_text: Michael Lombardi, the longtime advisor to Bill Belichick who was recently placed on leave as North Carolina's general manager, has resigned. "Effective September 3, 2026, Michael Lombardi has resigned from his position as General Manager of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill's football program," North Carolina announced in a statement. "The University will continue its ongoing investigation and will consider all appropriate corrective actions responsive to the information it learns." It is still unclear why Lombardi was placed on leave, what North Carolina is investigating, or why he resigned, although the matter reportedly stems from a complaint filed by a former North Carolina employee. Less than a week ago, Lombardi's lawyer was claiming the investigation into Lombardi's conduct was a " witch hunt ." Belichick hired Lombardi shortly after becoming North Carolina's head coach. Lombardi had previously worked with Belichick in both of Belichick's NFL head-coaching stints, with the Browns and Patriots. After North Carolina won its season opener on Saturday, Belichick made a point of praising Lombardi's role in building the team. Now Lombardi is gone, and Belichick has lost one of his most trusted aides.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Mike Vrabel: I don't have any reaction to Dianna Russini report
summary: The Athletic published the findings of its internal review of Dianna Russini's reporting on Thursday, several months after the release of pictures that revealed her relationship with Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel.
full_text: The Athletic published the findings of its internal review of Dianna Russini's reporting on Thursday, several months after the release of pictures that revealed her relationship with Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. Vrabel missed the final day of the draft while undergoing counseling in the wake of the release of photos covering multiple years and the review found that their relationship "was in clear violation of The Athletic 's standards." Mike Semel, who conducted the probe, wrote that he has "not found a clear link to conclude that Russini used her platform to help promote Vrabel or help his teams" even though instances of Russini writing favorably of Vrabel come off as "awkward or even uncomfortable." At a press conference on Thursday, Vrabel was asked if he had any reaction to the findings. "No, I don't have any reaction ," Vrabel said. "We're moved on and focused on Seattle and focused on the Patriots and focused on getting better this week." It's not quite " on to Cincinnati ," but the response definitely feels like one that Vrabel's former coach Bill Belichick would give in the same situation.
author: Josh Alper

title: Falcons to induct John Abraham, Bill Fralic into their Ring of Honor
summary: The Falcons will add two former players to their Ring of Honor during the 2026 season.
full_text: The Falcons will add two former players to their Ring of Honor during the 2026 season. The team announced that they will induct defensive end John Abraham and guard Bill Fralic. The ceremony will be held during the team's October 11 game against the Ravens on Sunday Night Football . Abraham was a Jets first-round pick in 2000 and he came to the Falcons in a 2006 trade. He spent seven years with the team and was a first-team All-Pro in 2010. He recorded 68.5 sacks while in Atlanta, which is the most for any Falcons player since sacks became an official stat in 1982. Fralic was the second overall pick in 1985 and started 115 games over eight seasons with the team. He was a two-time first-team All-Pro and four-time Pro Bowler before finishing his career with one season in Detroit. Fralic died of cancer in 2018.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dianna Russini responds to internal review by The Athletic
summary: On Thursday, The Athletic published the long-awaited report of its internal investigation regarding the work of former NFL Insider Dianna Russini.
full_text: On Thursday, The Athletic published the long-awaited report of its internal investigation regarding the work of former NFL Insider Dianna Russini. The article did not include a comment from Russini. A separate article from The Athletic does. “ I stand by any and all reporting I’ve ever done in my career ," Russini said in a statement to Andrew Marchand of The Athletic , while also declining to be interviewed. The issue wasn't the accuracy of her reporting, even though The Athletic pointed out her claim that a firing of then-Titans coach Mike Vrabel was "not happening," before he was fired. The problem was that “Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation" of the publication's standards. Either way, it's the first comment she has provided on the matter since her April 14 resignation letter. It remains to be seen whether she'll fully address the situation, before or after taking another job in sports media.
author: Mike Florio

title: SEC: We disagree with the court's decision, expect our rules to be followed
summary: The SEC confirmed in a statement that it will appeal the injunction allowing two former NFL players to sign with LSU.
full_text: The SEC confirmed in a statement that it will appeal the injunction allowing two former NFL players to sign with LSU. Judge William Jorden approved a preliminary injunction Thursday that prohibits the NCAA and the SEC from punishing LSU for playing Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris. The former Ole Miss players have joined coach Lane Kiffin in Baton Rouge and have been practicing with the team since being waived out of NFL training camps, per ESPN. The SEC still hopes to prevent Wright and Harris from returning to college after signing NFL contracts. "We disagree with the court's decision," the SEC's statement reads. "The SEC's presidents and chancellors unanimously adopted a clear and reasonable standard: Member universities should not place former professional athletes on their rosters. The conference and its member universities have the right to establish, through agreed-upon governance procedures, the rules under which they voluntarily compete and to expect those rules to be followed. "The SEC will continue to defend this standard, the principle of fair competition, and the conference's authority to govern competition among its member universities."
author: Charean Williams

title: SEC plans immediate appeal of injunction in LSU case
summary: The chaos will be getting even more chaotic.
full_text: The game of legal ping-pong will continue between LSU and the SEC. Via Dan Murphy of ESPN, lawyers representing the SEC said Thursday night that they plan to file as soon as possible an appeal of the injunction allowing multiple former NFL players to sign with LSU. Time is of the essence. Friday is the deadline for adding players to the roster, and LSU by all appearances intends to include Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris on the roster for Saturday night's game against Clemson. Via Pete Thamel of ESPN, Wright said he expects to be added to the team and to play on Saturday. Thursday's decision from a Louisiana state-court judge comes on the same day the SEC filed a federal lawsuit in Alabama against LSU and coach Lane Kiffin aimed at preventing them from adding former NFL players. And so the chaos continues, with two major questions. First, how will it all resolve? Second, what will the long-term fallout between the SEC and LSU be?
author: Mike Florio

title: Availability is Chiefs OG Trey Smith's first goal as he tries to play all 17 games again
summary: Chiefs right guard Trey Smith started 67 of a possible 68 regular-season games in the first four years of his career.
full_text: Chiefs right guard Trey Smith started 67 of a possible 68 regular-season games in the first four years of his career. He missed five games last season with back spasms and ankle injuries. In the eighth practice of training camp, Smith's hip began bothering him. He finally returned to the practice field Aug. 24 and started the Chiefs' preseason finale against the Seahawks. “I just don’t like putting my teammates in a position where now they’re having to take extra reps or for me to leave my team hanging and not being at my best,” Smith said Thursday, via Pete Sweeney of the Kansas City Star . “A lot of times I’m a little hardheaded in that regard, because if I’m not at my best, it’s not the best thing for the team. There are other guys that are willing and able to do it. But I’ve just always sort of been a guy that’s like, ‘If I’m able to go, I’m going to try to go and give as much as I have, regardless.’” Smith acknowledged that no NFL player will feel 100 percent at any point in the season. He wants to be healthy enough to do his job week in and week out. “It’s just part of the job and part of the responsibility,” Smith said. “And like [Eric Bieniemy] says, ‘Hell, we signed up for it.’ So at the end of the day, I signed a contract, so it’s my job to be out there. A lot of times I’m not out there, I feel like I’m not doing my job and letting my team down and . . . [letting down] me, my coaches. And that’s just something [where] I don’t really like that feeling whatsoever.”
author: Charean Williams

title: Patriots' video tactic for field goals was, and still is, legal
summary: Ernie Adams likes that "we are deep into other peoples' heads many years later."
full_text: ' Former NFL analytics coach Ryan Paganetti made a stir recently by pointing out that the Patriots have crafted an advantage for field-goal attempts via an optical illusion on the video board. It was, and still is, perfectly legal. Via Ben Volin of the Boston Globe , the NFL confirmed Monday that the tactic falls squarely within the rules . Volin adds the text of the policy: “Video During Kicks — All video and ribbon boards must show either a static image ( e.g. , no flashing images, blinking effects, moving text/images, etc.) or an All-22 view ( e.g. , high sideline, high end zone, etc.) during field goal attempts and extra-point attempts. Any flashing, moving, or blinking text/images displayed on video boards or ribbon boards during field goal attempts and extra points are considered a violation of this policy. The prohibition will begin when the kicking team reaches the line of scrimmage and continues through the signal by the Game Officials following the kick.” And while former Patriots rules and strategy savant Ernie Adams relishes the perception that it was another stroke of genius (“[i]f nothing else,” Adams told Volin, “we are deep into other people’s heads many years later"), the truth (as we understand it) is that the idea emerged innocuously: Former Patriots kicker Stephen Gostkowski didn't like seeing an image of himself on the board before he attempted a kick. That led, eventually, to the realization that it could be turned into another edge, with the all-22 image putting four goalposts in the view of the opposing kicker, with nothing on the board when the Patriots kicked. It worked out perfectly that the video boards are in the kickers' field of vision, and it's something that perhaps teams designing new stadiums may want to try to incorporate. Unless and until the rule changes.
author: Mike Florio

title: Robert Saleh on facing Jets: We want to win Week 1, I don't hold grudges
summary: The first game of Robert Saleh's second run as an NFL head coach comes against the team that gave him his first shot at the job.
full_text: The first game of Robert Saleh's second run as an NFL head coach comes against the team that gave him his first shot at the job. Saleh's Titans will host the Jets on September 13 and that will make the first time Saleh has faced the Jets since they fired him early in the 2024 season. During a press conference this week, Saleh said that any of his personal feelings about the way things ended are not going to be on his mind heading into the game. "New York is still a special place ," Saleh said. "Gave me my first opportunity as a head coach. Our desire to win Week 1 and beat the Jets is because it's Week 1 and nothing more. I am forever grateful for all the opportunity that they gave. I don't hold grudges." The Titans have ex-Jets like Jermaine Johnson and John Franklin-Myers on the roster, but Saleh said he's not worried about their ability to "keep the main thing the main thing" when facing their former team. Given how recent seasons have gone for both clubs, the chance to get to 1-0 should offer ample incentive outside of the shared history that will be in the air.
author: Josh Alper

title: Tank Dell agrees to revised contract for 2026
summary: Wide receiver Tank Dell and the Texans have worked out a revised contract for the coming season.
full_text: Wide receiver Tank Dell and the Texans have worked out a revised contract for the coming season. Per Spotrac, Dell has agreed to a one-year, $1.7 million contract for 2026. The move comes with $1 million in guaranteed money and saves the Texans nearly $2 million in cap space. Dell has not played in a game since suffering a severe knee injury late in the 2024 season. He will miss at least the first four games of this season after going on injured reserve this week in order to give him more time to work his way back from that injury. The 2026 season is the final one on Dell's rookie contract and he'll need to make a full return in order to put himself in the mix for another deal in Houston.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bears restructure Joe Thuney, Dayo Odeyingbo, T.J. Edwards contracts
summary: The Bears have reworked several contracts to free up cap space ahead of the 2026 season.
full_text: The Bears have reworked several contracts to free up cap space ahead of the 2026 season. Field Yates of ESPN reports that they have restructured the contracts of guard Joe Thuney, defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo, and linebacker T.J. Edwards. The moves free up approximately $17 million in cap space. All three players are signed through the 2027 season and will see their cap numbers for that rise as a result of the moves. It's not clear if the Bears have an immediate use in mind for some of that cap space, but they were among the teams with the least space prior to the moves and may simply want to have the breathing room for needs that could arise during the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: D'Andre Swift left Thursday's practice due to a cramp
summary: The Bears saw two offensive players leave practice early on Thursday and a report updates the reason why one of them left the field.
full_text: The Bears saw two offensive players leave practice early on Thursday and a report updates the reason why one of them left the field. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that running back D'Andre Swift had a cramp . Reporters at the practice said that Swift was holding his midsection as he made his way to the sidelines. There's no word on Swift's outlook, but the Bears will take a few days off before returning to finalize their preparations for their Week 1 trip to Carolina and a cramp would not seem to be a long-term injury. That would be good news as Kyle Monangai is questionable to play due to a hyperextended knee. Odunze's condition has not received a similar update, but reporters at the practice said he was trying to get back into the workout so the Bears may have avoided major injuries on both fronts.
author: Josh Alper

title: 49ers announce defensive end Sam Okuayinonu will not play Thursday vs. Rams
summary: Okuayinonu did not travel with the team to Australia and will not play Week One because of a foot injury.
full_text: '' The 49ers will not have defensive end Sam Okuayinonu in their Thursday night opener against the Rams in Australia. Okuayinonu was not on the team flight to Melbourne , but the 49ers originally indicated it was possible that he could make a later flight if he made progress in his recovery from a foot injury. Today, the 49ers announced that Okuayinonu will not play. Okuayinonu is an important part of the 49ers’ defense: Last year he started 12 games in the regular season and both playoff games. This year he’s expected to be a backup but get plenty of snaps in the defensive line rotation, when he gets healthy. The rest of the 49ers' active roster made yesterday's flight to Melbourne. That includes tight end George Kittle and defensive end Nick Bosa, both of whom are rehabbing from injuries but are expected to play against the Rams.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Dan Campbell: Jared Goff is massively underrated, reminds me of Drew Brees
summary: Lions head coach Dan Campbell was briefly Drew Brees' teammate in New Orleans, and was on the Saints' coaching staff for the last five seasons of Brees' career.
full_text: Lions head coach Dan Campbell was briefly Drew Brees' teammate in New Orleans, and was on the Saints' coaching staff for the last five seasons of Brees' career. And Campbell says that in Detroit today, he sees a quarterback who reminds him of Brees. Some might say Jared Goff hasn't earned the comparison to Brees, who was elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame on the first ballot this year. Campbell says Goff absolutely has. "I mean, he is massively underrated ," Campbell said of Goff, via Albert Breer of SI.com. "This is a quarterback that plays the quarterback position—he knows how to play quarterback. When you gotta have it, [he] can stand in the pocket, make an accurate throw, an accurate read, and that’s what the quarterback position is. And he’s a rare breed of man.” Campbell said Goff can read defenses as well as any quarterback. "His processing speed reminds me of Brees. He sees it, he sees it. And every year it’s gotten faster and faster. And then watch him under duress. Nobody makes a more accurate throw under duress than Jared Goff," Campbell said. Campbell and Goff are heading into their sixth season together in Detroit, and although they've already turned the franchise around, Campbell believes Goff's best football is still ahead of him.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Deion Sanders and Colorado start 1-0 with last-second win at Georgia Tech
summary: Coming off an ugly 3-9 season in 2025, Sanders is off to a strong start in 2026 after a big win in Atlanta.
full_text: '' Deion Sanders' fourth season as head coach at Colorado is off to a promising start. Sanders' team started 1-0 with a 14-13 win at Georgia Tech, in a wild ending that saw both teams block field goals in the fourth quarter and Colorado score a go-ahead touchdown in the final minute. The game ended when Colorado blocked Georgia Tech's game-winning field goal attempt as time expired. After going 3-9 last season, Sanders was heavily scrutinized, and there was talk that he could be on the hot seat if his team didn't improve this year. Sanders said afterward that he doesn't care about that talk. "I want to win, man. I don't give a damn — they talked about me when I came out of the womb," Sanders said. "This is a big win for these kids." Colorado was a 6.5-point underdog heading into the game, but Sanders' defense kept Georgia Tech's offense (led by quarterback Alberto Mendoza, brother of Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza) out of the end zone. Georgia Tech's only touchdown came on a 100-yard kickoff return. The win came on Georgia Tech's home field in Atlanta, the city where Sanders had many of his greatest moments as a player, both in the NFL with the Falcons and in Major League Baseball with the Braves. Sanders was asked after the game where that win ranks among his greatest moments in Atlanta. "I don't rank moments," Sanders said. "I try to turn them into monuments."
author: Michael David Smith

title: Von Miller gives Hunter Luepke "chicken for life" in exchange for No. 40
summary: Cowboys outside linebacker Von Miller and his teammate, Hunter Luepke, were playing a game of chicken with the No. 40.
full_text: '' Cowboys outside linebacker Von Miller and his teammate, Hunter Luepke, were playing a game of chicken with the No. 40. Miller wanted it; Luepke, a fullback, has had it since 2023. Both wore the number in training camp, but a decision had to be made Thursday about who would wear 40 in the regular season since the NFL doesn't allow for duplicate numbers. Miller finally blinked, giving up a percentage of his chicken company in exchange for the number he wore in high school, college and with the Rams and Bills. Luepke will switch to 30. “You got to give Hunter a great [shout] out,” Miller said, via Jon Machota of TheAthletic.com. “He’s learned from the best with the negotiators here with the Cowboys. It went down to the final hour, but we were able to get it done. I don’t want to get into the details of it, but I’m happy to say he’s my business partner. He’s a part owner of Greener Pastures Chicken. The chicken of champions .” Patrick Mahomes, Drew Brees and Nick Foles are among other current and former players who have a stake in the USDA-certified organic poultry processing facility in Elgin, Texas. “[Luepke] was a great fit for us,” said Miller, who majored in poultry science at Texas A&M. “It was a great fit for him. I’m happy that we were able to get it done.”
author: Charean Williams

title: DE Azeez Ojulari, OL Evan Neal, WR Ronnie Bell sign with Raiders' practice squad
summary: The Raiders worked out 16 players on Thursday.
full_text: The Raiders worked out 16 players on Thursday. They signed three. Wide receiver Ronnie Bell, offensive lineman Evan Neal and defensive end Azeez Ojulari are staying in Vegas to join the team's practice squad. In corresponding moves, the Raiders released defensive end Jahfari Harvey, offensive tackle Kamar Missouri and tight end Albert Okwuegbunam. The Giants released Neal on Sunday. He has not played since 2024. The Giants selected him seventh overall in the 2022 draft, and he began his career at right tackle. The Giants moved him to right guard, and he did not play a snap there last season. He ended his Giants career with 29 games played, including 27 starts. The Giants selected Ojulari in the second round of the 2021 draft, and he played four seasons in New York. He spent last season with the Eagles but played only three games. The Falcons signed him in March but terminated his contract on Sunday. In 49 games over five seasons, Ojulari has totaled 113 tackles, 22 sacks and 38 quarterback hits. The 49ers selected Bell in the seventh round of the 2023 draft. He has appeared in 28 career games for the 49ers and Saints, catching 10 passes for 113 yards and four touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Judge grants injunction allowing LSU to sign former NFL players
summary: LSU, SEC continue on a collision course.
full_text: Get more popcorn ready. Via Pete Thamel of ESPN, Judge William Jorden has converted a temporary restraining order into an injunction. More than 40 athletes now have both NCAA and SEC eligibility. The ruling allows multiple potential players who spent time on 90-man NFL rosters to join LSU for the 2026 season. The deadline for adding them to the roster arrives on Friday. If LSU goes through with it, the SEC will undoubtedly look for avenues to respond, perhaps very aggressively, to the move. The SEC reportedly has considered "extreme measures" against LSU if it welcomes former NFL players — up to and including expulsion from the conference. On Thursday, the SEC filed a federal lawsuit aimed at preventing LSU from signing former pro players.
author: Mike Florio

title: Greg Schiano on the hot seat after Rutgers loses to 29-point underdog UMass
summary: Greg Schiano is officially on the hot seat at Rutgers.
full_text: Greg Schiano is officially on the hot seat at Rutgers. Schiano, the former Buccaneers head coach who is in Year Seven of his second stint at Rutgers, has opened this season with perhaps the worst loss of his coaching career. Playing at home against a UMass squad that went 0-12 last year, Rutgers lost 37-21. How shocking is that result? UMass was a 29-point underdog heading into tonight's game. UMass was widely viewed as one of the worst teams in the nation heading into this season. UMass hadn't beaten an FBS opponent since 2023. And now UMass has gone on the road and beaten Rutgers easily. The 60-year-old Schiano first became head coach at Rutgers in 2001, when the Scarlet Knights were a bottom-feeder program, and steadily built his team up to the point where it went 11-2 in 2006 and he was named college football's Coach of the Year. After the 2011 season, Schiano was hired to be head coach of the Buccaneers, but he was fired after his two seasons in Tampa Bay resulted in two last-place finishes in the NFC South. In 2020, Schiano became head coach at Rutgers again, but he hasn't achieved the same kind of success in his second stint at Rutgers as he did in his first. Now his status at Rutgers looks tenuous. He's going to need to turn things around in a hurry to save his job.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Cowboys create more than $19 million in cap space with restructurings
summary: With the regular season approaching, the Cowboys have maneuvered to create some extra cap space.
full_text: With the regular season approaching, the Cowboys have maneuvered to create some extra cap space. Via Todd Archer of ESPN, the team has restructured the contracts of defensive tackle Kenny Clark, cornerback DaRon Bland, and tight end Jake Ferguson. The moves have created more than $19 million in additional 2026 cap space. Previously, the Cowboys had approximately $14.2 million in spending room. With more than $30 million in 2026 cap space now on hand, the Cowboys have plenty of space to absorb a veteran contract (or two) via trade. Coincidentally, or not, Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby has a 2026 base salary of $30 million. Just saying.
author: Mike Florio

title: Seahawks' new ownership group has 12 limited partners
summary: It's fitting that the new owners of the team known for the 12th man have a group of 12 limited partners.
full_text: It's fitting that the new owners of the team known for the 12th man have a group of 12 limited partners. Ben Fischer of Sports Business Journal has the full list . They are: former Sequoia Capital Managing Partner Mark Stevens; the Aramburuzabala family (descendants of the founder of Grupo Modelo; Val Blavatnik (son of DAZN owner Len Blavatnik); Sheryl Sokoloff (wife of Jonathan Sokoloff, co-managing partner of private equity firm Leonard Green & Partners); Gonzalo Hevia Baillères; Heavy Metal Equipment & Rentals CEO Jesse van der Werf, who is Canadian; Khosla Ventures managing director Samir Kaul; Apptio co-founder and CEO Sunny Gupta; Frazier Healthcare Partners managing partner Nader Naini; former U.S. secretary of commerce Penny Pritzker; Carlyle Dynasty Equity Group; and Sixth Street. The percentages of the team owned by the various limited partners were not disclosed. By rule, the Khosla family was required to purchase 30 percent of the team, absent investors or debt. At a purchase price of $9.612 billion, this means that the Khoslas were required to pay at least $2.88 billion. That leaves up to $6.7284 billion to be raised from limited partners.
author: Mike Florio

title: UNC investigation turns attention to Steve Belichick, others
summary: The probe expands before now-former G.M. Michael Lombardi.
full_text: '' The investigation that resulted in the resignation of North Carolina G.M. Michael Lombardi seems to be expanding. Via WRAL, lawyers hired to conduct the probe have now focused on Tar Heels defensive coordinator Steve Belichick, who is currently on medical leave. Steve Belichick previously served as the Patriots' defensive coordinator, when his father, Bill, was the head coach. Per the report, investigators are questioning witnesses regarding whether Steve Belichick "used drugs on the job or provided drugs to at least one player." The investigation separately is exploring whether an unnamed member of the North Carolina recruiting staff had a sexual relationship with a player, according to the report. Lawyers also have inquired about possible sexual relationships between assistant coaches and the recruiting staff. Subjects of the interviews include current and former Tar Heels players, parents, and staff members. The investigation also targets documents and screenshots of text conversations. Although head coach Bill Belichick has not been identified as a focal point of the investigation, he's the captain of the ship. And the ship, from a cultural standpoint, seems to be sinking.
author: Mike Florio

title: Stephen Jones: It will be "real difficult" to keep both George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb long term
summary: Not even a month ago, Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones called it "realistic" for the team to think it can keep CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens long term.
full_text: Not even a month ago, Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones called it " realistic " for the team to think it can keep CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens long term. This week, Jones admitted keeping both wide receivers beyond 2026 will be challenging. "I don't know of any teams that really can pay two top receivers top of the market, so that's gonna be a real difficult situation as we move forward," Jones told the DLLS Cowboys podcast. "We've managed to figure out how we can do it for this year. If everything works out the way we think it is, [in] which CeeDee and George both have huge years again, then it’ll be a bigger challenge next year.” Before the 2024 season, Lamb signed a four-year, $136 million extension. His $34 million annual average ranks sixth at the position. Pickens will play this season under the one-year, $27.3 million franchise tag. He is coming off a career year when he made 93 catches for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns. "George is really wanting to put back-to-back years on top of one another, so it'll help his market,” Jones said. “And certainly, I know at some point -- as does every player in this league -- will want to be rewarded with a long-term contract. So that certainly puts pressure on us to have a unique situation there at wide receiver.” The Bengals managed to pay Ja'Marr Chase (four-year, $161 million extension signed in 2025) and Tee Higgins (four-year, $115 million extension signed in 2025), and the Eagles paid A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith before trading Brown this offseason. But Pickens will want — and will deserve — more than Higgins or Smith if he has another year like last year. The Cowboys hope they face that problem in the offseason, because that will mean Lamb and Pickens both had solid seasons again. “[Cowboys defensive coordinator] Christian Parker will tell you, who went against us twice a year, what a challenge that it was for the Eagles when they played us, and he was on the defensive side of the ball trying to defend Dak [Prescott] and those two receivers,” Jones said.
author: Charean Williams

title: Tutu Atwell on Rams return: I feel like I never left
summary: Wide receiver Tutu Atwell moved on from the Rams in free agency this year, so he was taken by surprise when Rams head coach Sean McVay told him that he was heading back to the team last week.
full_text: Wide receiver Tutu Atwell moved on from the Rams in free agency this year, so he was taken by surprise when Rams head coach Sean McVay told him that he was heading back to the team last week. The Dolphins traded Atwell to the Rams for running back Jarquez Hunter — who didn't wind up making Miami's 53-man roster — and the wideout said he was "shocked" to hear the news. Once that feeling went away, Atwell immediately felt back at home after five seasons with the team. “Nah, man, it don’t feel like I was gone ,” Atwell said, via Greg Beachem of the Associated Press. “I’m back with my brothers, man. I just feel great and feel awesome just to be back here and with these great players and guys. I’m just excited.” McVay said the trade was not made with an eye on Puka Nacua being suspended and the team's unsettled third receiver spot is where Atwell could make his mark in his second run with the Rams. He'll need a return to the production that resulted in 81 catches in 2023 and 2024, so the familiarity with the offense should be a plus as he reintroduces himself to the team.
author: Josh Alper

title: Raiders work out 16 players, including OL Evan Neal, WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling
