title: Why the Bengals may choose not to extend DJ Turner, Dax Hill, or Chase Brown right now
summary: With the 2026 NFL season almost here, the Cincinnati Bengals have yet to hammer out new deals for three of their top impending free agents. A recent report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler suggests that the team is unlikely to get a contract extension done for fourth-year cornerback DJ Turner before Week 1. Because the team […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OH - OCTOBER 16: Cincinnati Bengals running back Chase Brown (30) carries the ball during the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals on October 16, 2025, at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, OH. (Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With the 2026 NFL season almost here, the Cincinnati Bengals have yet to hammer out new deals for three of their top impending free agents. A recent report from ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler suggests that the team is unlikely to get a contract extension done for fourth-year cornerback DJ Turner before Week 1. Because the team typically doesn’t get big extensions done in-season, this would likely mean Turner plays out the final year of his rookie contract. He’s not the only cornerback up for a new deal. Former first-round pick Dax Hill is set to play this season under the fifth-year option, and there hasn’t been anything to suggest that the team is close to signing him to an extension either. Finally, there’s Chase Brown, one of the NFL’s best running backs who’s still on a rookie contract. Back in January, there was a report from ESPN’s Ben Baby that Brown and the Bengals were working on a new deal, but since then, it’s been mostly crickets. With Week 1 vs. Tampa Bay kicking off soon, it appears there’s a very real chance that none of these three key players will get a new deal. While that will certainly cause some controversy, at least in the public eye, there are actually reasonable explanations as to why no new deals may occur. DJ Turner and the franchise tag Between the three, Turner is the only one who looks worthy of the franchise tag, as he performed like a top-tier cornerback last year. However, that was the first full season Turner has put together since being a second-round pick out of Michigan in the 2023 NFL Draft. He had some nice flashes in Year 1, then appeared to be making the jump midway through his second season before suffering a season-ending shoulder injury. While 2025 was a great year for Turner, it’s the only complete year he’s had to this point, so you can’t exactly blame the Bengals for wanting to see him do it for at least one more season before potentially paying him like one of the league’s best cornerbacks. Then comes the franchise tag. So long as Turner continues to play at a high level, the Bengals have the franchise tag in their back pocket when next offseason kicks off. This approach would be similar to what the Bengals did with Jessie Bates and Tee Higgins in recent years. Bates was tagged and allowed to walk, while Higgins was actually tagged twice before getting a long-term extension. So technically, the Bengals are 1-for-2 when it comes to big-name players getting the tag recently. Unless something disastrous happens or someone makes a crazy trade offer for the talented defender, there’s a good chance Turner is still playing for the Bengals when the 2027 season kicks off. Dax Hill and an incomplete resume While Turner has consistently shown promise since being drafted, the same cannot be said of Hill. After a disastrous two-year stint at safety to begin his career, Hill spent the next two seasons bouncing between slot and boundary cornerback, the latter being where he’s currently settled. It was a rocky road for Hill to endure, with many calling him a bust until he turned the corner last season. Problem is, Hill still doesn’t have a full season of good tape on the boundary, which makes it hard for the Bengals to give him any type of extension, especially one that pays him more than the $12.6 million he’s collecting this year on the fifth-year option. Anything he signs would likely need to average at least that over the life of the deal, and frankly, Hill likely hasn’t done enough in the Bengals’ eyes to warrant that type of deal. They weren’t even willing to pay Myles Murphy the fifth-year option of his rookie deal this year, which would have been $14.4 million, and Murphy has a better resume than that of Hill. Then there’s the injury concern. Hill missed all but five games in the 2024 season with a torn ACL. He rebounded with a solid 2025 season, only to miss most of training camp and the preseason this year with a hamstring injury. While it would be nice to extend Hill, it’s easy to see why the best scenario is probably for him to just play out this year and hope the two sides can hammer something out next offseason. Chase Brown and a devalued position Of the Bengals’ big three when it comes to impending free agents, one could argue Brown has the best overall resume. The 2023 fifth-round pick out of Illinois has amassed 2,806 scrimmage yards and 22 total touchdowns over the last two seasons and could be primed for his best year yet behind what should be the Bengals’ best o-line he’s run behind. Unfortunately for Brown, he plays a position that’s been widely devalued across the league. Smaller two- and three-year deals have become the norm, even for top-end running backs. And while Brown is good, he’s not in the elite tier of running backs like Saquon Barkley, Bijan Robinson, Jahmyr Gibbs, and Derrick Henry. One other worry I could see for the Bengals: Brown already has a lot of wear on his tires and is at the age where many running backs’ production begins to decline. He amassed 734 plays from scrimmage over his five-year college career, including 328 rushes in his final season at Illinois. He’s now 26 years old (turns 27 next March) and already has 642 plays from scrimmage in the NFL. Earlier this year, Apex Fantasy Leagues released a study showing a sharp decline in running backs’ peak seasons after they turned 27. If Brown were to sign just a two-year extension, he would turn 28 before the 2028 season even kicks off. So even a short-term deal has a very real chance of not paying off for a Bengals team that’s going to be tight on money with so many big-name players on the roster. While it would certainly be a setback for the Bengals to not get any new deals done for their big three impending free agents, it’s easy to see why they may very well do it. And after an offseason that saw them shell out big money to upgrade the defense, this is more than just a ‘they’re being cheap’ situation. They’ve proven they’re willing to spend big. This may simply be a scenario where they feel spending right now isn’t the best approach.
author: Jason Marcum

title: DJ Turner opens up about contract talks, which may be headed toward familiar territory for the Bengals
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have spent the offseason rebuilding their defense with the expectation that the unit can finally help push the team back into postseason contention. But as the regular season approaches, one important defensive storyline appears increasingly likely to carry over into 2027. That would be the future of cornerback DJ Turner II. Turner […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - OCTOBER 16: DJ Turner II #20 of the Cincinnati Bengals celebrates an interception during the NFL 2025 game between Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on October 16, 2025 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals have spent the offseason rebuilding their defense with the expectation that the unit can finally help push the team back into postseason contention. But as the regular season approaches, one important defensive storyline appears increasingly likely to carry over into 2027. That would be the future of cornerback DJ Turner II. Turner is entering the final season of his rookie contract after emerging as one of the Bengals’ most important defensive players in 2025. Unfortunately for Cincinnati, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the two sides are nowhere close to reaching a long-term agreement before the start of the season. In fact, Fowler’s assessment is about as definitive as it gets. “This deal has virtually no chance to get done before Week 1, barring a massive and unexpected uptick. It isn’t close, and Turner is poised to play out his rookie deal.” That’s obviously not what Bengals fans would like to hear about a player who appears to have developed into a legitimate No. 1 cornerback. But it also shouldn’t come as a complete surprise. Turner Has Become Exactly What Cincinnati Needed When the Bengals selected Turner in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft, his elite athleticism and speed made him an intriguing developmental prospect. The development happened quickly. After battling for a starting role entering the 2025 season, Turner became a fixture in the Bengals’ secondary and ultimately started 16 games. He was regularly tasked with following opposing teams’ top receivers and produced some of the best coverage numbers in the league. According to Next Gen Stats, Turner led all NFL cornerbacks with a 27.7% hawk rate in 2025. He also tied for third among cornerbacks with 18 pass breakups. His traditional statistics were impressive as well: 40 tackles, two interceptions, two forced fumbles, and 18 passes defended in 17 games. And perhaps most importantly, the Bengals trusted him to take on the difficult assignments. That’s what makes the current contract situation so significant. Cincinnati finally appears to have found a young corner capable of handling the responsibilities that come with being a team’s top outside cover man. Now the Bengals have to determine just how much they’re willing to pay him. The Price of Doing Business Has Changed One of the complications is that the cornerback market has exploded. Fowler notes that the top 10 cornerback contracts currently average approximately $24.7 million per season. That means the Bengals aren’t negotiating against the market they faced just a few years ago. They’re negotiating against a rapidly escalating one. The Rams recently made Trent McDuffie the highest-paid cornerback in the NFL at $31 million per year. Other elite corners have also pushed the market beyond the $30 million annual threshold. Turner doesn’t necessarily need to reach that level for his next contract to represent a major financial commitment. And that’s where Cincinnati’s dilemma comes into focus. The Bengals have already made enormous financial commitments to Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. The organization also has to account for other important players who will need new contracts in the coming years. Fowler points out that Cincinnati could therefore decide to follow a strategy it has used before. The Jessie Bates Blueprint If the Bengals can’t reach an agreement with Turner before the season, Fowler believes the franchise tag could become a legitimate possibility next offseason. That should sound familiar to Bengals fans. Cincinnati used the franchise tag on Jessie Bates III in 2022. Bates ultimately played under the tag before leaving Cincinnati in free agency the following offseason and signing a four-year deal with the Atlanta Falcons. The Bengals also used the tag on Higgins twice before eventually reaching a long-term agreement with him. Obviously, cornerback is a different position than that of safety and/or wide receiver, and the Bengals have traditionally held differing opinions on the respective values of those spots. But there is precedent for Cincinnati allowing a player to enter the final year of his contract, using the franchise tag as a bridge and attempting to negotiate a long-term deal later. The difference this time is that Turner plays one of the most valuable positions on the defense. If he puts together another Pro Bowl-caliber season, his price could become even more expensive. Turner Doesn’t Sound Concerned Interestingly, Turner doesn’t appear to be approaching the situation with the same urgency that fans might. Earlier this offseason, he made it clear that he wants to remain in Cincinnati but intends to let his representation handle the business side. His focus is elsewhere. “I’m not even getting into all that — for real,” Turner told ESPN during offseason workouts. “I’m just taking care of myself.” Turner also made it clear that he wasn’t satisfied with what he accomplished in 2025. “Last year was cool, but there’s so much more I’m trying to do,” he said. “So much more. I left a whole bunch of plays on the field last year.” Then on Thursday, Turner was asked about Fowler’s ESPN report and had this to say (via Mike Petraglia): “If I got a contract right now, I got a contract yesterday or tomorrow, I’ll be the same,” Turner said, later adding, “As I said, my mindset is gonna be the same, regardless if I’m the highest-paid (cornerback) or I don’t have a contract. It doesn’t really matter. “Just get better every week. Get better every week and win. That’s really all you’re gonna ask for.” DJ Turner on @JFowlerESPN report that barring an unexpected breakthrough, Bengals expected to let him play out his contract “My mindset is gonna be the same regardless. If I’m the highest paid, or I don't have a contract. It don't really matter.” pic.twitter.com/JD1Bk3GqYB — Mike Petraglia (@Trags) September 3, 2026 That mentality could ultimately be exactly what Cincinnati wants to hear. Turner isn’t entering the season trying to prove that he’s worth a certain contract. He’s entering it trying to become a better football player. Cincinnati Has a Big Decision Coming The Bengals have plenty of reasons to want Turner around for the long haul. He’s young. He’s athletic. He’s already demonstrated that he can cover top receivers. And he’s entering his prime as Cincinnati’s defense gets significantly more talented around him. But the economics are complicated. Fowler’s report suggests the Bengals and Turner are far enough apart that there is essentially no chance of a deal being completed before Week 1. That means the decision may simply be postponed. Cincinnati could let Turner play out the final year of his rookie contract, see whether he can replicate his 2025 breakout, and then determine whether the franchise tag—or a massive long-term contract—is the best way to proceed. The risk, of course, is that Turner has another monster season and makes himself even more expensive. The potential reward is that the Bengals get another year of evaluation before making what could be one of the largest defensive investments in franchise history. Either way, this doesn’t appear to be a contract situation that’s going away anytime soon. For now, Turner seems perfectly comfortable letting his play do the talking. And if he plays the way he did last season—or takes another step forward—the Bengals are going to have a very expensive decision to make.

full_text: Tennessee Titans cornerback Elijah Molden (24) tries to navigate around Indianapolis Colts offensive tackle Blake Freeland (73) but is unable to get the first down Sunday, Dec. 3, 2023, at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tenn. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co On Tuesday, the Cincinnati Bengals finished filling out their 16-player practice squad. They announced three outside additions from other teams, those being offensive tackle Blake Freeland, cornerback Trikweze Bridges, and defensive end Garmon Randolph. Freeland is the most likely to see a path to being called up to the 53-man roster early in the season, with the question marks at the swing tackle spot. Blake Freeland’s Resume Freeland is a 25-year-old who played college football at BYU. He had actually been a quarterback originally for his first couple of seasons in high school before switching to tight end as a junior and senior. At BYU, he switched to the offensive line. That athleticism still showed up when he jumped a 37” vertical at the NFL Scouting Combine, a record that still stands for offensive linemen. Freeland was selected by the Indianapolis Colts in the 4th round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He played in just over 700 snaps during his rookie season. He played in 16 games that season, starting in nine of them. He had starts at both left and right tackle that year. Freeland’s ability to play on either side was likely a selling point for Scott Peters and the rest of the Bengals offensive staff. Went back and watched new Bengals offensive tackle Blake Freeland (#73) as a rookie versus Cincinnati in 2023. pic.twitter.com/zkK79vS2ez — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 1, 2026 Freeland only played in 23 total snaps during his second season with the Colts. Then he fractured his leg in the preseason before the 2025 season began. Freeland did play in 153 snaps during this preseason. He finished with a really impressive 74.5 run-blocking grade per PFF. On the flip side, his pass blocking grade was a 43.1 this preseason. Going back and watching the tape, I haven’t seen it be nearly that bad, so take the pass-blocking grade with a giant grain of salt. Blake Freeland’s (#73) 1st half snaps vs. New England in preseason Week 1. I don’t know Clark, looks pretty good to me.. pic.twitter.com/qJAv7I62BZ — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 1, 2026 Freeland still has some concerns with handling NFL power. Weighing just 302 pounds, his anchor strength consistency is a concern. He does have excellent athleticism, good length with almost 34” arms, and impressive leg drive as a run blocker. The 6’8” Freeland was not claimed off of waivers. Ultimately, he landed in Cincinnati as a member of the practice squad. With actual NFL playing experience at tackle, it wouldn’t be a bit surprising if Freeland ends up being the swing tackle for the Bengals once he is up to speed on the playbook. What are your thoughts on the addition of Blake Freeland? Will he be able to come in and quickly earn the swing tackle spot over Foster, Rivers, and Hinton? Sound off in the comments.

title: Browns new DE Sam Williams: Everything you need to know from childhood to the pros
summary: The Cleveland Browns made a tweak here and there after the initial 53-man roster was decided and approved. RELATED: BROWNS HAVE A STRATEGY THAT JUST COULD WORK Then came the arduous creation of this year’s practice squad, which is composed of 16 players, plus one if the athlete has any international distinction. CB Michael Coats, […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Sam Williams #54 of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during the second quarter during the NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns made a tweak here and there after the initial 53-man roster was decided and approved. RELATED: BROWNS HAVE A STRATEGY THAT JUST COULD WORK Then came the arduous creation of this year’s practice squad, which is composed of 16 players, plus one if the athlete has any international distinction . CB Michael Coats, Jr. was impressive in training camp, made the final cut, was waived, then signed to the practice squad . DT Kalia Davis also found IR his new home with a quad issue. With these recent transactions, roster holes were created. GM Andrew Berry then signed DE Sam Williams and CB Noah Igbinoghene to replace the Coats and Davis. This year’s defensive front has possible issues creating a good pass rusher opposite EDGE rusher Jared Verse. Williams was signed to assist in this area. But who is Williams? What does he offer the Browns? Beginnings Williams grew up in Montgomery, Alabama, and attended Robert E. Lee High School after transferring from Marbury High School in Deatsville, Alabama. Football was always a part of Williams’ life. As a kid about six years old, he would stand in the backyard and throw the football over the house, then race around to the front yard and try to catch the pass. But at the age of seven years old, Williams and his siblings were taken from their mother and placed in the care of his grandparents. Later, an aunt would raise the children. They lived in Montgomery while their mother, TaTanisha Williams, lived and worked in Birmingham, just 90 miles away. Her work schedule included 12-hour shifts, so she never made the journey to Montgomery to see her son play defensive end on Friday nights. Williams had plenty of interest from colleges, but his grades weren’t up to par. So, he accepted an invitation to compete on the football team with Northeast Mississippi Community College in Booneville. By the time his sophomore year rolled around, Williams was a bona fide star player at this level. In that season alone, he had 75 total tackles, 17.5 sacks, 28.5 tackles for loss, 4 forced fumbles, and 1 fumble recovery in just nine games. Williams earned First Team NJCAA All-American Honors and was voted MACJC “Defensive Lineman of the Year.” The distance from Birmingham to Booneville is two hours and 42 minutes. He had offers from Oregon, Texas A&M, Old Dominion, Kentucky, Florida Atlantic, Ole Miss, Tennessee, Auburn, Florida, Southern Miss, LSU, and Florida State. He committed to Ole Miss on June 21, 2018. Ole Miss played a 3-4 on defense, and yet Williams was able to get a consistent pass rusher despite the extra blocker. In Week 2 of the 2019 season, his mother traveled to Oxford, Mississippi, and watched her son’s team prevail 31-17 over Arkansas. Williams had two tackles, one sack, and 1.5 tackles for loss. No one understands how much this means to me. I know I made her proud last night. I love my momma 💙😭 pic.twitter.com/T1zX1FWgag — SAM WILLIAMS SR (@DegarrickSamuel) September 8, 2019 By the time his Ole Miss career had concluded, Williams had 134 total tackles, 31.5 tackles for loss, 1 interception, 1 pass defense, 6 forced fumbles, 20.5 sacks, 16 pressures, 1 scoop-and-score, and 1 fumble recovery with a 40 time of 4.46. He was named First Team All-SEC and Third Team All-American. During his senior year, he was arrested for felony sexual battery, but later the charges were dropped. On to the NFL The Dallas Cowboys selected Williams (6’-4”, 260 pounds) in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft. His rookie deal was for four years, worth $6.53 million, and a signing bonus of $2.998 million, with the same amount guaranteed. As a rookie, he placed sixth in the voting for the “NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year” award. He missed all of 2024 with a torn ACL and a partial tear of his MCL. This all occurred in training camp, and he spent the season on IR doing rehab. For the other three seasons in Dallas, he had 85 total tackles (with a high of 37 in 2025), 9.5 sacks, 22 tackles for loss, 20 QB hits, 4 fumble recoveries, three batted passes, 1 forced fumble, 15 hurries, 11 knockdowns, 36 pressures, and 8 missed tackles. Last year he had just one sack, and coming into 2026 he inked a one-year deal worth $2.5 million following the expiration of his 4-year rookie contract. Going into training camp this July, he was almost giddy with excitement to get back on the field and start practicing. He displayed a hunger and got weekly praise from the coaching staff. They played him quite a bit on special teams, and he had a blocked punt against the Detroit Lions. In the preseason games, he was ranked #2 against the New Orleans Saints with six total tackles and one sack. Against the Arizona Cardinals, Williams had one sack, one tackle for loss, and four total tackles. In the opening contest versus the Seattle Seahawks, he had just two tackles. At the end of this year’s training camp, he was released on the final cutdown. Two days later, Berry signed Williams. What should Browns fans expect from Williams? When DE Alex Wright was lost for the season after he suffered a torn Achilles, there was an immediate need, obviously. Berry then signed free agent Derek Barnett, who is a former first-round draft pick. But Barnett wasn’t signed by any other NFL club waiting for a call because his last few years have had limited production. But he is a solid player with plenty of experience and a healthy body. The definition of "just like they drew it up." No resistance from the Cowboys' defense. Toia gets reached. William was taken out of the play. Second-level blocks executed. pic.twitter.com/lwoqtXN04s — Mauricio Rodríguez (@MauNFL) October 13, 2025 Williams is basically in “prove it” mode. He showed flashes with the Cowboys, had an entire year off, then did not play well last year. Dallas then gave him their own one-year “prove-it” deal, and was cut. It was assumed that they would then sign him to their practice squad, but Berry needed a healthy body and got him instead. He will need to carve out a depth role on the Browns. Williams won’t be expected to become the starter and destroy an opponent’s offensive backfield. Right now, he is simply an able body that has talent and will need to rekindle the success he has had in the past. Cleveland’s pass rush group has many question marks. Their setup beyond Jared Verse is unsettled. Isaiah McGuire is now the default starter opposite Verse, with Barnett listed as his backup. When Verse needs time to rest, it will be Williams now slated to come in. After that, at defensive end, the coaching staff has DTs Adin Huntington and perhaps Mike Hall to swing outside. On the practice squad are Sam Kamara, Logan Fano, Tyreak Sapp, and Khordae Sydnor. Williams will aim to at least operate on a rotational basis with Cleveland. He is athletic and has high-end physical traits. He hasn’t shown much as far as consistency with the pass rush and is a decent run-support guy, although he struggled with this early on at the NFL level. Quickness is his best friend, along with his long arms (33 1/8”), vertical jump (36”), wide wingspan (6’-8 1/4”), and is very strong. He once recorded a deadlift of 750 pounds. No, not a misprint. With Dallas, he posted a 12.8% pass-rush win rate as an edge defender. That was before his knee injury, so what has changed? The Cowboys simply gave up on him by inking him to only a one-year deal, then releasing him after a good camp. Williams will need to maintain gap integrity, which has been an issue for him. He resorts to straight-on rushing instead of using techniques to go inside or spin to the outer edge in order to lose the block. Plus, he lacks a polished pass-rushing plan. For the Browns, Williams has a constant…

full_text: It could be a long season ahead for the Cleveland Browns, but those first few weeks can go a long way toward setting the tone for what the rest of the season will look like. The Browns have a pretty favorable schedule overall , but they’ll have some tough matchups to deal with early in the season. Cleveland’s first home game in Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers is likely their most winnable game in the first quarter. The Panthers finished 8-9 in 2025, compared to the Browns’ opening matchup, the Jacksonville Jaguars, who finished 13-4 last season. The Week 2 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers will also be a challenge for several reasons. The Buccaneers have been one of the NFL’s more competitive teams in recent years, and this one won’t be easy with the Browns heading on the road to face Baker Mayfield – a matchup that comes with plenty of history. The pressure of that matchup alone could make things more challenging. The home environment in Week 3 should also work in the Browns’ favor, with an energized crowd giving the team a boost on both sides of the ball. On that same note, the Week 4 Thursday Night Football matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers is another opportunity for the team to get a win. While those AFC North matchups are always competitive, Cleveland has had some success against the Steelers in Thursday Night Football over the years. Games against Pittsburgh are always unpredictable, so a win is certainly not a guarantee. title: One outlet has extreme confidence in Dallas against the Giants
summary: Bucky Brooks of NFL.com believes the Dallas Cowboys are true Super Bowl contenders this season. And Jerry Jones, head cheerleader for the Dallas Cowboys, is confident the Cowboys can compete for a Super Bowl in 2026. “I feel like we’ve got a chance to really be good,” Jones said. “It’s going to be hard… Bottom […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - JANUARY 04: Brian Burns #0 of the New York Giants and Dak Prescott #4 of the Dallas Cowboys interact during the game at MetLife Stadium on January 04, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The New York Giants won 34-17. (Photo by Ishika Samant/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bucky Brooks of NFL.com believes the Dallas Cowboys are true Super Bowl contenders this season. And Jerry Jones, head cheerleader for the Dallas Cowboys, is confident the Cowboys can compete for a Super Bowl in 2026. “I feel like we’ve got a chance to really be good,” Jones said. “It’s going to be hard… Bottom line is, I love the excitement. [The media], for all practical purposes, don’t expect us to be a contender in the Super Bowl. Y’all don’t. Why would you? I like that, I do. I like that, and I like what we’ve put together to show you that we can do it.” The Cowboys hype has even prompted Adam Schefter to issue a warning to Stephen A. Smith . I got some bad news for Stephen A. Smith: The Dallas Cowboys are coming. They are coming this year and Stephen A. is gonna be tested. I’m telling you right now, it’s gonna be a long, anxious, nervous year for Stephen A. Smith. Be ready. Be that as it may, the Super Bowl is still far away, but the journey starts in Week 1. And for the season opener, the Cowboys are clear favorites against the Giants, at least according to NFL.com. All but one of their 10 panelists are projecting the Cowboys to win their season opener . Cowboys-Giants predictions are in. Football is so back! pic.twitter.com/8T1JmZpHsz — SleeperCowboys (@SleeperCowboys) September 2, 2026 Expectations are high for Dallas, and not just for the season opener. NFL.com gathered 19 of their analysts to predict this year’s division winners , and they have the Cowboys taking the NFC East. NFC EAST CHAMPS: Dallas Cowboys 1) Dallas Cowboys | 12 votes: Abdoo, Bergman, Ely, Filice, Gordon, Kownack, Okada, Patra, Shook, Smith, Umerani, Yam. 2) Philadelphia Eagles | 7 votes: Band, Cersosimo, McWilliams, Parr, Reuter, Rosenthal, Zierlein. Hype is never hard to find with the Cowboys, but this offseason has been different. They’ve been relatively drama-free , all the while making it clear a Super Bowl is the goal and they’re not shying away from it. So, why not the NFC East? The defense has been overhauled — including the addition of a Defensive Rookie of the Year front-runner in Caleb Downs and defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Dak Prescott’s offense is loaded and healthy and has finished as a top-five scorer in four of the past five seasons. Dallas is coming off back-to-back seven-win seasons. The last time Dallas had consecutive non-winning campaigns, it went 12-5 the following year and won the division in Mike McCarthy’s second year at the helm. Brian Schottenheimer is in Year 2 and has Texas-sized aspirations. Dan Parr, also of NFL.com, predicts the Cowboys will again have a top 5 offense this year. This is standard territory for the Cowboys. They have finished among the top five teams in OPPG in four of the past five seasons, with Dak Prescott ’s injury-shortened 2024 campaign the lone deviation. Prescott seems to still be in his prime after ranking among the top five quarterbacks in QBR and passing EPA last season. Dallas boasts the game’s top wide receiver duo, with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens performing at an All-Pro level. RB Javonte Williams kicked the injury bug that bit him earlier in his career and broke out in his first year in Big D, ranking ninth in the league with 1,201 rushing yards. If there’s one potentially fatal flaw, it’s at offensive tackle, with Dallas trading for Steelers castoff Broderick Jones , who is coming off a neck injury, in an attempt to shore things up at the position before the season begins . Barring pass protection on the edges becoming a thorn in its side, Brian Schottenheimer’s crew should be slicing through defenses again. And the defense? That’s where the optimism gets a little more complicated. The Athletic’s Mike Sando spoke with six NFL executives about their rankings of the top NFC teams, and wonders how much can the defense improve? “Anything is better than what they did last year on defense,” the voter placing Dallas second in the NFC said. “They shocked the system by trading Micah Parsons, and I just think generally speaking, new coordinators on defense create variance.” The voter ranking Dallas fifth thought the Cowboys’ defense might outrank the Packers’ defense, notable in light of the Parsons trade last year. “I like the coordinator,” this voter said of Parker. “He is going to help maximize what they have. The secondary is still not a strength, but they have an impressive front seven.” “Quinnen Williams is good, and they have a little more girth up front, so it should be better, but they’ve got some unknowns there too with coaches and philosophy,” the voter ranking Dallas eighth said. “I have defensive concerns, for sure,” one said. “Do they have enough pass rush? How healthy is Overshown? How good are the corners? But they did address the interior with Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark, and I like Caleb Downs. They will be better up the middle.” But everything starts in Week 1. A convincing win against the Giants would be a good first step toward validating all this optimism. And while the offense is expected to carry its share of the load, all eyes will be on the defense. Can Christian Parker’s unit improve just enough to turn the Cowboys from an intriguing team into a true contender?

summary: After a bit of drama surrounding if Joe Milton would return to the practice squad, the QB has returned. The Cowboys will wear “94” decals on their helmets to honor teammate Marshawn Kneeland who tragically passed on November 6th. Mandatory Credit: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect After a bit of drama surrounding if Joe Milton would return to the practice squad, the QB has returned. Brian Schottenheimer gave us details on who would be wearing the “C” on their chest in 2026 for the Cowboys, which is a much different approach than we have seen over the last few years. Quinnen Williams is excited about the turnaround he is seeing on the defensive side of the the ball for the Cowboys. Dallas also made some financial moves that could mean they are still looking to add players. Sources: Cowboys restructure deals of Clark, Bland, Ferguson – Todd Archer, ESPN Could more personnel moves be on the horizon for Dallas? The Dallas Cowboys created a little more than $19 million in salary cap space by restructuring the contracts of three players, sources told ESPN. Veteran defensive tackle Kenny Clark , cornerback DaRon Bland and tight end Jake Ferguson had their deals reworked to give the Cowboys flexibility as the 2026 season begins or allow the club to carry over any unused space to 2027. According to the NFL Players Association website, the Cowboys had roughly $14.2 million of cap space before the restructured contracts. Cowboys QB Dak Prescott, three others selected captains for 2026 season – Joseph Hoyt, The Dallas Morning News The Cowboys have named their 2026 captains. A bit different approach and some new faces will lead the Cowboys in 2026. The Cowboys have an 11-person leadership council for this year’s team. Now they have a smaller group of captains to go with it. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer announced the team’s four captains Thursday. Quarterback Dak Prescott was the lone offensive captain. He’s joined by defensive tackles Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark, as well as kicker Brandon Aubrey. Dak Prescott on Joe Milton’s return, ‘focused’ offseason & more – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys were thrilled to have Joe Milton clear waivers and return to the practice squad. Starting QB Dak Prescott speaks on that and more with Tommy Yarrish. FRISCO, Texas – It’s been a busy week for the Dallas Cowboys as they wrap up training camp and prepare for the regular season. First comes a league mandated break, where Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott said he’d enjoy some time with his daughters but find a way to get his heart rate going. Dallas’ quarterback room is now back at three, after the team brought Joe Milton back on the practice squad Wednesday afternoon. Prescott is glad that he’s back. “It means a lot,” Prescott said of Milton’s return. “Obviously, me just personally, I thought he would’ve gotten picked up in the waivers. Fortunate for us, we got a hell of a player back and a guy that makes our room better, a guy that makes our team better. His spirit, just the way that he approaches the day… he’s a hell of a dude, a hell of a competitor.” Cowboys have complete confidence in Tyler Guyton at left tackle – Brandon Loree, Blogging the Boys No one had more questions coming into training camp than left tackle Tyler Guyton. With just a few days left before the regular season, the Cowboys seem to have a ton of confidence in their starting left tackle. One of the offseason’s biggest question marks has turned into one of the team’s most confident players. Despite having doubts around Terence Steele at right tackle, Tyler Guyton has done everything the right way this offseason to be the left tackle of the Dallas Cowboys. Brian Schottenheimer recently discussed his resurgence . “Probably that second week of training camp is where we were like ‘whoa.’ It was just the way the confidence that he was taking in his sets and the counters that he was countering so when a defensive end rushes up field and tries to counter and go inside, he has the ability to move his feet inside and slam the door shut on that. Going up against different guys and watching him go up against different guys like Eze, watching him go up against RG and Malachi, and guys like that. You saw a guy that was beginning to understand the matchup element…” QUINNEN WILLIAMS: COWBOYS DEFENSE IS ‘NIGHT AND DAY’ DIFFERENT UNDER NEW DC CHRISTIAN PARKER – Kevin Patra, NFL.com We all assume the Cowboys defense will improve in 2026. But it’s always nice to hear the best defender on the roster see’s a night and day difference between the 2025 Cowboys defense and the 2026 Cowboys defense. Quinnen Williams joined the Dallas Cowboys for seven forgettable games in 2025 following his trade deadline deal . Even with the four-time Pro Bowler, the Cowboys defense stunk up the joint last season. In the months since, the 28-year-old has seen a distinct turnaround under new defensive coordinator Christian Parker. “The growth, it’s like night and day,” Williams said of the strides made by the Cowboys on defense, via the team’s official website . “Starting in OTAs, and starting the first week of training camp, getting a chance to go against one of the best offenses in battle every single day has helped us tremendously. The mindset coming from the coaches, top down to the players and to the leadership, has been drastically changed. It’s just fun, man. “I just can’t wait to see the process and the results from all the hard work, but we’re not done yet.” Predicting the 5 Dallas Cowboys players that won’t suit up for gameday in Week 1 vs. New York Giants – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Dallas It’s never too early to take a look at the possible gameday inactives for week one. Mauricio Rodriguez takes a stab at what the inactive list may look like on Sunday Night Football in a little over a week. DT Jonathan Bullard: The Cowboys are betting on Bullard’s experience and versatility. But he hasn’t practiced since Aug. 4 due to injury (groin/core) and I believe there will be a ramp up period before he plays. With Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark spearheading the group, I think the Cowboys can be patient with him. OL Drew Shelton: The fourth-round rookie is not NFL ready. His struggles in the preseason cannot be ignored by the Cowboys and I wouldn’t expect him to play early on. Can he develop into a starting tackle? Maybe. But it will take time. For now, Shelton might be looking at many “healthy scratch” games barring any injuries. Daily discussion question: What is your most conservative prediction for this season?

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 10
summary: It is Day 10 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: MIAMI - JANUARY 18: Quarterback Roger Staubach #12 of the Dallas Cowboys tries to avoid the Pittsburgh Steelers defensive tackle during Super Bowl X at the Orange Bowl on January 18, 1976 in Miami, Florida. The Steelers defeated the Cowboys 21-17. (Photo by Focus on Sport via Getty Images) | Focus on Sport via Getty Images It is Day 10 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. So here’s Day 10 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, and kicking off our top-10 iconic games we go to the first Super Bowl chapter of the Cowboys-Steelers rivalry. Dallas carried a lead into the fourth quarter and still had a chance to win on the final play, but Pittsburgh’s Steel Curtain defense and an unforgettable performance from Lynn Swann denied the Cowboys in massive heartbreak. Sunday, January 18, 1976 — 2:15 p.m. ET Miami Orange Bowl, Miami, Florida Final Score: Pittsburgh Steelers 21, Dallas Cowboys 17 Dallas reached Super Bowl X after a remarkable postseason run. The Cowboys had finished 10-4 as a wild-card team before beating Minnesota on the original Hail Mary and crushing the Rams 37-7 in the NFC Championship Game. They became the first wild-card team ever to reach a Super Bowl, while Pittsburgh entered at 12-2 looking to defend its championship from the previous season. The Cowboys took the lead early in the game. Roger Staubach found Drew Pearson for a 29-yard touchdown midway through the opening quarter. However, Terry Bradshaw quickly responded with a seven-yard scoring pass to Randy Grossman. Toni Fritsch then kicked a 36-yard field goal just 15 seconds into the second quarter, giving Dallas a 10-7 lead that held throughout the second and third quarters. Pittsburgh finally turned the game around in the fourth quarter. Reggie Harrison blocked Mitch Hoopes’ punt, sending the ball through the end zone for a safety and reducing Dallas’ lead to 10-9. Roy Gerela then kicked field goals from 36 and 18 yards, giving Pittsburgh its first lead at 15-10. With just over three minutes remaining and Pittsburgh facing third down, Bradshaw launched deep for Lynn Swann while taking a crushing hit from the Dallas pass rush. Swann caught the ball and completed a 64-yard touchdown, extending Pittsburgh’s advantage to 21-10 after Gerela missed the extra point. Bradshaw was knocked out on the play and never saw the touchdown himself. Swann had tortured Dallas all afternoon with a series of spectacular receptions including his iconic 53-yard acrobatic grab. He finished with only four catches, but those produced a then-Super Bowl record 161 receiving yards. He created enduring highlights to this day, and the 64-yard touchdown ultimately proved decisive. Dallas tried to come back. Staubach quickly drove the Cowboys 80 yards in only five plays and found Percy Howard for a 34-yard touchdown with 1:48 remaining. Remarkably, it was the only reception of Howard’s NFL career, and it pulled Dallas within four points at 21-17. The Cowboys received one last opportunity after Pittsburgh failed to convert on fourth down. Staubach moved Dallas to the Steelers’ 38-yard line and launched a final Hail Mary into the end zone with seconds remaining. Mike Wagner tipped the pass and Glen Edwards intercepted it, ending Dallas’ comeback and securing Pittsburgh’s second consecutive championship. This game belongs on the countdown because it helped establish Cowboys-Steelers as one of the defining rivalries of the 1970s. Dallas went from a wild-card berth to standing one possession away from beating the defending champions, while Pittsburgh survived behind its defense and Swann’s extraordinary playmaking. #Cowboys vs #Steelers 1976 Super Bowl X Final Score: Pittsburgh Steelers 21, Dallas Cowboys 17 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/aahysJFmX6 — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) September 3, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game Swann became the first wide receiver to win Super Bowl MVP. title: Cowboys have complete confidence in Tyler Guyton at left tackle
summary: One of the offseason’s biggest question marks has turned into one of the team’s most confident players. Despite having doubts around Terence Steele at right tackle, Tyler Guyton has done everything the right way this offseason to be the left tackle of the Dallas Cowboys. Brian Schottenheimer recently discussed his resurgence. “Probably that second week […]
full_text: One of the offseason’s biggest question marks has turned into one of the team’s most confident players. Despite having doubts around Terence Steele at right tackle, Tyler Guyton has done everything the right way this offseason to be the left tackle of the Dallas Cowboys. Brian Schottenheimer recently discussed his resurgence . “Probably that second week of training camp is where we were like ‘whoa.’ It was just the way the confidence that he was taking in his sets and the counters that he was countering so when a defensive end rushes up field and tries to counter and go inside, he has the ability to move his feet inside and slam the door shut on that. Going up against different guys and watching him go up against different guys like Eze, watching him go up against RG and Malachi, and guys like that. You saw a guy that was beginning to understand the matchup element…” When Guyton arrived in Dallas, he was a raw tackle prospect who hadn’t played the position for very long. His college career started at TCU, where he saw some action on defense, as an H-back, tight end, and occasionally along the offensive line. It wasn’t until he transferred to Oklahoma that he began the full-time switch to offensive tackle. Even then, Guyton was positioned on the right side to protect the blind side of a left-handed quarterback. Left tackle was a new challenge for him. The first two years of his NFL career have been up and down. His biggest struggle has been availability. Guyton has played in 25 of 34 regular-season games, missing time due to injuries. Guyton’s sophomore season was almost lost before it started with a knee injury he suffered during training camp, but he found a way back to the field for Week 1. Klayton Adams and Schottenheimer have talked about needing to see their left tackle stay on the field and not miss time. Guyton has been a warrior this offseason, staying healthy for the most part while also battling an elbow injury. That willingness to fight through the pain and be there for his team has caught the eye of his head coach. “He’s [Guyton] been as aware of it as anybody that his availability has not been the best. He didn’t blink with the elbow and I think that’s all part of the maturation process of a young player…He’s growing fast and I say it every time you guys ask me, but I’ll say it again, I’m super proud of him.” In his rookie season, Pro Football Focus graded Guyton at 49.4 overall . That ranked 16th out of 21 tackles from his draft class. Last year, Guyton was given a 57.4 overall grade, 14th out of 19 tackles from his class. Improvement has shown up, albeit in small increments, but the team isn’t looking to replace him. When Dallas traded for Broderick Jones from the Pittsburgh Steelers, it was made clear to Guyton that he wouldn’t be competing with him for the starting job on the left side. Jones would be competing with Steele at right tackle. That just shows how much faith the coaches and front office have in their left tackle and his development. “Hats off to Tyler Guyton, he’s solidified the left tackle position. He’s playing the best football he’s played since he’s been here. We have no worries or concerns about the left tackle spot.” Where Guyton goes in year three is still to be determined, but with confidence around him being at an all-time high, the arrow can only be pointing up for what the Cowboys hope can be their long-term answer at left tackle for the foreseeable future. #Cowboys Tyler Guyton gearing up for a big third season. Tyler Smith praised Guyton on how hard he’s worked this offseason and he’s poised for a jump. Working with @BigDuke50 and OL Masterminds will get you there. (🎥: @OLMTraining on IG) pic.twitter.com/FcYoiv5XYh — Brandon Loree (@Brandoniswrite) July 22, 2026

title: ESPN’s ‘bold surprise’ for Cowboys involves Caleb Downs
summary: The Dallas Cowboys drafted Caleb Downs. Just a few months ago that sentence sent everybody around here into a fever dream. Amazingly, given the level of hype and anticipation around him, Downs has sort of cooled. This has had nothing to do with him individually as by all measures he had a fantastic training camp […]
full_text: Aug 15, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Dallas Cowboys safety Caleb Downs (13) enters the field before the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys drafted Caleb Downs. Just a few months ago that sentence sent everybody around here into a fever dream. Amazingly, given the level of hype and anticipation around him, Downs has sort of cooled. This has had nothing to do with him individually as by all measures he had a fantastic training camp and ramp-up to the season, but so many other storylines popped to where the conversation shifted a bit. Still, Downs is hardly hiding or someone that people have forgotten about. He remains one of the most important members of the team. It is interesting in this sense that ESPN, who laid out “surprise predictions” for every team , included Downs for the Cowboys. Don’t be surprised if … rookie safety Caleb Downs never leaves the field. What I’m hearing: OK, maybe that’s a slight exaggeration, but the Cowboys believe they can use Downs in a ton of different ways. In their ideal world, he and veteran safety Jalen Thompson are interchangeable in the safety and nickel roles. Downs got a lot of work at nickel during camp, and Dallas has faith in his ability to play deep safety. The Cowboys believe in his ability to cover top receivers if that’s what they need from him, and they think he will be instantly capable of communicating at a high level and helping keep things organized on the defense. The Cowboys drafted Downs hoping they could plug and play him on defense in Year 1, and to their absolute delight, he has shown himself to be just that in every situation they’ve thrown at him so far. They’re counting on him to handle a key role in the revitalization of their defense under new coordinator Christian Parker, and I expect him to play a ton. Dan Graziano is the author in question here, someone with a long history covering the NFC East, so full and absolute respect. But what would be surprising about this? This actually feels like the complete and total opposite of a surprise. I don’t think there is anyone here or any Cowboys fan in general who expects Downs to be utilized less than 100%. His versatility is a huge reason for this. It has long been assumed that Christian Parker will move him around and that he will at times be in nickel. Maybe the Cowboys will want to play Downs exclusively at one position. There is certainly a discussion to be had around versatility and too much of it being a bad thing. Byron Jones, as an example, never fully settled at a position with the Cowboys and many people thought that limited his potential to really thrive at any one spot. This isn’t to say that this is who Caleb Downs is or what his future holds. But whatever he does, none of it will be surprising in this sort of way.

title: Cowboys 53-man roster proves special teams matter
summary: The Dallas Cowboys didn’t construct their 53-man roster as many of us predicted. Not only did they release players thought to be roster locks, but they kept several based on their special teams value. This is different from years past, proving the organization has put a higher priority on improving on special teams this season. […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys didn’t construct their 53-man roster as many of us predicted. Not only did they release players thought to be roster locks, but they kept several based on their special teams value. This is different from years past, proving the organization has put a higher priority on improving on special teams this season. Typically much of the Cowboys 53-man roster is dedicated to filling out the depth chart on both the offensive and defensive side of the ball, forcing the third phase of the game, special teams, to somewhat patchwork their units with what’s left available. This year though, Dallas allocated about half a dozen roster spots to players who excel, or are expected to, on special teams. S Markquese Bell S Alijah Clark OLB Tyrus Wheat CB Ameer Speed WR Jonathan Mingo WR KaVontate Turpin Turpin locking down a roster spot due to his special teams ability isn’t all that surprising. Neither is Brandon Aubrey or Bryan Anger, all of which are among the best of the given positions in the entire league. The other names mentioned above though are surprising. In order to keep both Bell and Clark for their special teams’ ability, the Cowboys surprisingly went six deep at the safety position instead of four or five. The same can be said for keeping Wheat over Sam Williams as well as Speed at CB and Mingo and WR. All should be key contributors on Dallas’ special teams units this year. All these players should improve Dallas’ coverage units. Add that with Brandon Aubrey’s ability to split the uprights consistently from 50+ yards, Bryan Anger’s field flipping ability as a punter, and KaVontate Turpin’s game changing ability as a return man, and the Cowboys special teams unit has a chance to be a positive this year. While very few, if any, of the players we mentioned above are likely to make much of an impact on the field either on offense or defense, the impact they can make a special teams could prove to be the difference between a win any loss this season. Only time will tell though, but regardless it feels like Dallas is placing a higher value on improving special teams this year.
author: Brian Martin

title: Recent moves show the Cowboys finally get something important
summary: A lot has happened over the last week. The Dallas Cowboys, like every NFL team, officially set their 53-man roster. As is usually the case this was an initial version of it because of various adjustments that had to be made. We saw that play itself out with the waiving of Joe Milton, the claiming […]
full_text: OXNARD, CA - JULY 28: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones listens as head coach Brian Schottenheimer answers a question during an opening press conference at training camp on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, in Oxnard, Calif. (Smiley N. Pool/The Dallas Morning News via Getty Images) A lot has happened over the last week. The Dallas Cowboys, like every NFL team, officially set their 53-man roster. As is usually the case this was an initial version of it because of various adjustments that had to be made. We saw that play itself out with the waiving of Joe Milton, the claiming of Emari Demarcado, and before either of those the trades involving Broderick Jones (in) and Nate Thomas (out). Roster cuts are often an emotional experience for people. When your pet cat makes it you feel like you won the lottery. The other side of that coin is that when he is cut you feel personally impacted. Dallas entered that period with a high approval rate for recent moves, but some of their cuts maybe burned a bit of it up. Given that the Broderick Jones trade was not well-received from a compensation standpoint and some of the proverbial wind has been lost behind the sails. As we have had a few days to sit on it, I have come to a realization personally: I am great with all of this. How many times have we talked about how notoriously inactive the Cowboys are in certain aspects of roster-building? Think of all of the years we have implored them to be more active in these types of areas. When you swing over and over and over again you are going to realize that batting 1.000 is tough work. We are looking for .300 here, a respectable mark, and more than anything the willingness to keep getting in the box. For all we know the Broderick Jones trade could even work out wonderfully and the C grade it received won’t even matter. In the aftermath of that deal there was some mild panic about Dallas having only four draft picks (quantitatively speaking) for next year, and you know what? I also love that. I love that the Cowboys were not averse to the deal because it would leave them shy for 2027 (they did pick up a seventh a day after the Jones trade by dealing Nate Thomas). I love that they, seemingly, trust themselves to figure it out when that time comes. The time at the moment pertains to 2026 and they have to stand in and take pitches, and most importantly they have to swing at the ones they like. Being shy about them because of how it might impact their batting average or what it could mean for the next at-bat, or heck even next season’s, isn’t prudent. Everything about this season continues to remain a breath of fresh air. Famous last words and all of that for obvious reasons, but right now this team seems to get it in some of the most important ways.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: Cowboys news: Joe Milton returns to Dallas
summary: After initially being beat out by Sam Howell for the backup quarterback spot and getting released, Joe Milton was signed to the Cowboys practice squad on Wednesday. Quinnen Williams re-signed with Dallas this offseason, and things have changed for the better as far as the team goes according to him. Dallas added running back Emari […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 28: Joe Milton III #10 of the Dallas Cowboys reacts to an incomplete pass against the New Orleans Saints during an NFL Preseason 2026 gameat AT&T Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images After initially being beat out by Sam Howell for the backup quarterback spot and getting released, Joe Milton was signed to the Cowboys practice squad on Wednesday. Quinnen Williams re-signed with Dallas this offseason, and things have changed for the better as far as the team goes according to him. Dallas added running back Emari Demercado off waivers, and his former coach praised the move. Camden Brown was able to make the final roster, and the way he heard about may shock some people. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create communi ty posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Dallas Cowboys sign QB Joe Milton to practice squad – SportsDay Staff, Dallas Morning News Joe Milton didn’t make the final roster cuts. However, he has retured to Dallas on the practice squad. Joe Milton will return to the Dallas Cowboys, the team announced Wednesday. The quarterback became a free agent after he went unclaimed on waivers, but is rejoining the organization via the practice squad. The Cowboys released Milton on Monday , signaling that they’d move forward with Sam Howell as Dak Prescott’s backup to start the 2026 season. Sam Howell on earning QB2 job: ‘The job doesn’t stop now’ – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Sam Howell was able to edge out Joe Milton for the primary backup quarterback role behind Dak Prescott. With that said, he knows he has to keep working hard to stay in that position. After initially keeping both Sam Howell and Joe Milton on the 53-man roster Sunday, Dallas chose to waive Milton on Monday, leaving Howell as the backup to Dak Prescott. “Obviously, extremely excited to be a part of this team and be a part of this organization,” Howell said. “It’s been a lot of hard work, and the work doesn’t stop now. I’m committed to this team and I’m going to try to find ways to help this team win, and that’s my job, and I’m excited to be here for sure.” Qunnien Williams: Culture, growth of Cowboys’ defense is ‘night and day’ – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com Qunnien Williams is entering his second season with the Cowboys, and the first one had its challenges. This year, he feels there’s a change within the team in multiple ways. “The growth, it’s like night and day,” Williams said of the strides made by the Cowboys on the defensive side of the ball, and in such a short period of time. “Starting in OTAs, and starting the first week of training camp, getting a chance to go against one of the best offenses in battle every single day has helped us tremendously. The mindset coming from the coaches, top down to the players and to the leadership, has been drastically changed. It’s just fun, man.” Andy Reid helps explains why Dallas Cowboys’ latest addition is better than it initially seems – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports Dallas added another piece to their running back room on Tuesday when they signed Emari Demercado off waivers from the Chiefs. His former coach, Andy Reid, dove into why he’s a good addition. Reid breaks down new Cowboys RB Before joining the Cowboys, Demercado spent the offseason with the Chiefs. Speaking to reporters last month, Reid provided his take on the young running back. Here’s what one of the most respected offensive minds in football had to say. “I like the pass protection, I like the way he’s not going to bounce anything,” Reid told reporters . “He sees (the hole), he lowers it, and he hits it in the run game, and I think that’s important. And pass routes are pretty good. He’s played it. He’s got experience.” Cowboys’ Camden Brown got his dream roster news in the strangest way – Jason Kandel, The Landry Hat Camden Brown has been a fan favorite during training camp and the preseason. He did enough to make the 53-man roster, but the way he found out about it was unique. Camden Brown learned he made the Cowboys’ roster through social media To be frank, that is a pretty funny (and stress-inducing) way to receive life-changing news. It’s the news Brown was obviously waiting for, but I bet he was hoping to hear it under better pretenses. But given social media helps news spread like wildfire, at least Brown’s friends and family let him know so he could get wind of the news in a timely manner. This isn’t on Schottenheimer when the Cowboys were likely more focused on calling the players who didn’t make the roster as opposed to the ones who did. 3 must-win games this Cowboys season – Matthew Holleran, Blogging The Boys The 2026 season is a huge one for the Cowboys as they look to make it back to the playoffs. Here’s three games they need to win to make that happen. It may seem a bit crazy to list a Week 2 matchup as a must-win, but this game absolutely falls into that category for the Cowboys. Dallas opens up the season with two divisional matchups in a row, traveling to New York to take on the Giants in Week 1 before returning home to host the Commanders. While Dallas has dominated the rivalry with the Giants in recent memory, this matchup will be much more difficult than years past. New York undoubtedly got better this offseason, and emotions will be running high as John Harbaugh makes his debut as the team’s new head coach. Dallas is favored and very well could win the game, but there is a real possibility they walk out of New York 0-1. Daily discussion question: What is your boldest prediction for this season?
author: Matthew Lenix

title: Broncos vs Chiefs is loaded with storylines, but Denver is keeping its focus internal
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country! The storylines for the Denver Broncos opener are thoroughly rich. It’s the first game of the season, against a hated division rival, on the road, on Monday Night Football, with their star quarterback returning from injury, against an opponent looking to rebound from a tough season, while Denver looks to start […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - JANUARY 25: Zach Allen #99 of the Denver Broncos lines up before the snap during the AFC Championship NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Empower Field At Mile High on January 25, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! The storylines for the Denver Broncos opener are thoroughly rich. It’s the first game of the season, against a hated division rival, on the road, on Monday Night Football, with their star quarterback returning from injury, against an opponent looking to rebound from a tough season, while Denver looks to start strong after a very good previous season. In other words, bring on Sept. 14 in Kansas City. “I think it’s going to be really cool, definitely get the season going,” Broncos defensive lineman Zach Allen said to the media earlier this week. “It’s good we have at least a little extra time to prepare for such a good opponent, and to do it on primetime is really cool. Division games are awesome, and the history between the two organizations amps it up even more. I’m really excited.” The fact that the Broncos open against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs just makes the next week and a half even more important. To really dial in and get as prepared as Denver can. “It’s huge. I think every week is about getting better,” Broncos right tackle Mike McGlinchey said to the media. “We’ve done that since we started training camp. This week is no exception. You don’t want to go into a game week next week off of a three-day off day and not feel like you accomplished something the week before or get better at your job. “I think it’s an incredible opportunity we have for the next three days to go and compete against each other for a couple more times here, hone in on some of the small details, kind of the introductions to what we want to do in the game plan against Kansas City, and then hit the ground running. Like I said, you want to be your best on Week 1, but it’s more important to be your best in Week 18. Every single week, you have to be better than the week before. It’s not going to be perfect when we first go out and start, but it’s about continuing to improve on each rep and each game as the season unfolds.” For Broncos head coach Sean Payton, the message is simple. It’s not about the Chiefs, the rivalry, or the opener; it’s about what the Broncos do. “There’s a history with all those division opponents, and usually you have to find a way to beat the one that’s at the top. So that was our task right away: it was Kansas City. They had won this division however many years in a row. So then, when you win it, now you’ve got to find a way to stay there. It’s pretty much the case around the league. “In New Orleans, I don’t know how many different division coaches that we saw. Tampa was the team that had won the Super Bowl, I think, in 2002. Early on, that was the team that you had to find a way to get past them. So that’s kind of where I see us right now. We’re competing in a real good division. You just look around, everyone has gotten better. The focus more is internal, our improvement and playing well. That’s kind of how I see it.”
author: Ian St. Clair

title: Evan Engram offers insight on Jaylen Waddle
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos are gearing up to take on the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football to begin the 2026 regular season. Going up against a division rival on the road ups the stakes and makes their Week 1 matchup the most intriguing game of the week. In order to […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - AUGUST 21: Jaylen Waddle (17) of the Denver Broncos takes the field before the game against the Green Bay Packers at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Friday, August 21, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. The Denver Broncos are gearing up to take on the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football to begin the 2026 regular season. Going up against a division rival on the road ups the stakes and makes their Week 1 matchup the most intriguing game of the week. In order to defend their AFC West Crow, it will be critical for the Broncos to take a big leap forward on offense. To help make that happen, they made a huge trade for Jaylen Waddle at the beginning of the offseason. Waddle’s a versatile player who can play inside and out. While his production dipped the last two seasons with the Miami Dolphins, he is still big-time playmaker. Since coming into the league, Waddle has been a tremendous chain mover, deep ball threat, and ranks highly with respect to yards after the catch. He has a chance to be the X-Factor for Denver’s offense this season and help them become a Top 10 unit in the National Football League. Yesterday after practice, tight end Evan Engram offered his thoughts on what Waddle has brought to the team’s dynamic on offense. “It’s a no brainer honestly. His impact that he has and the speed that he has. He’s really smart and savvy too. I think it’s going to help our offense a lot when you have to account for him every time that he is on the field. Sometimes that doesn’t even matter with his talent,” stated Engram. “We’re excited to have him. He’s had a great camp, and he’s meshed really well. He’s a great locker room guy. He’s really funny. He fits really well in with the DNA of our team, and he’s going to be a big part of our offense.” Join the conversation! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . One area Waddle should provide an immediate boost is with respect to catch percentage. He figures to be one of, if not the highest volume target in Denver’s aerial attack. Last season, both Courtland Sutton and Troy Franklin had issues in that regard. Both sported sub-65 percent catch rates, which is below average for top passing targets. If Denver wants to compete for a Lombardi Trophy, they have to get better on third downs, and their top pass catchers have to perform much better than that. Over the course of his career, Waddle has been nearly a 70-percent catch-rate player. His efficiency in that respect should give quarterback Bo Nix a top-flight target whether it’s on screens, operating over the middle of the field, or even on deep balls. I’m excited for the potential the Broncos’ offense has this season. In order for them to reach that, they are going to need Waddle to have an immediate impact with the team. I’m confident he will be able to do that and expect him to be a focal point of the team’s offensive gameplan for their Week 1 primetime matchup against the Chiefs. As always, thank you for reading. title: What uniform combination should the Lions go with against the Saints?
summary: We are nearly there. After the coming weekend, we will officially be into Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. For the Detroit Lions, that means hosting the New Orleans Saints back in the friendly confines of Ford Field. It’s a big season for Detroit in many ways, and after a 2025 season that fell […]
full_text: We are nearly there. After the coming weekend, we will officially be into Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season. For the Detroit Lions, that means hosting the New Orleans Saints back in the friendly confines of Ford Field. It’s a big season for Detroit in many ways, and after a 2025 season that fell short of everyone’s expectations—I expect the team to come out of the gates with a sizable chip on their shoulders. However, we still have over a week to get into all of the analysis and preparation for the game against New Orleans. So for now, let’s get into something that doesn’t matter very much at all, and yet many of us still care—uniforms. There was and still are plenty of discussions taking place surrounding the unveiling of the Lions’ 2026 Rivalry jerseys . Rather than jumping into those waters, let’s focus on another hotly debated topic amongst varying generations of fans: the silver pants. For a while now, the team has taken a liking to the monochromatic look where they have on all one color: the “blueberries” at home where they rock the blue home jersey with the blue pants, or the stormtrooper look on the road with the white on white. Listen, I like both of those looks, and they have their places, but please, wear the silver pants more often. At home, on the road. Both, if we are feeling crazy. And that brings us to today’s question of the day—what uniform combination do you want the Lions to wear in Week 1? My answer: You probably could have guessed this, but the blue tops with the silver pants. Lions coach Dan Campbell has put it out there before that the captains make the decisions for jerseys, and while I am also superstitious, let’s just try the traditional home look in Week 1. See how it goes and then we can go from there. Penei Sewell, Amon-Ra St. Brown, and the other captains, if you are reading this for whatever reason, do it for the 80s and 90s babies. What about you? What jerseys do you want the Lions to wear in Week 1 against the Saints? Let us know in the poll and comments below.
