title: The fair, unfair criticism of the Detroit Lions’ handling of Terrion Arnold
summary: In case you somehow didn’t already know, Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes and assistant general manager Ray Agnew spoke with the media Wednesday following the conclusion of training camp and roster cuts. In the wake of that media availability, and a few questions that were asked regarding Seattle Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold, there has […]
full_text: In case you somehow didn’t already know, Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes and assistant general manager Ray Agnew spoke with the media Wednesday following the conclusion of training camp and roster cuts. In the wake of that media availability, and a few questions that were asked regarding Seattle Seahawks cornerback Terrion Arnold, there has been some…discourse. Since this was the first time Holmes had been available to the media since everything went down, naturally, there would be questions regarding the former first-round pick. Sure enough, the first one after Holmes’ opening statement was tied to how the team handled everything involving Arnold. And without getting too into the weeds in regards to how the question(s) were articulated, I believe the spirit of the two questions being asked were: Did the Lions do their due diligence during the Arnold situation, and did Holmes and his staff do enough to make sure the cornerback position was in a good place if Arnold was not going to be on the team in 2026 and beyond? Did the Lions do enough due diligence throughout the situation with Arnold? Let’s address the point about due diligence first. Like everyone else, they first became aware of the situation involving Arnold earlier in the offseason, prior to the charges being formally filed against him in late July. During the aforementioned press conference, Holmes stated: “The more information that we got throughout the process, that was the result of us doing what the best and right thing was for the club, which was: move on and move forward.” At the owners meetings in late March, Lions coach Dan Campbell said: “We got all the information that says he wasn’t involved. That’s what we know, that’s all we know, and that’s really all I can say. As far as I know, it’s not a big deal. It seems like he still wasn’t involved with this.” Simply put, this was not a case of negligence, incompetence, or anything else of that nature. It is called being pragmatic and working with the information that is readily available at that point in time. Obviously, once the charges were filed, new information became available, and Detroit made the decision to part ways with a player who is now on the Commissioner’s Exempt list. Did the Lions do enough at the cornerback position with the uncertainty surrounding Arnold? Next up we have the angle that Holmes and his staff did not do enough at the cornerback position since they knew the situation surrounding Arnold was shaky at best. And while everyone is entitled to their opinion, I would ask this—what would you be comfortable letting go of in order to better shore up the secondary? From the other side of the discussion, the Lions did in fact make moves at cornerback. They re-signed veteran Rock Ya-Sin, someone who was very dependable and productive when he saw the field in 2025. They drafted cornerback Keith Abney II in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft, and they signed free agent Roger McCreary to a one-year deal, too. Now I know what some fans will respond to those three moves with: “But Morgan, none of those moves were for proven, starting-caliber players—the kind of move that can take the Lions to the Super Bowl.” And while I understand where that sentiment is coming from, it at least partially ignores the reality of roster-building and the salary cap that all 32 teams in the NFL operate under. Just like the edge rusher position, acquiring a player like that will come with a hefty price tag in the form of salary cap dollars or draft picks. And depending on the situation, it could end up being both. Circling back to my question about what the Lions would have to give up in order to acquire another young, starting-caliber cornerback. Say Detroit makes a move for that kind of player, they may no longer have the resources available to sign a player like center Cade Mays, which would put them in a tough spot at a position most would have argued was their biggest need prior to the 2026 offseason. In a different situation, let’s say they are still able to sign Mays, and instead wait until the draft to add to the cornerback depth. Most fans were happy on draft night when Detroit spent a second-round selection on edge rusher Derrick Moore. Finally , after drafting Moore and signing veteran defensive end DJ Wonnum, the Lions are prioritizing the spot opposite star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson. Would you feel as good about the state of the defensive line room as a whole if Detroit spent their second-round pick on a cornerback rather than taking Moore at pick 44? Or would Holmes once again be fielding questions regarding the edge depth behind Hutchinson and Wonnum? In that same train of thought, surely there aren’t fans out there wishing that the Lions took a cornerback in the first round, right ? That would leave veteran swing tackle Larry Borom at right tackle opposite All-Pro left tackle Penei Sewell. That would not be the worst scenario imaginable, but it certainly would not inspire confidence in the offensive line taking a much-needed step after a disappointing 2025 season. On the other hand, say they still drafted Miller at 17th overall, but they used the one-year, $5 million contract Borom got instead on a cornerback. That would leave them with (now injured) offensive lineman Giovanni Manu as the primary backup at tackle… so Devin Cochran? I don’t know about you, but I would not feel warm and fuzzy about that situation. At all. In essence, every team is flawed in some form or fashion. If you wanted “more” in the secondary, then you have to explain which piece they acquired is on the chopping block. That is the reality of the NFL and the way the salary cap works. Resources are finite with the intention to encourage parity across the league. And while Holmes has had his share of misses as it pertains to the draft, he has far more hits on his resume. That is why the Lions have paid so many young, core players over the last several years. It is also why Detroit is widely considered to have one of the best and most complete rosters in the league today.
author: Morgan Cannon

title: Detroit Lions rookie Derrick Moore among 6 jersey number changes
summary: When NFL teams cut their roster down from 90 to 53 players, it frees up a bunch of jersey numbers, and we often see a bunch of players change their numbers before the season begins. That’s exactly what has happened with the Detroit Lions in 2026, as six players will now have new numbers for […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - AUGUST 22: Derrick Moore #9 of the Detroit Lions plays against the Washington Commanders at Ford Field on August 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images When NFL teams cut their roster down from 90 to 53 players, it frees up a bunch of jersey numbers, and we often see a bunch of players change their numbers before the season begins. That’s exactly what has happened with the Detroit Lions in 2026, as six players will now have new numbers for the upcoming season. Here’s a quick look at those players: QB Luke Altmyer: Previous number: 2 New number: 15 WR Lucky Jackson Previous number: 11 New number: 9 DT Ben Stille Previous number: 72 New number: 96 EDGE Derrick Moore Previous number: 9 New number: 8 DB Keith Abney Previous number: 28 New number: 6 DB Aamaris Brown Previous number: 42 New number: 24 For Moore, his move from 9 to 8 now matches his college number at Michigan. Meanwhile, Lucky Jackson takes Moore’s old number and snatches up one of the final single-digit numbers. Keith Abney took another single-digit number. Now, just 5 and 7 remain unclaimed amongst the single-digit numbers. (Seven is retired by the team for Dutch Clark). One unresolved issue here is that Dobbs was previously #6, which is now owned by Abney. It’s not clear what Dobbs is changing his number to. These number changes have yet to be reflected on the team’s official roster , but they were announced on the NFL’s daily transaction wire.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: 2026 Detroit Lions roster comparison: Are they deeper than last year?
summary: One of the biggest problems the Detroit Lions have run into in the past few years is injuries. Detroit has had terrible luck in that department, being one of the most injured teams in football for three years running. While teams can try to do everything within their power to prevent injuries—whether it be practicing […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - NOVEMBER 24: Detroit Lions Center Frank Ragnow (77) lines up over the ball as the offensive line warms up for the NFL football game between the Detroit Lions and the Indianapolis Colts on November 24, 2024, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Allio/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of the biggest problems the Detroit Lions have run into in the past few years is injuries. Detroit has had terrible luck in that department, being one of the most injured teams in football for three years running. While teams can try to do everything within their power to prevent injuries—whether it be practicing habits, nutrition, strength and conditioning—the only tried and true method of protecting yourself against injuries is to build the best depth you can possibly have. The Lions haven’t had horrible depth in previous years, but it can always be improved. So let’s look at Detroit’s depth players only on the 53-man roster and practice squad and see if they’re in a better spot than they were in 2025. Note: Players who started the season on IR/PUP/NFI are not included in the depth, but mentioned, if relevant. Quarterback 2026: Josh Dobbs Luke Altmyer (PS) 2025: Kyle Allen C.J. Beathard Is the depth better? No. I don’t think so. Allen was a better backup than Dobbs, as identified by the fact that Allen went quickly in free agency, while Dobbs was cut this offseason and didn’t sign anywhere until August. That said, I do like the fact that Detroit now has a developmental backup in Luke Altmyer who showed enough to potentially be a long-term reserve option. Running back 2026: Sione Vaki Jacob Saylors Jabari Small (PS*) *For the sake of what I believe will happen, I’m assuming Small is coming back to the practice squad after some roster maneuvering 2025: David Montgomery Craig Reynolds Sione Vaki Jacob Saylors Is the depth better? Without a doubt, it is not. Isiah Pacheco was already a downgrade from Montgomery, and the fact that he will now miss at least the first four games of the season will hurt even more. There is certainly hope that Vaki and Saylors are better than the 2025 versions of themselves with another year in the system, but that improvement won’t make up the gap left by Montgomery’s departure. Wide receiver 2026: Tay Martin Tom Kennedy (PS) Lucky Jackson (PS) Dominic Lovett (PS) 2025: Isaac TeSlaa (started behind Kalif Raymond) Dominic Lovett Ronnie Bell (PS) Tom Kennedy (PS) Jackson Meeks (PS) Is the depth better? Nope. Detroit went very light on wideouts in 2026, and the depth looks worse off for it. Letting Kalif Raymond walk and replacing him with Greg Dortch has already failed, as Dortch didn’t make the roster. The Lions were also victimized by a season-ending injury to rookie receiver Kendrick Law, which would make this look a little better, but as it stands for the 2026 season, the Lions’ depth is clearly not great here. Hopefully the starters stay healthy. Tight end 2026: Brock Wright Tyler Conklin Jackson Meeks Thomas Gordon (PS) 2025: Brock Wright Shane Zylstra Zach Horton (PS) Is the depth better? Yes! The 2026 Lions get their first edge from last year’s squad due almost exclusively to the addition of Conklin. That said, the evolution of Meeks also brings some additional hope. After dealing with serious injuries last year, Detroit is in a much better spot to withstand poor luck this season. Offensive line 2026: OT Larry Borom OT Devin Cochran (PS) T/G Miles Frazier G Ben Bartch C Seth McLaughlin (PS*) G/C Mason Miller (PS) *Again, I’m assuming McLaughlin returns to the practice squad 2025: OT Giovanni Manu OT Dan Skipper (PS) G Kayode Awosika G/C Kingsley Eguakun OL Mason Miller (PS) OL Trystan Colon (PS) OL Michael Niese (PS) Is the depth better? I would say yes, emphatically. Borom is a huge upgrade at OT3 over Manu. Additionally, Bartch is a significant upgrade over Awosika as the first interior offensive lineman in. The Lions’ 2026 depth would look even better if Juice Scruggs was in a reserve position rather than having to be a starter with Cade Mays out. Defensive line 2026: EDGE Derrick Moore EDGE Tyler Lacy EDGE Ahmed Hassanein EDGE Eric O’Neill DT Levi Onwuzurike DT Skyler Gill-Howard DT Mekhi Wingo EDGE Anthony Lucas (PS) DT Chris Smith (PS) DT Ben Stille (PS) DT Tyre West (PS) 2025: EDGE Al-Quadin Muhammad (Davenport wasn’t injured yet) EDGE Tyrus Wheat DT Roy Lopez DL Pat O’Connor DT Mekhi Wingo DT Chris Smith EDGE Isaac Ukwu (PS) EDGE Andre Carter (PS) DT Myles Adams (PS) DT Keith Cooper Jr. (PS) Is the depth better? I think it’s fair to say yes. While the Lions have a bunch of unknowns in Hassanein, Gill-Howard, and O’Neill, they also have significant investments in their reserves, including Derrick Moore (presumably behind DJ Wonnum) and Onwuzuruike. Last year’s squad was devastated with early injuries. Remember there was no Alim McNeill, no Onwuzurike, and soon to be no Marcus Davenport, leaving Detroit perilously thin, especially on the outside. Linebackers 2026 LB Malcolm Rodriguez (assuming Devin White starts for now) LB Jimmy Rolder LB Trevor Nowaske LB Joe Bachie (PS) LB Amen Ogbongbemiga (PS) 2025: LB Grant Stuard LB Trevor Nowaske LB Zach Cunningham LB Anthony Pittman (PS) Is the depth better? Again, I think this is a clear yes. Rodriguez brings a very capable starter (he was injured last year). Nowaske brings the same subpackage potential as last year, but with one more year of experience. Rolder brings some big potential and significant special teams skills. And Bachie and Ogbongbemiga have loads of experience both on defense and special teams. Don’t get me wrong, Stuard and Cunningham were great depth players last year, but Detroit simply has more playable talent in the linebacker room this year. Cornerback 2026: CB Ennis Rakestraw CB/NB Roger McCreary CB/NB Keith Abney CB Khalil Dorsey CB Nick Whiteside (PS) I’m assuming Christian Izien will be the primary nickel, and therefore not “depth” 2025: Rock Ya-Sin Khalil Dorsey Amik Robertson was considered the starting nickel, so is not included among the depth Is the depth better Eh… it’s a toss up. They have more bodies and more competition, but having Ya-Sin as a depth player rather than the starter is a pretty big difference. Eventually, though, the 2025 squad saw its depth decimated. They had to add Whiteside, Arthur Maulet, and Kendall Fuller to the roster to help. The depth wasn’t particularly good last year, and it’s not good this year, either. Take your pick. Safety 2026: Thomas Harper Aamaris Brown (PS) 2025: Avonte Maddox Daniel Thomas Thomas Harper Erick Hallett (PS) Loren Strickland (PS) Is the depth better? Obviously not, but that comparison will obviously change drastically when (if?) Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph return from IR. Having Chuck Clark, Avonte Maddox, and Thomas Harper in depth roles would be a phenomenal safety room, although Detroit may not have the roster spots for all of those players upon Branch’s and Joseph’s return. The 2025 depth was actually pretty impressive, and they ended up needing it. So, I still think the Lions did a pretty good job maintaining that depth in 2026, even if it’s a downgrade from last year. Overall Well, they’ve gotten worse at four positions, gotten better at four positions, and there’s one toss-up. The most positive development is that they are deeper on both sides of the trenches, which could result in this team finding its identity again in 2026. Still, there are serious concerns in Detroit’s secondary, and with the thin reserves at skill positions, time will tell.
author: Jeremy Reisman

title: Survey: Which Lions RB will get the majority of Isiah Pacheco’s snaps?
summary: Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host NFL fan surveys, sponsored by FanDuel Sportsbook. For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and this week’s question focuses on which running back will add more offensive snaps to their responsibilities now that Isiah Pacheco has been placed on injured reserve. While […]
full_text: Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff (16), hands the ball to running back Sione Vaki (33) at practice during training camp at Meijer Performance Center in Allen Park on Thursday, July 30, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Throughout the offseason, SB Nation will host NFL fan surveys, sponsored by FanDuel Sportsbook . For Pride of Detroit, we are tasked with fielding questions from Detroit Lions fans, and this week’s question focuses on which running back will add more offensive snaps to their responsibilities now that Isiah Pacheco has been placed on injured reserve . While general manager Brad Holmes said the team is hopeful to get Pacheco back this season , losing the veteran running back for at least four games could be a big blow to the Lions’ depth. Fortunately, the Lions have improved options at the RB3 and RB4 spots, but they’ll need someone to pick up the slack and take on some RB2 duties. Wth four other running backs on the roster, who will get the majority of Pacheco’s snaps? Jahmyr Gibbs is expected to be the Lions’ “bell cow” running back this season, and he could easily be the first option to absorb more snaps. He is by far the most dynamic option of the group and would give the Lions the best chance to win whenever he is on the field. The Lions will need to give him some rest, but there’s still a world in which he gets even more reps than expected. Sione Vaki has gotten a lot of hate this offseason, but I believe a lot of that is because fans haven’t gotten a chance to see him play running back due to recent injuries and coaches’ decisions to keep him out of preseason games. However, there is one thing that has been crystal clear: ever since Pacheco was injured, it’s been Vaki who has taken the majority, if not all, of the RB2 reps in training camp practices. Jacob Saylors has been a great success story this preseason. With Gibbs, Pacheco, and Vaki not playing in the preseason, Saylors has started each game and performed very well. He’s looked decisive in his reads, strong through the hole, executed subtle moves to shake into space, and had the power to finish runs. His balanced skill set and reliability could elevate him into an RB2 role to start the season. Jabari Small is the wild card of the group because he was on the roster when the poll was published, but was waived during the voting process . There’s still a chance he could be elevated for a game or three, but the chances of him making a significant impact have been dramatically reduced. That said, Small had a very nice training camp, and when on the field (he was injured in all three preseason games), he’s shown well. It’s also worth mentioning that coach Dan Campbell noted that he and Saylors were neck-and-neck in their competition for a depth role all camp. So, in your opinion, which running back will get the majority of Pacheco’s reps? title: The Madden Curse is real and it’s coming for the Bears
summary: I live in suburban Chicago Illinois, which has several benefits. One of the big benefits is that I get to hear overconfident Bears fans on the radio, which I enjoy more than hearing overconfident Green Bay Packers fans on the radio. Don’t get me wrong, I’m not at all against proclaiming the superiority of your […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 18: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears looks on during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Rams in the NFC Divisional Playoffs at Soldier Field on January 18, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images I live in suburban Chicago Illinois, which has several benefits. One of the big benefits is that I get to hear overconfident Bears fans on the radio, which I enjoy more than hearing overconfident Green Bay Packers fans on the radio. Don’t get me wrong, I’m not at all against proclaiming the superiority of your football team when it’s warranted, but when I listen to Wisconsin sports radio the, ahem, “quality” of callers praising the team often has me questioning whether the Packers are actually any good at all. Here in Chicagoland, it works in reverse. The vast, vast majority of the city is convinced of three things: Caleb is DEFINITELY the man. It. The promised one. And at the very least, he is superior to Jordan Love. The Bears are legitimate Super Bowl contenders, and possibly at the beginning of a dynasty. No other team in the division is even close. These all seem…how to put this delicately…“not true.” Or, less delicately, “delusional.” The Bears had a very good, very fun season in 2025, but I spend most of my time writing about luck and regression to the mean and the like, and let me tell you, if the Packers were coming off of the season that the Bears just had, I would be in full fledged panic mode. I already have a bit of a reputation as a Debbie Downer and if the Packers and Bears switched places I’d reach new levels of doomsaying. I would be researching top five picks in the 2027 draft already. I mean, if we had a first-round pick in that draft, I would be doing that, in this alternate universe which we are thankfully not in. It’s important to perform this mental exercise to ensure that 1 . I’m not just hating on the Bears because I do actually hate them and they’re a terrible franchise that’s probably moving to Indiana, or 2 . because the Brewers are facing the Cubs right now and I’m taking out my frustration at Cubs fans continually chanting “ Green Bay Sucks ” in between cheering for shallow flyouts they really thought were going to be home runs. Fortunately, you don’t have to take my word for it. We have neutral arbiters we can turn to for these questions, namely casinos! The team with the best betting odds to win the division isn’t the Bears, it’s the Lions, who sit at +145 at Fanduel. The Bears are also not second, falling short of the Packers (+160). They’re a comfortable third (+350), just ahead of the Vikings (+460). The venerable football analytics website FTN.com also projects the Bears for 9 wins and third place in the division behind the Lions (10.5 wins) and Packers (9.5), and just one game ahead of the Vikings (8). People wagering actual money or doing advanced math all kind of hate the Bears, and rightfully so. I’ve read plenty of offseason pieces poking holes in the Packers’ roster, but only a few on the Bears, so allow me to poke away. Regression to the Mean Comes for Us All First, the Bears were super lucky last year. By Tom Bliss’ luck metrics, the Bears were the eighth-luckiest team in football (Minnesota was seventh), gaining basically half a win of Win Percentage Added (WPA) over the course of the season due to events completely outside of their control. Luck dashboard through week 17 Most impactful plays: – CHI dropped pass with 0:36 left in Q4 (+20.0% for SF) – LAR dropped pass with 10:09 left in Q4 (+18.8% for ATL) – ATL makes 51-yd FG with 0:25 left in Q4 (-17.6% for LAR) pic.twitter.com/9FqV0Pya9n — Tom Bliss (@DataWithBliss) December 30, 2025 You can also see this in their expected record versus their actual record (9.1-7.9 versus their actual 11-6), and the fact that they were third in the division in point differential, behind the Lions and Packers. Point differential predicts future win totals better than previous win totals predict future win totals (say that five times fast), and so bettors and nerds see the Bears as more of a true nine-win team). The Bears were also alarmingly lucky on defense. They were 30 th in yards per play allowed, they allowed the most explosive passing plays in the league, and they allowed a league-leading 13 passing touchdowns of 20+ yards. They allowed the most rushing yards before contact in the league and the fifth highest explosive run rate. They were terrible at everything that matters. The only reason they were not getting blown out week-in and week-out is turnovers. Turnovers are not ALL about luck, but the Bears were extremely lucky on fumble recoveries, and while interceptions involve more skill than fumble recoveries do, they managed an incredible 32.4% interception rate on their passes defended, easily leading the league. No other team was a bove 25%, and the league average is closer to 20%. Finally, the Bears were 26 th in the league in DVOA on first and second down, and shot up to ninth best on third and fourth down. FTN , who produced most of these statistics (buy their annual almanac here! ) has tracked this for at least two decades now, and when third down efficiency is vastly better than first and second down efficiency, the team’s defense almost always craters the following year, as those high leverage third down plays fall back to average (or worse). And while the Bears were staging all of those thrilling, but unsustainably lucky comeback wins, the Packers and Lions were getting phenomenally unlucky , ranking 29 th and 30 th in the Bliss rankings. The Lions were the only team to lose WPA in all four major luck categories, while the Packers experienced a lot of positive fumble luck, while giving it all back (and then some) on opposing field goals and opposing dropped passes. It’s one thing to be lucky while your major opponents are basically average. Instead, the Bears benefitted from their own luck, as well as colossal bad luck from their closest rivals. Caleb Williams Was “Fine” On offense, I think the Bears have outstanding personnel, especially at the skill positions, but anyone claiming the Caleb Williams is currently better than Jordan Love needs to put down the Malort and take a few deep breaths. Williams did a nice job making big plays, and those comebacks were all thrilling, but over the entire 60 minutes of a game, the man just wasn’t very good. Including the playoffs, Caleb Williams had a worse completion percentage last season than JJ McCarthy, and every other quarterback except Shedeur Sanders. He was just 13 th in yards per game (slightly ahead of Jordan Love and the slow-as-molasses Packers) while Jared Goff was 2 nd . He was 19 th in TD% (Love was 10 th , Goff was 6 th ). Caleb does at least have Love on some of the counting stats, as Love missed two games, and the Packers just don’t pass that much, but in the more advance stats, Love was third in Completion Percentage Over Expected (CPOE) to Caleb’s 29 th (Goff was 12 th ), and Love was fifth in Adjusted Net Yards per Attempt (ANY/A) to Williams’ 11 th (Goff was third). Love and Goff have better success rates, passer ratings, and Love even has Williams on Average Depth of Target. The only place where Williams clearly outperformed the league was in protecting the ball. Williams’ 1.2% INT% was truly special and led the league among qualified quarterbacks, but Love and Goff weren’t exactly butchers, ranking fifth and sixth respectively. Williams also led the league in fourth quarter comebacks, but it’s worth noting that he was one of the reasons they were so frequently behind in the first place. Now, this is all overly negative on Williams, and I actually like Williams as a prospect and expect he will improve into a truly dangerous quarterback. The fact of the matter is that he can make a lot of throws that other quarterbacks cannot, that I trust he will continue to make big plays a standard part of his game. He really only…

(Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I’m excited for MarShawn Lloyd. I’m worried for MarShawn Lloyd. In some ways his offseason reminded me of a low-level viral tweet from a while back : he accidentally became important at work, and it might be ruining his life. I don’t think anybody anticipated the Packers would go into Week 1 with Lloyd as the de facto number one running back, yet that’s the position in which we find ourselves. Coming out of two seasons plagued by injury and illness (don’t forget his appendix issues his rookie year), the easy narrative for Lloyd would be a season of redemption. Finally he would get to put his injuries behind him and figure out what it means for him to be an NFL back. But in the wake of Josh Jacobs’ legal situation, suddenly the stakes are much higher for both Lloyd and the Packers. Now, he can’t be just one of the guys in the backfield. He suddenly has an important role. The intensity of the spotlight has just ratcheted up quite a few notches. Now, Lloyd faces actual expectations. He’s going to play a significant role. He’s going to be counted upon to make real contributions. I can hardly imagine a tougher set of circumstances for a guy just trying to have a normal season for the first time in his career. But hey, if anybody’s got the mental fortitude to get through a season of sudden importance, it’s probably Lloyd, right? He’s dealt with nothing but challenges to this point. What’s one more? title: Why this is Houston’s Year
summary: Nearly a decade ago I wrote about the Houston Texans entering the franchise Red Zone, a place where they were in scoring range of Super Bowl Glory. Well, that didn’t work out as expected. Obvs. From Bill O’Brien’s ascension and Jack Easterby’s Grima Wormtonguing to the throw away years of David Culley and Lovie Smith, […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 20: Will Anderson Jr. #51 and Danielle Hunter #55 of the Houston Texans look on from the field after the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at NRG Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nearly a decade ago I wrote about the Houston Texans entering the franchise Red Zone, a place where they were in scoring range of Super Bowl Glory. Well, that didn’t work out as expected. Obvs. From Bill O’Brien’s ascension and Jack Easterby’s Grima Wormtonguing to the throw away years of David Culley and Lovie Smith, things got dark – fast. Then the sun rose over the Gulf and owner Cal McNair made 2 of the best decisions of his life: hiring Nick Caserio as general manager, and signing off on the hiring of Demeco Ryans as head coach. While it took those men a few years to rebuild what BO’B and Grima destroyed, not only did they do it, they assembled arguably the best team the Texans have ever had. "I was at Houston Texans practice the other day and their defense is humming.. The players on every single level of the ball are unbelievable.. It's incredible to watch" ~ @JJWatt #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/57NiMYh437 — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 28, 2026 Lights Out Defense It’s almost unfair how ‘Madden Cheat Code’ good the 2025 Texans defense was. And, as you can expect from Caserio and Ryans, they improved that unit this off-season. Any ranking that doesn’t have the Houston D as #1 heading into the 2026 season is immediately invalid. Will Anderson Jr. Sheldon Rankins Danielle Hunter Azeez Al-Shair Henry To’oTo’o Derek Stingley Jr. Kamari Lassiter Jalen Pitre Callen Bullock Reed Blankenship Let’s face it, every one of those players has a legit chance at landing on a Pro Bowl/All Star roster next January. The upfront pressure is sure to slow opposing running games and speed up opponents passing attacks. And when you do both, 3-and-outs and turnovers become normal expectations. Speaking of turnovers, Sting, Pitre, Bullock and Lassiter each had 4 interceptions last season. And, each of them improved in the off-season. This defense is nothing short of nightmare fuel for opposing offensive coordinators. Improved Offensive Line While rising up from the bottom of the barrel to middle of the pack isn’t all that impressive, the 2025 Texans offense was legitimately only a handful of positive plays away from a far more positive outcome. Take a little pressure off C.J. Stroud in the New England Patriots game and give Houston a +7/Pats -7. Now we’re looking at a 23-21 Houston win, not a 16-28 Pats victory. With the upgraded line, the offense should stay on the field a bit longer, score a bit more and commit a few less turnovers. All that is just enough incremental improvement to swing games in a league where margin of victory is often razor-thin. More Experienced Coaching Every day, Demeco Ryans grows as a NFL coach. And he’s already one of the best in the league. As his growth increases, his game management, situational awareness and motivational skills improve. Offensive coordinator Nick Caley was largely to blame for last year’s offensive offensiveness. However, as the season progressed, so did Caley. Word out of training camp is his communication with quarterback C.J. Stroud has also taken a quantum leap forward. Having them on the same page every moment of the game can only help. The Houston defense was really good under Demeco Ryans, but when he handed the reigns to defensive coordinator Matt Burke, it jumped from really good to great. This year, Burke seems poised to take it from great to historically dominant. Get ready to pencil them in along side the ‘85 Chicago Bears and 2000 Baltimore Ravens. C.J. Stroud Speaking of ranking lists, Houston field general C.J. Stroud has seen his name on an awful lot of “most improved” and “players to watch” lists this offseason. Actually, he probably hasn’t seen his name on those lists simply because he’s been too busy working on becoming the best Houston Texan he can be instead of reading his own press. Players, coaches and reporters have all taken notice. Between the improved offensive line and Stroud’s commitment to living up to his potential, he certainly seems poised to take this team all the way. Rumors swirl this morning that Stroud just turned down a $50 mil/year contract extension, meaning he’s confident in his own ability to earn top QB cash this year. Hopefully that’s a bet worth taking. “A lot of pressure on [C.J. Stroud]. … A lot of money on the line!” —Adam Schefter @AdamSchefter discusses the Texans setting a deadline for Stroud’s contract talks ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/aj3QIuBsNc — Get Up (@GetUpESPN) September 2, 2026 Texans schedule The NFL schedule makers were very kind to the 2026 Houston Texans, slotting them with the 26th overall hardest schedule. Houston’s upcoming opponents had a combined win percentage of .474 in 2025 according to CBS Sports. Looking over the rest of this year, there are a lot of matchups where the opponents simply don’t have enough gas in the tank to throttle past this Texans defense. Dallas Cowboys, Cleveland Browns, Cincinnati Bengals, plus 2 more opportunities to wear the new Rivalry Unis and whoop the BESFs. Our 25th Season schedule is set 🤘 | @Ticketmaster pic.twitter.com/j4O8IXjDtA — Houston Texans (@HoustonTexans) May 14, 2026 10 days til Kickoff – get excited! #GOTEXANS

Carmel High School alum Will Heldt is also a potential power rusher, but with his 6’7 size he could bulk up past his current reported weight of 260 lbs. and slide inside more this year for Clemson or in the NFL. I'm a bit biased with this one. But Clemson EDGE Will Heldt is going to be a legit 2027 prospect. 6'6' 260 pounds. 45 pressures + 7.5 sacks in 2025. pic.twitter.com/xvI41DUVa8 — Tyler Brooke (@TylerDBrooke) April 29, 2026 Overall this could be a very strong Edge draft class with over 15 players getting Round 1-3 grades early on in summer scouting. There is a good variety too in terms of prototypes and size profiles, so there is a strong likelihood of a pass rusher being available that fits what the Colts want at the position and is of Big Board value whenever the Colts pick in Round 2 in 2027. Still a whole season to get through first before final grades and scouting reports are complete, but it’s hard not to get excited about this class from a draft evaluator perspective.

title: Anthony Richardson named Colts backup quarterback
summary: Anthony Richardson Sr. has officially won the Indianapolis Colts’ backup quarterback job. Head coach Shane Steichen announced Thursday that Richardson will serve as the Colts’ QB2 behind Daniel Jones, while Riley Leonard will open the season as QB3. It ends a long offseason competition between Richardson and Leonard, who split second- and third-team reps throughout […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, INDIANA - AUGUST 19: Anthony Richardson Sr. #5 and Easton Stick #4 of the Indianapolis Colts step back to pass during the joint practice against the Atlanta Falcons at Grand Park Sports Campus on August 19, 2026 in Westfield, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Anthony Richardson Sr. has officially won the Indianapolis Colts’ backup quarterback job. Head coach Shane Steichen announced Thursday that Richardson will serve as the Colts’ QB2 behind Daniel Jones, while Riley Leonard will open the season as QB3. It ends a long offseason competition between Richardson and Leonard, who split second- and third-team reps throughout training camp and each received extended playing time during the preseason. Richardson finished the preseason 21-of-33 passing for 249 yards, doing enough to hold off Leonard and remain one injury away from the field. The decision is notable because Richardson’s future in Indianapolis looked uncertain for most of the offseason. He and his agent requested a trade in February, but the former No. 4 overall pick remained with the team and continued competing for a role. Richardson also struck a positive tone after being named the backup, saying he was thankful the Colts believed in him enough to promote him to QB2 and that he is ready to work and provide his best self. That has been a consistent theme from the organization in recent months, with general manager Chris Ballard repeatedly praising Richardson’s attitude and presence around the team. From a roster standpoint, this was probably the right call. Richardson is still raw and inconsistent, but he remains the more physically gifted and experienced option compared to Leonard. If the Colts are forced to turn to a backup quarterback, Richardson at least gives them a player with starting experience, elite rushing ability and a higher immediate ceiling. Leonard still has developmental appeal, but asking him to be the primary backup this early would have been a tough sell. He showed flashes during the Texans regular season game last season, but this preseason he looked like a quarterback who needs time. Keeping him as QB3 allows the Colts to develop him without rushing the process. He still looks like a strong option for the long-term QB2. The bigger question is what this means for Richardson’s long-term future. Being named QB2 does not suddenly make him the franchise quarterback again, and Jones remains the clear starter. Still, it does keep Richardson in the picture. After a trade request, months of uncertainty and a legitimate battle with Leonard, Richardson has at least stabilized his spot on the roster. For now, the Colts have their quarterback hierarchy set: Jones is QB1, Richardson is QB2 and Leonard is QB3. It may not answer every question about the future, but it does give Indianapolis clarity before Week 1.

full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - DECEMBER 25: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos and head coach Andy Reid of the Kansas City Chiefs meet on the field following the Broncos 20-13 win at Arrowhead Stadium on December 25, 2025 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest Make sure you download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For more information, click here . There was a new champion of the AFC last season after the Kansas City Chiefs represented the conference in the Super Bowl for three consecutive years. The question is: can the Chiefs reclaim the throne from the New England Patriots ? Some NFL executives are skeptical. NFL execs rank AFC teams: Bills lead a jumble of contenders. Does anyone trust the Chiefs? | The Athletic 6. Kansas City Chiefs Votes: 5-5-3-9-5-7 | Avg: 5.7 | Median: 5 | Vegas wins: 10.5 (T-2nd-AFC) Tier votes: SB contender: 1 | Division contender: 5 It’s strange seeing the Chiefs all the way down here. “Yeah, Andy Reid and a healthy Patrick Mahomes?” the exec slotting Kansas City third said. “I’ll take my chances with them coming away with 11 wins.” That’s barely higher than the Chiefs’ Vegas win total, which ranks tied for second in the AFC. “Mahomes coming off the knee, they lose the corners in (the offseason) — those are all good players, right?” an exec ranking the Chiefs fifth said. “I’m a little skeptical how they are going to replace those corners. We know Mahomes is good, but I don’t know how healthy he is.” Chiefs rush to rebuild defense around veteran Chris Jones | ESPN “Besides Chris, you want guys that can [get] pressure,” Reid said. “If you leave these quarterbacks [time] in this league, and let them sit there [in the pocket], they’re going to rip you apart. You’ve got to make them uncomfortable — and you have to have the guys to be able to do that. “The guys Brett bought in have that ability. It’s just a matter of getting it done.” Unlike any previous year under Spagnuolo, who joined the Chiefs in 2019, this year’s path for the defense to be its most effective is expected to be made through the improved production of the linemen. Latest Kansas City Chiefs salary cap update after RG Trey Smith restructures contract and what it means for the team | A to Z Sports Why did the Chiefs choose Trey Smith for the restructure? Kansas City had several options for contract restructures, including defensive tackle Chris Jones and center Creed Humphrey. So why did the team go with Smith? The biggest and most logical reason is that the Chiefs view Smith as a vital piece of their offensive line and their team leadership. They expect him to be with the organization through the remaining three years of his contract. I’m not sure they’re so certain about Jones. And Humphrey will soon be due a new contract after the center market jumped this offseason considerably. NFL players, coaches, GMs under the most pressure in 2026 | ESPN Xavier Worthy, WR, Kansas City Chiefs Worthy had a 157-yard game in the Super Bowl loss to the Eagles in 2024, but his 2025 season was ruined by a shoulder injury, and it’s unclear whether he is more than just a downfield burner. What’s new on Arrowhead Stadium menu during Chiefs’ games? Check out the ‘26 lineup | The Kansas City Star Collaborating with fellow chefs on the team and taking feedback from fans is how Wishon finds inspiration for what to bring each season. No items are repeats from years prior, such as the Uncrustable Crunch, Endzone Express appetizer box or the Breakfast Burger from 2025, or the Touchdown Toast from 2024. She will, however, try her hand at something that didn’t go over well in the past to see if the fans’ appetites have changed. This is why fans will see a few more dessert options on menus this year, like the Nutella Knockout (French toast croissant sprinkled with cinnamon sugar and filled with Nutella and sweet cream cheese) or the Sticky Bourbon Cinna-win Roll (homemade cinnamon roll topped with a Bourbon cream glaze and crispy bacon bits). Around the NFL Cardinals agree to terms with WR Michael Wilson on three-year, $75 million extension | NFL.com The Cardinals have agreed to terms with receiver Michael Wilson on a three-year, $75 million contract extension, NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport and ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Thursday. Wilson’s deal includes $47 million guaranteed and can be worth up to $78 million, per Rapoport and Schefter. The 2023 third-round pick will be signed in Arizona through the 2029 season. The Cardinals later announced the deal on Thursday. Giants’ Cam Skattebo says he mulled retiring after 2025 injury | ESPN He said Thursday that coming out of Arizona State, he thought about what he would do if he suffered a major injury in the NFL. “Coming out of college and going into the NFL, I think I gave myself one rule and it was if I ever got a major injury I was done playing,” he said. “And that happened seven games into my career, so it kind of sucked.” However, the monotony of his recovery, during which he said he would “do absolutely nothing” for 14 hours a day “for weeks on end,” helped him to “find who I am as a player and a person.” And that has reenergized him to play football this season. 49ers land in Melbourne ahead of next week’s game vs. Rams | Pro Football Talk The 49ers will practice in Melbourne on Saturday morning before beginning their usual game-week schedule on Monday. They will face the Rams at Melbourne Cricket Ground at 10;35 a.m. on Friday, Sept. 11, Melbourne time, which is 8:35 p.m. ET Thursday, Sept. 10, U.S. time. The Rams are not making the longest trip in NFL history until Wednesday, landing less than 24 hours before kickoff. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs cornerback L’Jarius Sneed on playing in the slot: ‘I miss it’ “Yeah, I miss it,” Sneed responded when asked about playing the Nickel position. “Spags threw me in there my second year; he just threw me in there, and I fell in love with it.” Before Sneed was locking down No. 1 receivers during the 2023 campaign, he was a playmaking slot defender who flashed as a blitzer and in run defense. The veteran sounded excited to have more responsibilities than just press coverage on an outside receiver off the line. “I feel like I can move around and do what I want to do,” Sneed said about playing in the slot. “Not just locked down on one side.” From The Feed Follow Arrowhead Pride on Social Media Facebook: Like our page Instagram: @ArrowheadPride X: Follow @ArrowheadPride AP Staff on X: See complete list

(Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On Thursday, the Kansas City Chiefs held the final “training-camp-style” practice of the 2026 preseason and were missing key players. Chiefs Kingdom is getting familiar with the uneasiness of reading that left tackle Josh Simmons is missing practice due to a back injury, but standout rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas has now been added to the list of potential worries with 11 days until Week 1. R Mason Thomas missed practice with a hamstring injury — Pete Sweeney (@pgsween) September 3, 2026 In addition to the report of a hamstring injury by friend of the site Pete Sweeney , Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com shared with his X followers that Thomas was observed “wearing a compression sleeve on his right leg.” This is the first time Thomas has popped up on the injury report since training camp began during the last week of July. During his time at the University of Oklahoma, Thomas missed multiple games due to ankle and quad injuries in three of his four years there. With three days off until the Chiefs reconvene on the practice field on Monday, the last session before game-week practices begin, it will be important to see if Thomas’ hamstring issue keeps him sidelined or if he’s able to participate, whether it be at a full or limited capacity.

title: Andy Reid praises Chiefs’ rookie and ‘No.2 back’ for pass protection
summary: One of the most surprising cuts among the many the Kansas City Chiefs made last weekend was veteran running back Emari Demercado, who was subsequently claimed by the Dallas Cowboys on the waiver wire. Behind lead back Kenneth Walker, the Chiefs have two inexperienced players: rookie Emmett Johnson and second-year back Brashard Smith, who played […]
full_text: ST. JOSEPH, MO - JULY 29: Emmett Johnson #10 walks to the field during the Kansas City Chiefs training camp on Aug 11, 2026 at Missouri Western State University in St. Joseph, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One of the most surprising cuts among the many the Kansas City Chiefs made last weekend was veteran running back Emari Demercado, who was subsequently claimed by the Dallas Cowboys on the waiver wire. Behind lead back Kenneth Walker, the Chiefs have two inexperienced players: rookie Emmett Johnson and second-year back Brashard Smith, who played wide receiver for the majority of his collegiate career. Moving on from an experienced player speaks to the trust in the young backs; head coach Andy Reid talked about the backfield during a press conference on Wednesday. “I like the way the running backs were running,” Reid said to local media. “They were hitting it and seeing it. It looks like they have good vision, which helps you, too. Enough patience, but good vision.” During training camp, Demercado told reporters that pass protection is a strength of his game . ”I take a lot of pride [in pass protection],” Demarcado told the media after practice on Wednesday. “I think that’s just where I found my niche in the league.” Heading into a season where quarterback Patrick Mahomes will be fresh off recovery from tearing his ACL and LCL, protecting the franchise player will be key. Reid made it clear he and the team have confidence in Johnson, the fifth-round pick from Nebraska, to step into a role usually suited for a veteran. When asked about what has stood out about Johnson over the last few weeks, Reid led with that skill. “Pass protection,” Reid shared. “We knew he could run the ball, but the thing we had to see was pass protection. For him to be that No. 2 back, you have to be able to do that. He’s a smart kid and willing to stick up in there.” While the starting offense is potentially readying to deploy a one-two punch with Walker and Johnson, Smith is a change-of-pace back who has improved in his own regard this summer. He shares the starting kick-return duties with wide receiver Nikko Remigio and understands the value of the third phase in football. “I love special teams,” Smith told reporters during a press conference on Wednesday. “I feel like that’s the spark that gets the offense going. I feel like special teams is the biggest part in the game… You make a big play, that gets everybody going; everybody on offense gets going after that. I love it.” While Kansas City is clearly more comfortable asking Remigio to field punts, Smith’s 4.39-second 40-yard dash time represents the big-play ability he has compared to Remigio on kick returns. The Chiefs like what Smith brings to the team with the ball in his hands, and could get creative on how to get the most out of his dynamism on both offense and special teams.

title: Chiefs cornerback L’Jarius Sneed on playing in the slot: ‘I miss it’
summary: To supplement the exciting, young players the Kansas City Chiefs have at the cornerback position, the team called on an old friend this summer. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed was signed during OTAs, bringing experience in the system to a defensive backfield that was missing a veteran. During training camp, spectators saw little of Sneed, who is […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 28: Cornerback L'Jarius Sneed #38 of the Kansas City Chiefs speaks to teammates from the sidelines of an NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Arrowhead Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images To supplement the exciting, young players the Kansas City Chiefs have at the cornerback position, the team called on an old friend this summer. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed was signed during OTAs, bringing experience in the system to a defensive backfield that was missing a veteran. During training camp, spectators saw little of Sneed, who is still managing a knee injury that has plagued him throughout his NFL career. Led by the Chiefs’ Vice President of Sports Medicine and Performance, Rick Burkholder, the team already has history with managing Sneed’s knee. The cornerback credited Burkholder, assistant athletic trainer Julie Frymyer and the entire staff for keeping him healthy this preseason. Sneed appeared in the third and final exhibition as the Nickel defender, manning the slot with the Chiefs’ starting defense. #Chiefs CB L'Jarius Sneed was asked if he's physically ready for week one. He says, "Wherever they put me at, I'm ready to go." — Sports Radio 810 WHB (@SportsRadio810) September 2, 2026 We might see more of that when the Chiefs take the field in Week 1. During a press conference on Wednesday, head coach Andy Reid talked about the versatility Sneed brings to the defense. “He can play inside or outside; that’s the advantage you gain there with him,” Reid told reporters. “He loves doing both, and his size- he’s a big kid, tough. Arguably one of the best corners in the league when he left here, and now that he’s back healthy and going, I’d tell you he’s playing like that right now. He’s doing a nice job.” Reid wasn’t exaggerating about Sneed loving to play both inside and outside as a cornerback. For the last three seasons, Sneed has been nearly exclusively used on the boundary, but defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo seems to have a plan for him as the slot defender in Nickel formations — and he is excited for the opportunity. “Yeah, I miss it,” Sneed responded when asked about playing the Nickel position. “Spags threw me in there my second year; he just threw me in there, and I fell in love with it.” Before Sneed was locking down No. 1 receivers during the 2023 campaign, he was a playmaking slot defender who flashed as a blitzer and in run defense. The veteran sounded excited to have more responsibilities than just press coverage on an outside receiver off the line. “I feel like I can move around and do what I want to do,” Sneed said about playing in the slot. “Not just locked down on one side.” One of the key reasons Sneed would be moving inside with the Chiefs is the young talent on the outside. Rookie Mansoor Delane and Nohl Williams are set up as the starters, and Sneed is supportive of his fresh-faced teammates. “He’s definitely a dog,” Sneed described Delane. “And he’s a first-rounder for a reason.” “They’re hungry, they’re young alpha males,” Sneed said about the young secondary as a whole. “They listen, they’re some dogs and I love that about them.” Spagnuolo is the ringleader of the group, so it’s no surprise that he was the one who reached out to Sneed when Kansas City started to show interest in re-signing him. The long-time defensive coach admires Sneed a lot, and that made this summer feel like a homecoming. “Definitely felt like I was coming back to my mom’s house,” Sneed smiled.

title: Can the Chiefs establish a superpower this season?
summary: Sports are about matchups, something that is often overlooked when discussing individual seasons rather than individual games. Why did the Philadelphia Eagles beat the Kansas City Chiefs in the Super Bowl two years ago? Simple. Matchups. The Eagles had the best defensive line in the NFL. The Chiefs’ offensive line was in shambles. Philadelphia exposed […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs warms up prior to a preseason game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sports are about matchups, something that is often overlooked when discussing individual seasons rather than individual games. Why did the Philadelphia Eagles beat the Kansas City Chiefs in the Super Bowl two years ago? Simple. Matchups. The Eagles had the best defensive line in the NFL. The Chiefs’ offensive line was in shambles. Philadelphia exposed what the AFC failed to. The matchup defined the season. The Eagles’ defensive line was a superpower. Most Super Bowl champions have one. The Seahawks’ superpower was their defense, rolling three deep at every position on that side of the ball. How are you supposed to handle that as an offense? You don’t, it turns out. You hold on as long as you can, and say, “good game” when it’s all over. The Chiefs lived a similarly charmed life for most of the past decade. The offense was among the best in the league from 2018-2022. Kansas City rode that superpower to three Super Bowl appearances and two titles. The defense emerged as the superpower in 2023 and 2024, resulting in two more Super Bowl appearances and another title. Those superpowers fizzled out last season. The offense wasn’t very good. The defense was fine, but nothing more. Even when you break down the individual aspects of the units, there wasn’t anything to write home about. The passing game was inefficient, the running game lacked explosion, the pass rush was non-existent. At least the run defense was solid, I suppose. For the first time in the era of quarterback Patrick Mahomes, the Chiefs lacked an identity. The team had nothing to hang its hat on each week. Will that change in 2026? Which areas of the roster are even capable of serving as the superpower for this year’s club? This is something I’ve spent an inordinate amount of time thinking about over the past few weeks. The Houston Texans and Denver Broncos come into the season boasting a ’superpower’ quality defense. You can throw the Seahawks’ defense into that category, as well, until proven otherwise. The Los Angeles Rams have an offense worthy of that kind of praise. The Dallas Cowboys and Chicago Bears each hope their offense can rise to that level. Do the Chiefs have anything that could rise to the point of being a superpower this year? Defense The pass rush doesn’t measure up against the likes of the Texans, Broncos or Seahawks. The spine of the defense, including defensive tackles Khyiris Tonga, Bryson Eason, Peter Woods, and linebacker Nick Bolton, has the potential to be quite good against the run, but it doesn’t look the part of an overwhelming group. There’s a lot to like about the potential of the team’s top cornerback duo: Nohl Williams and Mansoor Delane. However, the safeties are merely average, and the lack of a dominant pass rush doesn’t lend itself to a dominant group against the pass. So this unit probably won’t meet superpower status. Offense I’m as excited about the Kenneth Walker signing as anyone, but I’m not delusional enough to believe the Chiefs are going to become the 2024 Eagles when it comes to reliance on the ground game. This is still an offense led by long-time head coach Andy Reid; the season will still likely come down to the passing game. Mahomes, coming off a devastating knee injury, is going to be tasked with once again leading a dominant passing attack. The Chiefs will ask him to do so with Walker as a potential option in the screen game, Kelce as a weapon across the middle and a wide receiver group that includes Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, Tyquan Thornton, Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen. Is that enough? I think most outside observers would say no, but this is the same quarterback and offensive staff that turned Kelce, JuJu Smith-Schuster, Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Justin Watson, Isiah Pacheco, and Jerick McKinnon into the NFL’s No. 1 offense in 2022. With Mahomes at quarterback, everything feels possible as long as he’s on the field. But what worries me is that the Chiefs might need a dominant pass game to reach the ultimate goal. The Chiefs are no longer judged based on their ability to get to the playoffs. It’s not about winning the division or winning a certain number of games. Seasons are judged on a pass-fail scale, with an appearance in the Super Bowl as the only real way to pass. Reaching the Super Bowl will likely require something from this Chiefs team to become a superpower. I’m not entirely sure what that will be, but I’m excited to see how it plays out.

title: Chiefs News: Is everyone sleeping on the Chiefs?
summary: The latest Make sure you download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For more information, click here. The NFL season will start in less than a week. It’s time to make predictions about how the conference standings and the divisions will play out. The Kansas City Chiefs will battle with the Denver Broncos, […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 16: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs yells before the game against the Denver Broncos at Empower Field At Mile High on November 16, 2025 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Jamie Schwaberow/Getty Images) | Getty Images The latest Make sure you download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For more information, click here . The NFL season will start in less than a week. It’s time to make predictions about how the conference standings and the divisions will play out. The Kansas City Chiefs will battle with the Denver Broncos , Los Angeles Chargers and Las Vegas Raiders in the AFC West, looking to reclaim the throne the team sat on from 2016 – 2024. AFC West Preview: Is Everyone Sleeping on the Chiefs? | The Ringer Reasons for Concern I just gave you the stats on how the offense performed with Mahomes last season. And there’s another important stat: Mahomes often carried the Chiefs with his legs, averaging a career-high 30.1 rushing yards per game. Given that he’s coming off of a knee injury, the scrambling option that got the Chiefs out of a bunch of jams last season might not be as available to him. L’Jarius Sneed is embracing nickel role in his second act on the Chiefs | The Kansas City Star Thus, Kansas City’s best cornerback lineup may include the young corners outside, with Sneed turning back the clock four seasons and manning the nickel. “L.J. and I talked about it a lot, and he’s comfortable in both,” defensive coordinator Spagnuolo said last week. “Here’s his response always when I ask him: ‘Wherever you need me.’ That’s what he says. And so a little bit of it will be determined by who else is out there and what they can do. “L.J. was always a lot like Trent (McDuffie). L.J. was always effective inside. But when we needed him to match up on somebody outside, that kind of dictated it. So that same thing might happen. We’ll see where the other guys are.” Kansas City Chiefs set to host discarded Denver Broncos wide receiver on a tryout, but it’s probably not for the reasons you might think | A to Z Sports Why Broncos WR Cam Ross could make sense on the Chiefs’ practice squad The Chiefs kept Nikko Remigio as their primary punt return specialist, and Brashard Smith as their primary kick return specialist. However, that doesn’t mean that Brett Veach isn’t on the hunt for upgrades. At 5-foot-10 and 190 pounds, Ross is thickly built and durable. He has the build, demeanor, and experience to be valuable as a reserve return specialist. Xavier Worthy’s message about Patrick Mahomes ahead of Chiefs season: ‘He’s back’ | KMBC 9 “He’s back,” Worthy said Wednesday. “It’s not potentially back.” Worthy told reporters Wednesday that he had an up-close look at Mahomes’ work and rehab during the offseason. He said Mahomes’ determination stood out. “His grind, his will and want-to is beyond anybody I’ve ever seen,” Worthy said. “Whatever he puts his mind to, that’s what he’s gonna do. He kind of leads the team in that way.” ‘I Cannot Stand’ — Jason Kelce Expresses Frustration With Chiefs Posting Viral Travis Kelce Practice Clip | Pro Football Sports Network But his brother isn’t a fan. On the latest episode of the “New Heights” podcast, which they host together, the legendary center laid into teams who constantly post clips from practice on the internet. “I liked watching this because you’re my brother and I thought it was great. I cannot stand when teams put these clips online. The Eagles do it too. And I love the Philadelphia Eagles. And I love watching the clips, but they put out a clip of Jalen Carter beating the [expletive] out of a guy who’s trying his hardest to make the team. It’s like, dude, can we just let practice be its own thing? We don’t need to show everything.” Around the NFL New York Jets work out Justin Tucker, two other kickers: Source | The Athletic Tucker is the biggest name the Jets have brought in since the departure of last year’s kicker, Nick Folk, who signed with the Atlanta Falcons in March. Tucker, 36, is an eight-time All-Pro but hasn’t kicked in an NFL game since 2024 and hasn’t been on an NFL roster since the Ravens released him in May 2025. While a free agent last year, Tucker served a 10-game suspension for violations of the NFL’s personal conduct policy after multiple massage therapists accused him of sexually inappropriate behavior. Raiders name Kirk Cousins starting QB for Week 1 over Fernando Mendoza | ESPN Mendoza will be the first quarterback drafted with the first overall pick to not start in Week 1 since Baker Mayfield in 2018. Playing for the Cleveland Browns at the time, Mayfield didn’t start until Week 4 after Tyrod Taylor started the first three games that season. Kubiak didn’t comment on whether there’s an expectation for Mendoza to play this year. “[Cousins] played really good football,” Kubiak said. “I’m happy with all three of our quarterbacks. Kirk’s had a really good offseason, very [training] camp and he’s earned it.” Cowboys’ Stephen Jones on Pickens, Lamb: Not sure any team can pay two WRs at top of market | NFL.com “George is really wanting to put back-to-back years on top of one another so it’ll help his market,” Jones said. “And certainly, I know at some point — as does every player in this league — will want to be rewarded with a long-term contract. So that certainly puts pressure on us to have a unique situation there at wide receiver.” There are some instances with teams paying two receivers. Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins come to mind. A.J. Brownand DeVonta Smith just were broken up in Philly. However, it’s far from the norm and takes some juggling. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs Mailbag: What is Kansas City’s most concerning position group? EPF Asks Outside of injuries to certain position groups (which are impossible to predict), who do you see as first up for any practice squad elevations? I think the answer is fullback Ben VanSumeren. The Chiefs do not have a fullback on the roster, and none of their four tight ends stand out as strong run game blockers. With a significant portion of the offense being put on Kenneth Walker’s legs, VanSumeren’s skills may be needed. I suspect he chose Kansas City’s practice squad after being sold on the potential to carve out a significant role, despite not attending training camp with the team. title: Chargers among NFL’s most watchable teams in 2026
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are just over a week away from the start of the season, where they hope to be among the league’s top teams. The Chargers are eyeing their third straight playoff appearance, but they are attacking this season a bit differently than the past two. The team has a new offensive coordinator […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 27: Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers drops back to pass during the first half in a preseason game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Chargers are just over a week away from the start of the season, where they hope to be among the league’s top teams. The Chargers are eyeing their third straight playoff appearance, but they are attacking this season a bit differently than the past two. The team has a new offensive coordinator in Mike McDaniel, who is part of the reason why ESPN analyst Ben Solak placed the Chargers at No. 4 in his watchability ranking of all 32 teams. “The Chargers could easily have the coolest offense, with Herbert, McDaniel, speedy running back Keaton Mitchell, second-year running back Omarion Hampton and a healthy No. 1 receiver in Ladd McConkey. Even if the defense takes a step back without Jesse Minter (now the head coach of the Ravens) calling the shots, the Chargers should be better equipped to score fast, score big and win shootouts,“ Solak wrote . The only teams that ranked higher than the Chargers were the Detroit Lions, Los Angeles Rams and Chicago Bears, all of whom are in the NFC, making Los Angeles the most watchable team in the AFC. An explosive offense should take some of the pressure off the defense. Los Angeles utilized its defense last season to become a top-five unit in the league, but defensive coordinator Jesse Minter left the organization to join the Baltimore Ravens as their head coach. Chris O’Leary has taken over the defense, and they hope to be above average in the league if both the offense and the defense can play at a high level. The Chargers should not just be one of the most watchable teams in the league, but also one of the best.

full_text: San Diego, California - August 05: Quentin Johnston, Ladd McConkey and KeAndre Lambert-Smith of the Los Angeles Chargers look on during an NFL football training camp at Torero Stadium on Wednesday, Aug. 5, 2026 in San Diego, California. title: When did the Rams last beat teams on the 2026 schedule?
summary: It is officially one week until the Los Angeles Rams kick off the 2026 season against the 49ers down under. The Rams are looking to ensure they finish with more than an NFC Championship berth this season, as another Lombardi Trophy is firmly in their sights. Until then, LA has seven 2025 playoff teams on […]
full_text: Los Angeles Rams' Matthew Stafford rolls out while throwing a 2nd quarter touchdown to Davis Allen against San Francisco 49ers during NFL game at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara on Sunday, November 9, 2025. (Photo by Scott Strazzante/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) It is officially one week until the Los Angeles Rams kick off the 2026 season against the 49ers down under. The Rams are looking to ensure they finish with more than an NFC Championship berth this season, as another Lombardi Trophy is firmly in their sights. Until then, LA has seven 2025 playoff teams on its schedule, so the path back to the Super Bowl won’t be easy. It’s time to take a trip down memory lane and reflect on the last time the Rams beat each of their opponents on the upcoming 2026 regular season schedule. San Francisco 49ers Last Win: Week 10, 2025 In Round 2 of Matthew Stafford versus Mac Jones, the Rams got their revenge after losing to the Whiners a few weeks prior. Los Angeles jumped out to a 21-0 lead before San Francisco clawed within eight points just minutes into the fourth quarter. The Rams’ offense was unstoppable in the 42-26 win, as Stafford threw four touchdown passes and Kyren Williams tacked on two more scores on the ground. ‘Twas a fine day at the office in a win over a hated rival. Matthew Stafford completed 13 of 18 passes against the blitz for 161 yards and 4 TDs in the Rams' Week 10 win over the 49ers. Stafford's 13 TDs against the blitz over the last 3 weeks is 6 more than any other QB in a 3-game span over the last 10 seasons. #LARvsSF | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/68Fw4p3RTX — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) November 10, 2025 New York Giants Last Win: Week 17, 2023 This was a nail-biter and certainly gave fans heart palpitations. With the Rams fighting to secure a playoff spot, all they needed was to defeat the woeful Giants, which proved much harder than expected. Williams saved the day with three rushing touchdowns. New York had a chance to win it with 34 seconds left. However, veteran kicker Mason Crosby missed a 54-yarder as LA clinched its sixth win in seven games following a 3-6 start. THE RAMS SURVIVE Mason Crosby misses the game winning FG pic.twitter.com/O5afqCr5gG — NFL Retweet (@NFLRT) December 31, 2023 Denver Broncos Last Win: Week 16, 2022 Turf Show Ramily, let’s ride. Sorry, don’t know what got into me there. The Rams were riddled with injuries during their miserable 2022 campaign, yet played like a contender against a horrible Broncos squad led by Russell Wilson. Wilson threw three interceptions, including one to former Seahawks teammate Bobby Wagner. Baker Mayfield was lethal, going 24-of-28 for 230 yards and two touchdowns, while Cam Akers reached the end zone three times on the ground. Denver fired first-year head coach Nathaniel Hackett shortly after this one, so Merry Belated Christmas, Broncos Country? Philadelphia Eagles Last Win: Week 2, 2020 LA has yet to beat the Eagles in the Nick Sirianni era, so we’ll have to take the way-back machine to Doug Pederson’s time in Philly. Carson Wentz was a mess in 2020, his last season in the City of Brotherly Love. The Rams’ top-ranked defense picked off Wentz twice, en route to a 37-19 win. Meanwhile, Wentz’s draftmate Jared Goff threw three touchdown passes, all to tight end Tyler Higbee. Rams, if you finally end the streak, cheesesteaks will be on me. Buffalo Bills Last Win: Week 14, 2024 This one was awesome, perhaps one of the best Rams games ever under Sean McVay alongside the 2018 epic against the Chiefs (more on that shortly). Somehow, Los Angeles overcame MVP Josh Allen’s six-touchdown performance (three passing, three rushing) in the 44-42 win. They even managed not to choke away a 17-point lead entering the fourth quarter, as Buffalo scored 21 points in the final frame. So yeah, it was an insane game, putting it mildly. THE RAMS BEAT THE BILLS IN THE HIGHEST SCORING GAME OF THE SEASON 😱 WHAT A SHOWING FOR THESE TWO OFFENSES 👏 pic.twitter.com/8WPn5fQkiu — ESPN (@espn) December 9, 2024 Arizona Cardinals Last Win: Week 18, 2025 The poor Cardinals. They had a chance to play spoiler against a Super Bowl hopeful, but it crumbled away in the fourth quarter. After three quarters, though, Arizona was down by just three points. Jacoby Brissett did his best to keep them in it. However, Stafford’s four touchdown passes, including three in the second half, helped the Rams put away the Redbirds for good in the 37-20 win. Las Vegas Raiders Last Win: Week 7, 2024 After beginning the year 1-4, the Rams needed a win in the worst way. Luckily, that’s what the Raiders are for. There wasn’t much of note in this one, outside of Stafford and company not doing much, as they amassed only 259 yards of offense. LA jumped ahead 20-6 halfway through the third quarter and let the Raiders kick three field goals the rest of the way, making the final score appear respectable. Still, this game kicked off the Rams’ 9-3 stretch to end the 2024 campaign and secure the NFC West title. Los Angeles Chargers Last Win: Week 3, 2018 The Rams and Chargers have played twice since moving back to Los Angeles, splitting the matchups. Last time the Rams beat their roommate came early in the 2018 season. Goff threw three touchdown passes, including two to Robert Woods, as Todd Gurley produced over 150 total yards of offense and a touchdown in the 35-23 win to move to 3-0. Washington Commanders Last Win: Week 15, 2023 This was a game that could’ve gotten ugly for the Rams, especially if they couldn’t come away with the win. Los Angeles moved back to .500 in a 28-20 win over Washington, which saw them jump ahead 20-0 before the Commies chipped away at the lead. Had LA completely blown the lead, it would’ve put their playoff chances on life support. Fortunately, that didn’t happen, so we don’t have to consider that alternative history. Green Bay Packers Last Win: Week 8, 2018 Like Philadelphia, Green Bay has been the Rams’ Kryptonite, especially in the Matt LaFleur era. However, things were different in the waning weeks with Mike McCarthy at the helm. LA escaped the Coliseum after a too-close-for-comfort 29-27 win to move to 8-0. Thank the football gods for Ty Montgomery’s selfish fumbled kickoff, or else Aaron Rodgers might’ve handed the Rams their first loss. Kansas City Chiefs Last Win: Week 11, 2018 You just knew it had to be this one. What else can really be said about this one, besides calling it one of the greatest and most high-scoring games in NFL history? No words that I type will give this game justice, so that’s why I’ll leave these highlights here: The Rams and Chiefs gave us an all-timer when they met in 2018 🎬 NFL Schedule Release – Thursday at 8pm ET on ESPN/NFLN pic.twitter.com/uUUDAWTiCl — NFL (@NFL) May 13, 2026 Dallas Cowboys Last Win: Week 1, 2020 Can you believe it’s been this long since the Rams last beat the Cowboys? Crazy! In the first game ever at SoFi Stadium, LA limited a high-powered Dallas offense to just three second half points after them Boys had a one-point lead at halftime. It was a quality start to a new chapter in team history, but also a season where the Rams finished with the top-ranked defense in the league. Seattle Seahawks Last Win: Week 11, 2025 Out of three matchups between the NFC West foes last season, this one was the lone one the Rams won. It helped that Sam Darnold threw four interceptions, arguably his worst game of the season. Seattle’s defense kept the game close after LA had an early 14-3 lead. It wasn’t enough as the Rams narrowly won, 21-19. It’s a shame neither of the other two games between the teams went the Rams’ way. Darn it, Darnold, you had one job! Tampa Bay Buccaneers Last Win: Week 12, 2025 On Sunday Night Football, the Rams proved to the NFL world that they were the best team in football — a title that lasted a whole week. Anyways, in front of a primetime audience, they put on a show, winning 34-7. Los Angeles didn’t have to do much after going up 31-7 at…
