(Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Howie Roseman: The bottom line is winning, Jalen Hurts and Nick Sirianni do that – PFT Roseman said on WIP that he doesn’t agree with the perception that quarterback Jalen Hurts is “on the clock” and is heading into a make-or-break year to remain the franchise quarterback. “No I don’t agree with that,” Roseman said. Roseman said Hurts and head coach Nick Sirianni are proven winners, and that’s what the franchise needs. In games started by Hurts since Sirianni became head coach, the Eagles are 56-22 in the regular season and 6-4 in the postseason, including winning a Super Bowl. “I think the bottom line for us, in the position we’re in, and really for all our fan base, is winning football games,” Roseman said. “And all [Hurts] does is win football games, and that includes our head coach as well. For me, the barometer is winning football games. In terms of what Jalen does, he’s another guy with a tremendous track record. All he does is go out and play good football. Really excited to have him as our quarterback, excited about this season and what we have going forward, and I know there are a lot of fan bases out there that would love the results we’ve had with him as our starting quarterback.” Join the conversation! NFL players, coaches, GMs under the most pressure in 2026 – ESPN Let’s touch on that offensive shift, which involves three young offensive assistants around the NFL. O’Connell is about to ask his quarterback the same question that these assistants will of theirs, but as a highly regarded head coach, he’s not on the same sort of hot seat that any coordinator is in a given season. The Commanders (Jayden Daniels), Ravens (Lamar Jackson) and Eagles (Jalen Hurts) have three successful quarterbacks who have thrived working out of the shotgun or pistol and made a meaningful impact moving the ball with their legs on designed quarterback runs. And to some extent, those three teams are going to ask their quarterbacks to do something different in 2026 by operating from under center. […] It’s a big bet by three teams with quarterbacks who have already proved themselves as successful without needing to go under center very often. If those bets work out, Blough, Doyle and Mannion could be in line to earn head-coaching consideration as early as next offseason. If not, well, the world isn’t very forgiving to young playcallers. Mannion is the fourth Eagles coordinator in four years. Klint Kubiak had three single-season stints as a coordinator before landing his head-coaching gig with the Raiders. It’s about how to fall in love with the process. And my favorite chapter in this book was being faithful in the small things. …Here are the highlights of this chapter: Focus on the small things, focus on the things you can control.” Eagles TEs coach excited about Stowers’ development, but preaches patience – NBCSP “I think for every player coming into the NFL,” Mahaffey said, “I’m always extremely mindful of a rookie that they have the proper mindset in terms of, ‘What’s our point of focus each and every single day?’ And the most important thing is that you’re remaining process-driven. title: Mike Tomlin explains why Steelers traded George Pickens
summary: Ahead of the 2026 NFL season, former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and new NBC NFL analyst Mike Tomlin has been doing the media rounds, as NBC gets ready for season No. 21 of Sunday Night Football. Appearing on The Rich Eisen Show, Tomlin and the titular host discussed a variety of topics, including to the […]
full_text: Ahead of the 2026 NFL season, former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and new NBC NFL analyst Mike Tomlin has been doing the media rounds, as NBC gets ready for season No. 21 of Sunday Night Football. Appearing on The Rich Eisen Show, Tomlin and the titular host discussed a variety of topics, including to the polarizing decision Pittsburgh made to trade star receiver George Pickens to the Dallas Cowboys last May. “For us, I just thought, it’s not only play. It’s development in other areas, intangible areas. I think when you’re a high dollar, second-contract guy, I think there’s some leadership responsibilities, and things of that nature. And I just don’t feel like that was in his natural wheelhouse. We felt better about DK’s abilities in those areas.” Tomlin also noted that the Cowboys have been seemingly hesitant to give Pickens a second contract. “[A second contract] didn’t happen for us with George,” Tomlin said. “But that doesn’t necessarily mean that he’s not gonna be a spectacular player. I think he’s already proven that to a degree with his first year in Dallas. But there’s also been something that stopped Dallas from making that long-term commitment to him, as well…” The Steelers selected Pickens in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft out of Georgia, where he immediately showcased the ability to make spectacular catches and big plays, but on and off-field antics were constant. From being late to meetings and games to several on-field fights and tantrums, the Steelers decided to trade away the budding star, who went on to have an All-Pro season in 2025 with the Cowboys. title: Payton Wilson takes jab at previous Steelers coaching staff
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defense will look much different in 2026. Pittsburgh’s defensive unit was the highest-paid defense in the entire league in 2025, but finished 26th in total defense. Under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham and key additions like Jamel Dean and Jaquan Brisker, there is plenty of reason to be optimistic about the direction […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - JANUARY 12: Payton Wilson #41 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on from the field during an NFL wild card playoff football game against the Houston Texans at Acrisure Stadium on January 12, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers defense will look much different in 2026. Pittsburgh’s defensive unit was the highest-paid defense in the entire league in 2025, but finished 26th in total defense . Under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham and key additions like Jamel Dean and Jaquan Brisker, there is plenty of reason to be optimistic about the direction of the Steelers defense this season. Some players like third-year linebacker Payton Wilson believe that the new defense will allow him to play more freely. During his appearance on Cam Heyward’s “Not Just Football” Podcast , the Steelers linebacker did not mince words when talking about the shift in his mentality this season. “We were really tight as a linebacker unit, and they kind of empowered me in a sense to just go to play,” Wilson said. “And then just [Patrick Graham], his schematics, the way he coaches it. I’m finally just getting back to playing ball, rather than ‘Hey, if you make a mistake they might take you out.’ Or ‘Hey, if you do this wrong, you might come out of the game,’ and you don’t know when you’re coming back. Not to say I’m going to make mistakes all the time, but now it’s just playing ball and it kind of feels like my last few years of college again. It’s slowed down a lot and I’m just excited to be back out there rather than I guess nervous, not nervous but just anxious.” Without explicitly saying it, Wilson seems to be calling out Teryl Austin and Mike Tomlin’s coaching during his first several years in the league. It sounds like Wilson won’t be nitpicked for his mistakes as much this season and will be able to learn on the fly, something that he is suggesting may not have been possible under the former regime. Wilson totaled 79 tackles and nabbing an interception in his second year in the league. The Steelers’ inside linebacker room will look largely the same in 2026, allowing Wilson to continue to grow as a key piece of the Pittsburgh defense and into a more confident player overall. title: Seattle Seahawks sale officially closes, full list of co-owners revealed
summary: It has been just over 30 years since Ken Behring attempted to move the Seattle Seahawks to Southern California, with Paul Allen stepping in to buy the team and prevent a move. full_text: MOUNTAIN VIEW, CA - DECEMBER 03: Engineer Vinod Khosla and Neeru Khosla attend the 2018 Breakthrough Prize at NASA Ames Research Center on December 3, 2017 in Mountain View, California. (Photo by Jesse Grant/Getty Images) | Getty Images It has been just over 30 years since Ken Behring attempted to move the Seattle Seahawks to Southern California, with Paul Allen stepping in to buy the team and prevent a move. Allen’s purchase of the franchise, however, did not just prevent the franchise from moving, it also led to the hire of Mike Holmgren as head coach, which in turn led to the first Super Bowl appearance in team history. Of course, the Holmgren era turned into the blink that was the Jim Mora 2009 season, which led to the Pete Carroll era and two more Super Bowl appearances, including the first Lombardi Trophy in franchise history. Paul Allen then sadly passed away in 2018, but under the quiet watch of his sister, Jody Allen, the Seahawks continued their winning ways, specifically hoisting a second Lombardi after the 2025 season . As of Thursday, though, the Seahawks have announced that the ownership of the Allens has officially ended, with the recently approved sale of the team to the Khosla family having closed. Following approval by NFL owners on August 26, we are proud to announce the sale of our franchise to the Khosla family has officially closed. The Khosla family is now the controlling owner of the team. Read more » https://t.co/gzDMD529Lq pic.twitter.com/B359updk6B — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) September 3, 2026 Vinod Khosla will serve as the Chair of the franchise, with his wife Neeru Khosla as the Controlling Owner, and their son Neal Khosla as Vice Chair. Several other individuals or entities make up the remainder of the ownership group, including: Mark Stevens Aramburuzabala Family Val Blavatnik Sheryl Sokoloff Gonzalo Hevia Baillères Jesse van der Werf Samir Kaul Sunny Gupta Nader Naini Penny Pritzker Carlyle and Dynasty Equity Sixth Street And thus, when the Seahawks kick off their Lombardi Trophy defense on September 9 when the New England Patriots visit Lumen Field, it will not only mark the start of the 2026 NFL season, it will mark the start of the Khosla ownership era for Seattle.

title: How much the Patriots roster has changed since Super Bowl loss to Seahawks
summary: The Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots are set for a Super Bowl rematch next Wednesday at Lumen Field. While Patriots fans are hoping for some measure of revenge, neutrals are probably hoping this game is a little more dramatic and competitive than the Super Bowl proved to be. What we do know is that […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: A.J. Brown #1 of the New England Patriots warms up prior to an NFL preseason football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks and New England Patriots are set for a Super Bowl rematch next Wednesday at Lumen Field. While Patriots fans are hoping for some measure of revenge, neutrals are probably hoping this game is a little more dramatic and competitive than the Super Bowl proved to be. What we do know is that there have been some high-profile roster changes for both teams. There’s no need to rehash the Seahawks’ departures and additions because, well, there weren’t that many changes, plus we’re a Seahawks site obligated to cover every morsel of news. But what about the Patriots? The AFC champions made some major moves at wide receiver, but what else have they’ve done? Let’s look at who the Patriots lost and gained since the Super Bowl, with an emphasis on outgoing players who actually played meaningful snaps in Santa Clara. Notable New England Patriots departures Garrett Bradbury is no longer the starting center , having been traded to the center-needy Chicago Bears after Drew Dalman retired. Fullback Jack Westover was released during roster cuts and has since signed with the Washington Commanders practice squad. Starting wide receiver Stefon Diggs was released and is now with the Washington Commanders. Wide receiver Kayshon Boutte was traded in preseason to the wide receiver-needy Houston Texans, who lost Jayden Higgins for the season to a torn ACL. Boutte was second in touchdown receptions behind Stefon Diggs and third among wide receivers in catches. Reserve tight end Austin Hooper signed with his original drafting team, the Atlanta Falcons, in free agency. Hooper was TE2 behind Hunter Henry. Starting safety Jaylinn Hawkins signed with the Baltimore Ravens in free agency. Outside linebacker Anfernee Jennings was released and signed with the New Orleans Saints. Jennings was a rotational player (280 regular season defensive snaps). Starting outside linebacker K’Lavon Chaisson signed with the Washington Commanders as a free agent. Inside linebacker Jack Gibbens signed with the Arizona Cardinals in free agency. Gibbens started half the season and played defensive snaps in every game. Inside linebacker Jahlani Tavai was released and has since signed with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Tavai was a rotational backer who was one of New England’s leading special teams guys in snaps played. Defensive tackle Khyiris Tonga agreed to a three-year contract with the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency. Tonga played a career-high 337 snaps in a rotation with Milton Williams and Christian Barmore. Notable New England Patriots arrivals Wide receiver A.J. Brown was acquired in a big trade with the Philadelphia Eagles. Wide receiver Romeo Doubs signed a four-year contract as a free agent. Fullback Reggie Gilliam joined as a free agent from the Buffalo Bills. Starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker signed a three-year deal in free agency. Starting safety Kevin Byard signed a one-year contract in free agency. Outside linebacker and former Seahawk Dre’Mont Jones signed a three-year contract in free agency. New England Patriots rostered 2026 draft picks Round 1, pick 28: Right tackle Caleb Lomu Round 2, pick 55 : EDGE Gabe Jacas Round 3, pick 95 : Tight end Eli Raridon Round 5, pick 171 : Cornerback Karon Prunty Round 6, pick 196 : Left tackle Dametrious Crownover Round 6, pick 212 : Linebacker Namdi Obiazor Round 7, pick 234 : Quarterback Behren Morton Round 7, pick 247 : EDGE Quintayvious Hutchins New England Patriots unofficial depth chart Do not worry about the Patriots not having a punter listed, as Bryce Baringer is on IR and will be back later in the year. Veteran Mitch Wishnowsky will get elevated from the practice squad in his absence. One other note is that pass rusher Harold Landry is starting the year on PUP, so that’s another Super Bowl participant who won’t be factoring into Wednesday’s game. It’d be unwise to assume the rematch will go exactly like the Super Bowl; we already experienced this with the 2014 Seahawks winning an early season overtime thriller over the Broncos after thrashing them in Super Bowl 48. It would, however, be very funny if it does pretty much go the same way despite numerous starting lineup changes.

summary: In news that came as no surprise, the 49ers will be without defensive end Sam Okuayinonu for their season opener. full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JANUARY 11: Sam Okuayinonu #91 of the San Francisco 49ers lines up before the snap during an NFL wild card playoff football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on January 11, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images In news that came as no surprise, the 49ers will be without defensive end Sam Okuayinonu for their season opener. The Niners initially listed Okuayinonu as questionable with a foot injury and he did not make the long journey to Melbourne, Australia with the rest of the team on Thursday as they prepare to face the Los Angeles Rams next week. That was a clear sign Okuayinonu would likely not be hopping on a later plane to join the team and make his season debut, and the 49ers have now downgraded him to out. It is a significant setback at a position where the 49ers have scant depth. Okuayinonu would have been expected to start at defensive end across from Nick Bosa. In his absence, Keion White will be the favorite to take that spot, with rookie Romello Height — who has been dealing with an ankle injury — seemingly set for a decent workload if deemed healthy to play. San Francisco has Ogbo Okoronkwo and Vincent Anthony Jr. on the practice squad. With Okuayinonu out, it appears inevitable Okoronkwo will be elevated to the gameday roster. The 49ers are already trying to piece things together at defensive end before a ball has even been snapped in the regular season. Bosa is their only outside pass rusher whom the Rams will fear and he has been dealing with knee tendinitis following his ACL reconstruction. It is a desperate situation for the Niners to be in up front, and Okuayinonu’s absence makes it worse.

title: 49ers News: Swoop on those Rams like an angry magpie
summary: How the 49ers, NFL made ‘seamless’ travel plan to Australia“As the 49ers and the NFL collaborated over the past four months to move their football operation nearly 8,000 miles from the Bay Area to Melbourne, a unique challenge emerged of ensuring no California soil hitched a ride into one of the most isolated, ecologically guarded […]
full_text: NEWCASTLE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 16: (AUSTRALIA OUT) A magpie swoops a cyclist along Lambton Road, New Lambton, in Newcastle. (Photo by Darren Pateman/Fairfax Media via Getty Images/Fairfax Media via Getty Images via Getty Images). | Fairfax Media via Getty Images How the 49ers, NFL made ‘seamless’ travel plan to Australia “As the 49ers and the NFL collaborated over the past four months to move their football operation nearly 8,000 miles from the Bay Area to Melbourne, a unique challenge emerged of ensuring no California soil hitched a ride into one of the most isolated, ecologically guarded nations on the planet. Australia enforces some of the strictest biosecurity measures in the world. Introducing any sort of invasive species, insects or plant disease could lead to ecological and/or economic disaster, per the Australian government’s Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry. And while the cleaning process didn’t need to be over the top — the goal was to eliminate any large clumps of dirt or grass — it added a layer of consideration as the Niners prepared for departure….In this unchartered operational territory, some of the obstacles that 49ers and NFL officials pointed to include visa and passport acquisition; finding a plane big enough to carry the team comfortably; figuring out how to get through customs and security at the Melbourne airport; ensuring the practice facilities, hotel and stadiums were properly set up for an NFL team; and then how to break it all down and get back to California. The preparation started back in March, Valentine said, when the NFL asked the Rams and 49ers to send any items they would want but didn’t immediately need for Week 1 to a cargo ship in New York. That cargo ship also carried an additional 60,000 pounds of equipment from the league, including goal posts, Gatorade products and coolers, field equipment (chains, pylons, etc.), practice site equipment and medical gear. The ship departed on April 15 and arrived a little more than two weeks ago. And lest anyone believe Australia didn’t take its biosecurity efforts seriously, customs agents denied San Francisco’s supply of protein powder from entering the country.” Will Nick Bosa, George Kittle have Week 1 pitch counts? 49ers mailbag (paywall) “ Yes. Somehow Samuel, one of the most recognizable names in the sport, has flown under the radar this summer. Unlike most of his receiver and running back teammates, he didn’t miss any practices after signing with the team. And he’s looked good when he’s been out there. I’m not saying he’s back to looking like 2021-season Deebo. But 2023-season Deebo seems reasonable. The 49ers also have not been shy about giving him carries and talking about using him as a running back. So not only is Deebo back — wideback is back….I expect we’ll be talking about pass rush/defensive ends as the Nov. 10 trade deadline approaches. The 49ers will have a lot more five-man fronts and call more blitzes than in previous years. So their pass-rush and sack numbers might look good at a glance. But will it be anything more than a clever comb-over to disguise a bald spot? Keep an eye on points allowed per game, which last year was a respectable 21.8 despite all the missing players and lowly sack numbers.” Why 49ers rookie De’Zhaun Stribling refuses to see himself as a star: ‘I’m just a man’ (paywall) “When he came in, he was very businesslike,” said George McDonald, the Ole Miss wide receiver coach at the time. “He knew what he wanted to accomplish.” Aisha realized he was all grown up by then, a far cry from the 5-foot-nothing high school freshman who loved to surf and play kendama, a Japanese skill toy that was all the rage at Hawaii recesses during the mid-2010s. Stribling curbed the surfing habit for obvious reasons. He still owns a few kendamas… …Some players like the attention success brings. Stribling, his mom attested, would rather avoid it. He never wanted to be a role model or leader in the “rah-rah” mold. If his example was worth following, then fine. “He doesn’t want to have to mouthpiece it to say, ‘This is who I am,’” Aisha said. An athlete’s why can be revealing. Aisha never asked him what his was. “I always just assumed,” she said. “I don’t like the assumption I have. I just assumed it was that he wants to make his family proud.” What’s wrong with that? “I always tell him I’m proud of him,” she answered. “I’m proud of you. ‘Haven’t done anything yet.’ I’m proud of you. ‘Haven’t done anything yet.’” There’s a Hawaiian pidgin term for a person of Portuguese descent: podagee. Locally, it’s often an endearing way of identifying someone who talks a lot. Stribling seems more soft-spoken, unless he is with those who know him well enough to know he is a podagee, too.” How wife Jenna, life at home make 49ers star Brock Purdy a better quarterback “It allows me to be a better quarterback and everything because I understand, I am loved,” Purdy told NBC Sports Bay Area. “I have an amazing wife, an amazing daughter, and a second baby on the way, and everything is OK. “And now I get to go and play free and play hard for them, and it’s been better.” The Purdys, who make their offseason home in the Nashville area, still prioritize going for walks and grocery shopping as a family. “We love and crave those things,” Purdy said.” 49ers release first official depth chart “During the preseason, Collins played like a player who is still nursing an injury. He wasn’t forceful. He didn’t initiate things. He was too reactionary, and he often leaned on the player blocking him instead of trying to dictate the action or disengage. That’s something to keep an eye on as the season progresses. Because Gracen Halton was supposed to be the pass rush specialist. If he’s not going to play right away after missing all of this time, then it puts more pressure on the rest of the defensive line — or Keion White when he kicks inside — to produce. The defensive line rotation is anyone’s guess if Sam Okuayinonu is out or if Romello Height can’t play. Malik Mustapha returning to practice is a great sign. He’s the player with the highest ceiling, perhaps in the entire secondary.” BONUS: Magpie swooping: Inside the Australian bird’s annual reign of terror “Streets and parks become a battleground, as the birds – descending from above and attacking from behind – swoop down on anything they fear poses a threat to their offspring. High up in their nests, they rule over their kingdom with an iron claw, while on the ground, humans dust off their protective hats – traditionally a plastic ice-cream container – and duck for cover. At times drawing blood, their ambushes can cause serious injuries, and in a handful of cases, death. …But they also say magpies can interpret simple gestures like running through their territory as a slight, and not only can they recognise individual faces – they tend to hold a grudge. “Let’s say you’ve shown some kind of response by waving your arms or trying to hit the bird away from you,” says animal behaviourist and Emeritus Professor Gisela Kaplan, who literally wrote the book on magpies. “That act is a declaration of open war. A magpie interprets that as a sign of aggression and will then always swoop that person from then on, every year. “[And] somebody of a similar build, a similar height and hair colour may get mistaken in their fury, or anxiety.” …But if all else fails, beg for mercy. Although authorities usually warn against feeding wild birds, Prof Kaplan suggests leaving a peace offering like a little bit of bread or meat to win the magpies’ favour. “You can make friends with magpies… they tend to be very diplomatic,” she says.”

title: Will the 49ers benefit from any Rams suspensions ahead of Week 1?

full_text: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - JULY 27: Puka Nacua #12 of the Los Angeles Rams looks on during the Los Angeles Rams Training Camp at Loyola Marymount University on July 27, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images) | Getty Images Will the NFL suspend Puka Nacua? Or Alaric Jackson, for that matter. The San Francisco 49ers are set to face the Los Angeles Rams in an international game next week. Nacua and Jackson, the Rams’ projected starting left tackle, aren’t on the commissioner’s exempt list — a sign that they’ll be good to go for Week 1. For those who don’t know, Nacua is currently facing a civil lawsuit alleging physical assault and battery, in which the victim alleged Nacua bit her on the shoulder on New Year’s Eve. In this New York Post article , Puka’s ex doesn’t have any specific allegations, but she claimed abuse on Nacua’s part. We’re a week away from the game, and the NFL still hasn’t decided whether to suspend Nacua or Jackson. In 2017, the NFL suspended kicker Josh Brown for six games on September 8. In 2015, the NFL suspended one player on September 3, another on September 5, and five others on September 8 for violation of the Personal Conduct Policy. The year prior, Ray Rice’s domestic violence incident landed him an indefinite suspension on September 8. Six days prior, Josh Brent was suspended for six games. There was one more suspension back in 2010 that occurred on September 1. So there are enough examples of players getting suspended during the first week of September since 2010. However, we know the NFL cares about getting eyeballs on its product. We’ll see whether the suspensions happen after Australia, since the league probably doesn’t want those incidents discussed on the broadcast or leading up to the game. Will we see any suspensions?

title: Who should be the starting safety duo for the 49ers this season?
summary: This time last year, as the San Francisco 49ers were heading into their Week 1 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, Kyle Shanahan was reluctant to name his starting safeties. In a mild upset, rookie Marques Sigle beat out Ji’Ayir Brown, as the 49ers took the field with a Day 3 rookie and veteran Jason Pinnock. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - NOVEMBER 24: Malik Mustapha #6 and Ji'Ayir Brown #27 of the San Francisco 49ers on the sideline during the game against the Carolina Panthers at Levi's Stadium on November 24, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Panthers 20-9. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images This time last year, as the San Francisco 49ers were heading into their Week 1 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, Kyle Shanahan was reluctant to name his starting safeties . In a mild upset, rookie Marques Sigle beat out Ji’Ayir Brown, as the 49ers took the field with a Day 3 rookie and veteran Jason Pinnock. Sigle’s start to the season was a mixed bag. The ball has a way of finding you when things aren’t going your way as a defensive back. It’s like in baseball, when a new defensive player takes the field. In Sigle’s case, he allowed a near-perfect passer rating in 27 targets during the first month and a half, starting with 23 of those passes resulting in completions. In Sigle’s defense, he was probably in a position to make a play on the ball for about 20 of those. But that doesn’t cut it in the big leagues, as he found out. As frustrating as Sigle was, he at least showed promise. The same cannot be said for Pinnock, who wound up allowing a whopping 88.5% of his 26 targets to be completed, including four for touchdowns, without registering a single pass breakup. The 49ers hoped to weather the storm until Malik Mustapha returned from an injury. By the time Week 7 rolled around, Sigle and Pinnock’s snaps were halved. Tig took over as the starter and never looked back. Brown finished the season allowing 61.5% of his passes to be completed, but did surrender six touchdowns compared to two pass breakups and a pair of interceptions. He increased the floor at the position ever so slightly. Mustapha slowly but surely regained his role as the starter, and was cemented there by Week 8. Mustapha recorded the lowest missed tackle rate of the bunch, but at 15%, it was a figure that paled in comparison to the numbers Jimmie Ward and Jaquaski Tartt put up. Those veterans may not have had the flashy plays in coverage that fans want, but their mistakes were few and far between. Mustapha limited the damage in coverage for most of the season, outside of a 44-yarder in his first start against the Texans. Will it be another season where Mustapha needs to work himself back into shape before starting, or will Raheem Morris trust Mustapha out of the gate? His defense spent the last month with Brown and Sigle as the starting duo. In a situation that’s likely to be fluid until two either prove they have what it takes to be starters in this league, or one eliminates themselves, which duo do you trust the most to start?
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers release first official depth chart
summary: We will not hear from the San Francisco 49ers until their next block of practices. On Wednesday, the team released its first official depth chart of the season. Keep in mind that the communications staff put this together. The reaction to Connor Colby trotting out with the rest of the starters and lining up at […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Kyle Shanahan of the San Francisco 49ers looks on during a preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images We will not hear from the San Francisco 49ers until their next block of practices. On Wednesday, the team released its first official depth chart of the season. Keep in mind that the communications staff put this together. The reaction to Connor Colby trotting out with the rest of the starters and lining up at left guard after being demoted to third string would be comical. If Colby is the best player for the job, then so be it. That doesn’t change the hilarious fact that he would have gone from first string to third and back to the first team in a month’s span. It wouldn’t be surprising to see Deebo Samuel or Demarcus Robinson either outsnap De’Zhaun Stribling or all three play the same amount. We know the trio’s usage will differ. One area where Deebo’s addition is being slept on is his blocking prowess. He was exceptional in that category. Robinson was not. So maybe Robinson only sees the field on obvious passing downs, where Stribling and Deebo can be used more on a down-to-down basis. On the defensive side, Alfred Collins is going to have to take a page out of Nick Bosa’s playbook and rip the band-aid off. Collins told reporters he’s “not where I wanna be yet,” but acknowledged he’s made strides since then. Collins’ shoulder injury kept him out for the first block of training camp practices back in July. During the preseason, Collins played like a player who is still nursing an injury. He wasn’t forceful. He didn’t initiate things. He was too reactionary, and he often leaned on the player blocking him instead of trying to dictate the action or disengage. That’s something to keep an eye on as the season progresses. Because Gracen Halton was supposed to be the pass rush specialist. If he’s not going to play right away after missing all of this time, then it puts more pressure on the rest of the defensive line — or Keion White when he kicks inside — to produce. The defensive line rotation is anyone’s guess if Sam Okuayinonu is out or if Romello Height can’t play. Malik Mustapha returning to practice is a great sign. He’s the player with the highest ceiling, perhaps in the entire secondary. After missing so much time, we’ll see whether Mustapha has a chance to start, or if he gets worked in the rotation in some capacity. Remember, even when he was healthy, he was rotating with Marques Sigle.

title: 49ers pass rush takes another hit as starter listed as questionable with a foot injury
summary: Late Wednesday night, multiple San Francisco 49ers reporters said Sam Okuayinonu is not flying with the team to Australia because of a foot injury. Okuayinonu will have a questionable designation for Week 1. It’s not out of the question that he travels later on and can still play, but it’s not a good sign he […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 17: Sam Okuayinonu #91 of the San Francisco 49ers reacts after making a tackle during the second quarter of an NFL divisional playoff football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on January 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Late Wednesday night, multiple San Francisco 49ers reporters said Sam Okuayinonu is not flying with the team to Australia because of a foot injury. Okuayinonu will have a questionable designation for Week 1. It’s not out of the question that he travels later on and can still play, but it’s not a good sign he isn’t traveling with everybody else. According to NBC Sports Bay Area’s Matt Maiocco, everybody else traveled. The 49ers are already paper-thin when it comes to the health of their edge rushers. Nick Bosa did team drills for the first time during Wednesday’s practice . Bosa practicing is a great sign. However, it’s unlikely he’ll be able to work his way into football shape in a week. Bosa and Okuyinonu were likely the first two defensive ends to take the field. They are the two best, and arguably only, run-stopping options at the position. Keion White is better suited inside, while Romello Height — who made plays and was competitive against the run in the preseason — was drafted to rush the passer. The 49ers were likely to elevate Ogbo Okoronkwo from the practice squad before Okuayinonu’s injury. That’s inevitable now if Sam O can’t suit up. There might need to be another move at the position if Romello Height continues to miss practice with an ankle injury. In an ideal world, Sam O plays on early downs, with White and Height spelling him on passing downs. But without Okuayinonu, and potentially Height, White has to rush predominantly from the edge since you’re short on bodies. In contrast, defensive tackles Alfred Collins and CJ West may have to pick up the slack on passing downs. We could find out how much Morris trusts rookie Jaden Dugger earlier than expected. Injuries could force his hand into more 5-man fronts with Dugger walked down on the line of scrimmage. That may have been the case, regardless of Okuayinonu or Height’s availability, given how many three-tight-end sets the Rams use. The domino effect of potential injuries up front will test Raheem Morris’s creativity and the Niners’ depth.

title: Will CB Melvin Smith add something to Titans, or is he just another Jalyn Armour-Davis?
summary: The Tennessee Titans were awarded three players off waivers on Monday. Among the new additions was cornerback Melvin Smith. The Titans also signed safety Terrell Burgess and offensive tackle James Hudson, making five total additions after the initial 53-man roster was set. Smith entered the league as an undrafted free agent with the Kansas City […]
full_text: Aug 9, 2025; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Melvin Smith Jr. (39) against the Arizona Cardinals during a preseason NFL game at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Tennessee Titans were awarded three players off waivers on Monday. Among the new additions was cornerback Melvin Smith. The Titans also signed safety Terrell Burgess and offensive tackle James Hudson , making five total additions after the initial 53-man roster was set. Smith entered the league as an undrafted free agent with the Kansas City Chiefs last offseason. Titans GM Mike Borgonzi was already in Tennessee, meaning he isn’t directly connected to Smith through his KC days. It’s safe to assume the tendencies he searches for in late-round cornerbacks is still in place with the Chiefs, however. Smith played 47 total snaps for the Chiefs during this recent preseason period. The former Southern Arkansas standout allowed four receptions for 29 yards and a touchdown, per Pro Football Focus. He also had six tackles. The Titans waived Erick Hallett II to make room for Smith on the 53-man roster. It was a bit surprising, because Hallett played pretty well throughout training camp and the preseason. He has since been re-signed to the practice squad, so at least Borgonzi managed to retain him. Smith did not play a single regular-season snap for the Chiefs in 2025. He essentially spent his entire rookie campaign on the practice squad. The Chiefs brought in multiple new cornerbacks this offseason, including former Titans L’Jarius Sneed and Kristian Fulton. They also drafted multiple corners, including first-round pick Mansoor Delane. That made Smith expendable to them. It’s worth remembering the Titans claimed two cornerbacks off waivers last season. They added Jalyn Armour-Davis and Sam Womack II via the wire process. Armour-Davis was a downright liability, and Womack couldn’t really get on the field for them. Most waiver additions amount to nothing; that’s why they’re available in late August. Borgonzi’s history with late-round cornerbacks in Kansas City makes the Smith addition interesting. Together, they found gems like Joshua Williams, Sneed, and Jaylen Watson. Speaking of Williams, he begins his first season with the Titans on short-term IR. That makes Smith the fifth cornerback right now. Hopefully Smith turns into a waiver-wire gem.

(Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Daily Slop – 4 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Commanders.com Smoot, Paulsen and Moss talk about Commanders linebackers (and more) The linebacker position Smoot: I think one thing about the middle linebacker section is that all these guys are athletic profilers off the chain. Even Kain Medrano can run. Jordan Magee can get out there and get it. When I look at them, nobody’s there just because “I’m mentally good.” Everybody’s there because “I’m mentally good, plus I’m a hell of an athlete.” Paulsen: I think they’re all above nine RAS [Relative Athletic Score]. Jordan was like 9.7; Kain was like 9.8. Leo Chenal was 9.9, and obviously Sonny was a 10 (unofficial). Moss: Looking at this linebacker room, it’s funny, because I visually the 2012 receiver corps that we had here. We had Pierre [Garcon]; we had myself, Leonard [Hankerson], Al [Aldrick Robinson], [Josh] Morgan. With all that being said, you look at that group of guys, and you’re like, “Who’s gonna play? Who’s not gonna play?” And we all played, and there were certain packages we came in, and we all swapped out. I’m looking at these linebackers, knowing what we run and how we run things…but I’m very interested to see the different kind of packages that they put on the field because of what their skill set allow them to do.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Nicki Jhabvala’s mailbag What is the team’s thinking around the offensive line? It is now abysmal. What are the next steps? I believe depth and starters are needed. What are your thoughts? — Avinash P. The team’s thinking is that it likes the guys it has on the O-line and didn’t feel it was worth paying a center $27 million. But to say the group is “abysmal” is a leap at this point. (For the record, I said the offense looked the worst it has in years during Washington’s joint practice with the Ravens last week. The O-line was rough that day , and it was a group that featured three starters, plus a rotation of guys at the two other spots that the team ultimately deemed worthy of making its active roster and practice squad. But I never said the offense overall looked horrible for all of camp and the preseason. Hardly.) That joint practice at Baltimore isn’t necessarily an indicator of how the front five will play in the regular season. Neither are preseason games. But the center position and the overall depth on the interior worry me, much like the receiver depth worried me ahead of last season. I agreed — and still agree — with the team’s decision not to give Tyler Linderbaum, or any center, a record contract. Washington had several premium positions to fill, will have more premium positions to fill next offseason, and will soon have to give Jayden Daniels a massive deal. I also don’t mind the decision to make Allegretti the starting center; he’s played both guard and center over the years. But the move meant losing a key piece of Washington’s depth, which was stripped again when Brandon Coleman moved back outside to tackle in the wake of Tunsil’s triceps injury (which, by the way, was undoubtedly the biggest blow to the line and offense overall). After all of this, could the line surprise and play really well together? Of course. Could the offense turn into one of the league’s more prolific groups? Sure. This team shocked the NFL in 2024 and could absolutely do it again with Daniels at the helm — if he can stay upright and healthy. Have you ever done this much reporting on a team’s center position before Week 1? — Jim S. I have not. But there was a good bit of center talk in 2021, when injuries decimated Washington’s line and it was down to its fifth center in practice for Week 14. Jon Toth, who doubled as a big-and-tall model (‘ memba him ?!), briefly took reps with the starters when Chase Roullier, Wes Schweitzer, Tyler Larsen and Keith Ismael were all dealing with injuries. Since the Peters/Quinn combo arrived in 2024, a lot of young players have had trouble getting meaningful playing time. Does it seem like the team/management has a priority to develop/assess its drafted players this season, or should we expect more playing time for free agent veterans? — Anonymous U. I beg to differ. First, if you’re looking solely at playing time, players with two years or fewer in the league were on the field for 23.8 percent of Washington’s offensive snaps and 9.7 percent of the team’s defensive snaps over the past two seasons. Those rates were the 11th- and 10th-highest, respectively, in the NFL in that span. I feel like there’s only been so much put out there of all of us, all five being out there at once.” Conerly also called out the Ravens’ joint practice that caught so much attention, saying, “You’ve got your little bit of what you guys saw and how you guys interpret that from the joint practice, but I don’t necessarily think it went that way.” Conerly doubled down in another interview with Mitchell Tischler, saying, “Working throughout the offseason, just knowing the amount of work that everyone’s put in…we’ve came so far…If there was like this narrative about us in the spring…alright, it could have been true. But at the same time, we have been working our a– off. There is no reason for there to be a false negative without a game being played yet.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) NFL decision-makers’ 2026 survey: MVP predictions, Jayden Daniels vs. Caleb Willams vs. Drake Maye and more As evidenced by the vote, Maye is further along in his development, but the Williams backers believed another jump is on the horizon. “After this year,” a head coach said, “it will be Caleb.” Daniels has become the forgotten man in the equation after his sophomore season was shortened to seven starts due to mounting injuries. Remember, he was viewed as an MVP candidate a year ago. “Daniels still has the most true talent,” a head coach said. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Heavy.com Jayden Daniels Prepared to Trust the Pocket More Taking off to scramble too often has long been a problem for Daniels. Jones put the problem into perspective with these numbers : “The league’s average quarterback scramble rate the past two seasons is 5.5 percent. Daniels sits atop the NFL at 13.8 percent, multiple percentage points ahead of runners-up like Justin Fields, Tyler Huntley and Drake Maye. Those stats are why Blough is putting “up some guardrails” around the Commanders’ QB1. The new safety measures include Daniels getting under center more often and leaning on the play-action passing game . Kingsbury’s up-tempo pace forced defenses to stick with largely the same personnel and hastily called pressure and coverage looks. This made opponents more predictable and easier for Daniels to read, but Blough is asking his quarterback to be more thoughtful. Daniels is going to have to sharpen his skills deciphering the pre-snap looks shown by defenses. title: How Commanders could operate with seven receivers on 53-man roster
summary: The Commanders chose to keep seven receivers on their initial 53-man roster. That’s a bit higher than the normal five or six.   Washington was among five teams to keep seven receivers on its initial 53-man roster, with every organization having slightly different reasons for retaining that number.   Sometimes its a placeholder until other […]
full_text: The Commanders chose to keep seven receivers on their initial 53-man roster. That’s a bit higher than the normal five or six. Washington was among five teams to keep seven receivers on its initial 53-man roster, with every organization having slightly different reasons for retaining that number. Sometimes its a placeholder until other moves can be made to even things out. The Commanders have held at seven to this point, for a few reasons. They’ve got punt returner Jaylin Lane in the position group. Kick returner Luke McCaffrey’s there, too. They also have deserving veterans in Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown who probably won’t take a practice squad spot (and could find work elsewhere). Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs and rookie third-round pick Antonio Williams are immovable objects on the roster and will be on-field mainstays during this season. That’s how you get to seven. McCaffrey was someone thought to be on the bubble, but I think there’s a decent chance he doesn’t make it through waivers. As a returner, capable slot receiver and fairly recent Day 2 draft pick , it’s highly possible someone puts in a claim. If that’s not worth the risk, then you’re sitting at seven. The Commanders are thin at other spots – cornerback comes to mind, as does running back – but there are good players at those positions who are worthy of a game-day elevation. New practice squad signing Terell Smith could help in the cornerbacks room and on special teams. Even if Robert Henry Jr. needs more development, Craig Reynolds has experience to step up and help the running backs. That allows the Commanders to continue with relative bloat at one spot. On game day, you’ll probably have an inactive receiver, likely Brown or Burks considering the special teams value with McCaffrey and Lane. The primary receiver rotations won’t change. As previously mentioned, it’s fair for McLaurin, Diggs and Williams to see the most action. Brown could be a stretch-the-field option if he’s active while Burks could be a big-bodied target, depending on the best possible matchups. Those guys can provide injury protection should something go wrong in-game. They can provide Diggs some relief should his snap counts be relatively down, as they were last season in New England . Layne has improved as a receiver and has serious speed. McCaffrey can help as a taller slot, as he has previously proven. The Commanders have options, especially with tight-end usage expected to be high. Chig Okonkwo will also play off the line, so the Commanders have tons of receiver options. Will they keep seven all season? That seems unlikely, especially if another position group gets beset by short-term injuries. The player they move in the situation could be based on performance and need, as they continue to mold the roster to best serve all position groups.

title: Will Adam Peters UDFA success alter Washington Commanders trajectory?
summary: Recently, long-time sports writer Mike Tanier wrote a response to a question in his mailbag article attempting to validate the idea the Washington Commanders could be the “worst team in the league” this year. Part of his logic included the idea Adam Peters “should have stockpiled late-round picks and UDFAs and given the ones they […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - AUGUST 23: Colson Yankoff #41 of the Washington Commanders runs with the ball after making a catch in the second quarter of the NFL Preseason 2025 game against the Baltimore Ravens at Northwest Stadium on August 23, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images Recently, long-time sports writer Mike Tanier wrote a response to a question in his mailbag article attempting to validate the idea the Washington Commanders could be the “worst team in the league” this year. Part of his logic included the idea Adam Peters “should have stockpiled late-round picks and UDFAs and given the ones they did have better opportunities to win roster spots and roles.” Unfortunately, Mr. Tanier apparently hasn’t spent much time researching his subject. The Commanders did come in below the league average in 2026 with nine undrafted free agent signings this year; well below the Baltimore Ravens league-leading nineteen . However, the lower number provided the coaching staff the opportunity to give those players more reps to actually compete for roles and have a chance to crack the roster. Undrafted free agent kicker Drew Stevens is the most obvious example, as Larry Izzo awarded him the starting role after the first preseason game, but there were others. The loss of Laremy Tunsil exposed concerns regarding the offensive line depth, and highly athletic, yet raw, guard prospect Tanoa Togiai found himself on the final 53-man roster while 2024 UDFA safety Tyler Owens also made it past final cuts over long-time veteran Will Harris. Adam Peters has brought a fundamental shift in how Washington views and incorporates undrafted free agents. In 2024, the Washington Commanders paid the highest amount of guaranteed money to undrafted free agents in the league, signing Chigozie Anusiem ($300K) and running back Michael Wiley ($275K), and similarly awarded one of the highest guarantees of 2025 to offensive lineman Timothy McKay ($275K). While the COVID years are an understandable exception, Ron Rivera often signed a similar number of undrafted free agents. The perception, though, was that these hopefuls were given little, if any, real chance to win roster spots, with Rivera preferring to keep veterans like David Mayo in reserve roles. When Adam Peters and Dan Quinn arrived in 2024, they preached open competition as one of their core philosophies, and while that tenet may appear to be inconsistently held at times, it has rung true for their undrafted free agents. Tyler Owens and Colson Yankoff both won roster spots in 2024 based on their innate athletic ability and special teams play. Headed into 2026, both seem to be poised to claim a bigger role with the team based on their development and scheme fit. Undrafted free agent linebacker Ale Kaho was somewhat of a surprise addition to the roster in 2025, but he won a spot based on his performance in the preseason and tackling ability. While Kaho has been relegated to the practice squad this year, he holds value as a potential depth piece to elevate during the season and a prospective member of the roster in 2027. While Kaho was the only UDFA to make the final 53-man roster in 2025, fellow undrafted free agent Ricky Barber made good on his potential in 2026 and is slotted in as a replacement for Johnny Newton in the current lineup. Throw in Drew Stevens winning a starting role as the kicker and Tanoa Togiai’s inclusion, and it would be fair to say Adam Peters has found some success signing undrafted free agents. Given the number of mid-to-late round picks given away in various trades, the unexpected additions are welcome, but do they really have any significant impact on the speed of the Washington Commanders’ recalibration? To answer, we take a look at an NFL franchise known for their success with undrafted free agents, the Baltimore Ravens. Over the last past five years, 92 undrafted free agents have earned a role on the Ravens active roster or practice squad, the most in the league. Baltimore has had at least one undrafted rookie on their initial 53-man roster for 22 of the last 23 years, with the exception being a COVID-limited year in 2020. The undrafted free agent market has become quite competitive over the years, with teams scrambling to sign players as quickly as possible. So what is the reason for their success? Mark Azevedo, Baltimore’s current director of player personnel, coordinates not only with the scouting department but also the coaching staff. While Azevedo certainly doesn’t discount the hard work done by his team, he knows that Baltimore’s best advantage is their own proven track record of undrafted free agents making the team. The draft isn't the only way to become a Raven. Here's what our UDFA process looks like behind the scenes. You missed Wired?! We got you covered: https://t.co/to1BNtNYs3 pic.twitter.com/lHYhixtJ9M — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) May 25, 2026 In short, success breeds more success. That is why the accomplishments of players like Tyler Owens and Colson Yankoff, along with a high-visibility role for Drew Stevens, may aid Adam Peters in his roster-building efforts going forward. As the team continues to face frequent roster churn along with a potentially high-value contract extension for Jayden Daniels in the near future, continued success in the UDFA market could play a role in helping restore the long-term success of the franchise sooner than later. This article contains statistics and information on the Baltimore Ravens from Ryan Mink, managing Editorial Director for Ravens.com. To read his full piece on the Ravens’ success with UDFAs click here .

title: Commanders roster: Jayden Daniels, pass rush among Washington strengths
summary: The Commanders training camp and preseason took an odd trajectory. Optimism pervaded through everything done at the beginning, even when Nick Allegretti suffered a calf injury and Trey Amos wasn’t practicing, and it became unavoidable that Washington needed a No. 2 receiver.   It crescendoed a few weeks later when Stefon Diggs got signed and held […]
full_text: The Commanders training camp and preseason took an odd trajectory. Optimism pervaded through everything done at the beginning, even when Nick Allegretti suffered a calf injury and Trey Amos wasn’t practicing, and it became unavoidable that Washington needed a No. 2 receiver. It crescendoed a few weeks later when Stefon Diggs got signed and held an all-timer of an introductory press conference. But then Laremy Tunsil got hurt and Johnny Newton went down and Allegretti and Amos kept not coming back and all these small injuries kept cropping up. The joint practice versus Baltimore and the lack of post-cut additions seemed to keep pushing vibes down. Now we’re nearing the regular season and Commanders sentiment seems worse than before. It’s not all doom-and-gloom in Washington, with this roster holding several pluses as we enter the 2026 campaign. Let’s provide some counter programming here and talk about Commanders roster strengths heading into Week 1. Jayden Daniels and the QB room Expectations for Jayden Daniels’ third NFL season are varied. Some expect him to return to 2024 production and remind everyone why he was named offensive rookie of the year . Others have somehow forgotten that season ever existed. Others panic about the lack of a supporting cast (more on that later). Those who watched Commanders practice all summer have a different take on Daniels. He has been super accurate and throwing receivers open while having no trouble acclimating to David Blough’s new offensive system despite it’s increased under-center requirements. Daniels has taken the steps required to be a force in 2026 and, if you’re going to discuss any position among a roster’s strengths, quarterback is what you want. Daniels can be an upper-tier starter and Marcus Mariota’s returning from an MCL sprain to be a quality backup. You don’t want Athan Kaliakmanis playing in a game right now, but there’s hope he develops into someone who can down the line. Frontline skill players The Commanders have a quality group of skill players who can perform almost any function well. They have Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs as frontline producers in the passing game. They’ve got a talented slot option in Antonio Williams. Want a receiving tight end who can line up anywhere? Chig Okonkwo. A blocking tight end? John Bates. A running back who excels at catching passes? Rachaad White. How about an agile zone runner with good burst? Bill Croskey-Merritt. You certainly see my point here, that the Commanders have a man for every offensive requirement. If they use them well and top talents perform to expectation – and Daniels gets protection — Washington will be able to move the ball well. Pass rushers are a plus Remember way back when – like three weeks ago – when the Commanders pass rush looked explosive and a real force? You should. That occurred when Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson were healthy and active in camp. Daron Payne and newcomer Charles Omenihu are capable of getting good push up front. We saw examples of blitzers being impactful – think Amik Robertson getting home versus Detroit – and the group working well together The Oweh and Chaisson injuries seem short-term , even though they felt long ‘cause training camp’s a vortex with so much going on each day with the same passage of time. Those guys are back. So is Payne. Now add in the Daronte Jones wrinkles we haven’t seen yet and this defense will be able to get after the quarterback. Linebacker speed Some folks didn’t love Sonny Styles’ preseason performances , but that’s a small sample size compared to how he worked all camp. And don’t get me started on individual reps caught on video with no context. The first-round pick is going to be fine. We saw essentially nothing from Frankie Luvu in the preseason, and I think Leo Chenal will find an impactful role within the scheme. There’s little doubt about Styles’ speed. When he starts playing fast, we’ll see his true impact. There’s optimism about Luvu’s return to form and I’m still a big Chenal believer within Jones’ scheme. This was a position group of strength to start camp. It remains so now.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Articles Sports Illustrated Commanders believe Styles is developing into a defensive leader Having Luvu share [the green dot] responsibility should help. Styles won’t be thrown into every situation alone, and the veteran gives Washington another experienced voice who can handle the communication when personnel packages change. That should give Jones flexibility in who wears the green dot while still allowing Styles to grow into the role without forcing every part of the defense onto him at once. The bigger takeaway is how quickly Washington appears willing to trust him. There were always questions about how much Styles would be asked to handle as a rookie , especially in a defense with this many moving parts. The answer is becoming pretty clear. Washington didn’t draft him seventh overall just to make plays. They drafted him to become one of the pieces the defense can eventually revolve around, and giving him a hand in directing it before his first regular-season snap shows they may already be treating him that way. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders.com Commanders remain confident in their offensive line It’s worth pointing out that Washington’s current mashup of offensive linemen was not the plan the team had in mind. In a perfect world, Tunsil would remain the left tackle, Allegretti would have been on the field for most of camp and the duo of Sam Cosmi and Josh Conerly would have continued building their chemistry together on the right side. The only position that would have been undecided was left guard, but the team felt like it was in a good spot with either Coleman or Chris Paul. But Tunsil’s injury changed all that. The team likes what it has with Coleman at tackle, but that move affected the depth at guard. The uncertainty at guard put a brighter spotlight on the center position, which was already going through some flux with Allegretti’s injury. That’s a lot of uncertainty for a position at which Commanders need to be solid this season, but the team is looking at the situation with optimism. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag 8 Commanders whose stock could explode beyond recognition in 2026 Antonio Williams – Commanders WR The Washington Commanders’ wide receiver room looks strong. There are some proven performers and also some reclamation projects who could improve within David Blough’s system if everything goes well. There is also Antonio Williams . The third-round rookie wideout was projected as a first-rounder before a disappointing final college campaign with the Clemson Tigers. Williams has the talent, and the Commanders believe there is something that could be a major asset. Based on the impression made over the summer, he’s got a chance to feature as part of a trio with Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs. Williams is a slick route runner who knows how to separate. He’s got assured hands, can make things happen after the catch, and now has a chip on his shoulder after being overlooked until No. 71 overall in the draft. McLaurin and Diggs will lead the charge. But don’t be surprised if Williams becomes a surprise most don’t see coming. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders.com 5 takeaways from Dan Quinn and Adam Peters’ joint press conference The Commanders have dealt with multiple injuries over the past month, but there was some good news from Quinn: many of these players are working their way back to practice. Quinn started the press conference by announcing that Allegretti, Marcus Mariota, Daron Payne, Jordan Magee and Ben Sinnott would be back at practice. Mariota’s return is more of an insurance policy for Daniels, but players like Allegretti, Payne and the rest are either starters or will get significant playing time. Their returns provide them with valuable reps to prepare for the team’s Week 1 road game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Trey Amos, however, was not among the players who returned to practice, as he was placed on Injured Reserve earlier in the day. Amos will now have to miss at least the first four games of the season nursing an ankle injury he suffered in camp. Outside linebacker Odafe Oweh was also not among the players returning to practice, but Quinn said the team is “feeling good” about his progress. “We’re thrilled that he’s making this kind of progress to get ready.” To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders Roundtable 3 Commanders who can step up if Oweh isn’t ready to play in Week 1 Dan Quinn said Odafe Oweh is expected to return to practice next week. Whether that happens remains to be seen, but losing Oweh for Week 1 against the Eagles would be a major blow. Javontae Jean-Baptiste Jean-Baptiste has had the most complicated path of anyone in Washington’s edge room. A seventh-round pick out of Notre Dame in Peters’ first draft class in 2024, he spent most of his first two seasons either on injured reserve or playing limited rotational snaps behind a deep depth chart. A torn pectoral in 2025 cost him most of the year — he played just three games. But he came back healthy this spring, posted a 75.5 overall PFF grade across his limited 2025 snaps — with a 71.2 run-defense grade that ranked as one of the better marks among Washington’s edge defenders — and has been one of the more consistent veterans in camp this August. His career line is modest: 19 tackles and two sacks across 15 games. But the run defense and the effort level have never been the question. Against an Eagles offensive line that will likely try to establish the run early, Jean-Baptiste’s physicality and gap discipline make him a useful early-down piece if Oweh can’t go. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN Who calls plays for every NFL team in 2026? Blough spent one year in Minnesota learning coach Kevin O’Connell’s offense and was on Detroit’s practice squad in 2023 under coordinator Ben Johnson. Blough was influenced by Johnson in particular and will use a lot of play-action passes, more snaps from under center and far less no-huddle than Washington used under Kliff Kingsbury the past two years. They will retain some elements of Kingsbury’s system — some run-pass option. Blough also could mimic Johnson when it comes to trickery and creativity. — John Keim Key stat: Last season (with Blough as assistant quarterbacks coach and Kingsbury as offensive coordinator), the Commanders rushed on 61.4% of their red zone plays, the highest rate in the NFL. — ESPN Research To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Photos Commanders.com PHOTOS | Prep begins for Week 1 The Washington Commanders were back on the practice field for their first practice after final roster cuts View Link View Link View Link View Link Podcasts & videos COMMAND CENTER: ADAM PETERS COOKED! 🔥 Why the 2026 Commanders Are Built DIFFERENT | Podcast |…

title: 2026 NFL season X factors: Key players for all 32 teams
summary: What do Marvin Harrison Jr., Jared Verse and Travis Hunter have in common? The success of their teams could depend on them.
full_text:
The NFL season is but five days away -- we've almost made it! And as such, we've almost talked about these NFL teams and previewed this NFL season in as many ways as we can. Almost.

 Today, I have for you my yearly look at 32 X factors -- one for each team. X factor players, as I understand them, are players who can dramatically swing the season with their individual play. A helpful way of defining an X factor is "if this team has a surprisingly great year, I'm certain that this one player had a great season." X factors are the straw in the wind -- the way they bend is the way everything will go.

 Last year's X factors featured Seahawks RB  Kenneth Walker III  (Super Bowl MVP, I dunno if you heard), Cowboys WR George Pickens and Patriots WR Stefon Diggs . It's not just the good ones who are winners, unfortunately. Bills WR Keon Coleman , Steelers OT Broderick Jones and Buccaneers LB SirVocea Dennis were also key X factors ... whose season went the wrong way.

 Finding an X factor for each team is as much about what they aren't as what they are. Here are my self-imposed X factor restrictions, which force us to talk about players who we wouldn't otherwise touch on in such detail.

 No quarterbacks. Obviously , an elite season at quarterback will have a bigger impact on the team than any other position. Same with a disastrous one. Some quarterback X factors are certainly bigger than others (What if Kyler Murray is lights-out in Minnesota? What if Bryce Young falls apart in Carolina?). But all quarterbacks are huge factors. Which means none of them made this list.

 No coaches . See above quarterback explanation. All coaches are X factors, so we're not going to talk about them here.

 No rookies . Every team will experience a huge and surprising leap if it drafts  Puka Nacua in the fifth round. I think Bryce Lance is a huge X factor for the Saints, but there isn't much to say about it besides "drafting a starting wide receiver on Day 3 is really helpful." Safely assume I think every rookie your team drafted (and even a few of the UDFAs) are X factors, and read on.

 Now that we've defined what an X factor is (and isn't), we can get into the nitty-gritty. There were a few good candidates for each team, but I had to land on one per franchise (or cheat and do two -- which I did). Here they are, starting with a desperately needed breakout in Arizona.

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 NFC WEST 
 

 Arizona Cardinals : WR Marvin Harrison Jr . 
 There are only a few players on the Cardinals' roster who I'm confident are above-average starters. On defense, there is safety Budda Baker and edge rusher Josh Sweat , and tight end Trey McBride and wide receiver Michael Wilson on offense. With rookie and third pick Jeremiyah Love , a prospect I loved coming out of Notre Dame, we are close to a third offensive player -- all skill position guys.

 So imagine if Harrison can take a leap under a new offensive coaching staff. New head coach Mike LaFleur, a branch off the old Sean McVay tree, comes from an offense that doesn't typically enjoy a traditional X-receiver -- 6-foot-4, big frame, running all sorts of sideline routes. As such, it's fair to expect the Cardinals to move Harrison around the formation more than he has been to this point in his career. Over the past two seasons, 78.6% of Harrison's targets have come from out wide (24th among 106 wide receivers), and he has averaged 13.1 air yards per target (17th). Some easier targets from the slot and in motion would be welcome for a player whose superpower in college was route running.

 The Cardinals' quarterback play figures to be rough this season, but hits on Love and Harrison could give Arizona such a deluge of playmakers that its offense remains dangerous even with below-average quarterback play. And if they end up investing by drafting a quarterback high in 2027, a Harrison breakout would make the bedrock for that quarterback's development all the richer.

 
 
 

 

 Los Angeles Rams : LB Nate Landman 
 The Rams' defense will be elite with Myles Garrett , Aaron Donald , Kobie Turner and Byron Young up front and Trent McDuffie , Jaylen Watson , Kam Curl and Quentin Lake in the secondary. These are good players at key positions with a few elite players to boot. I believe in this group immensely.

 But if something goes wrong, the linebacker spot feels like the culprit. I expect the Rams to play a ton of dime personnel and other one-linebacker packages as they strive to get their best 11 on the field. They feel great about Landman, whom they signed to a one-year deal in March 2025 and gave a three-year extension eight months later after he quickly developed into a starting linebacker. Sometimes, those breakouts work great ( Zack Baun ). Sometimes, they can be total fool's gold.

 In an effort to hide from the Rams' pass rush and avoid their new cornerbacks room, I expect offenses to get the ball out quickly to backs and tight ends -- a passing attack that will challenge Landman in coverage and force him to tackle in space. Another avenue to attack this loaded Rams' defense: get in heavy personnel and run the air out of the ball. Again, Landman will be the first line of defense for finding run stops and TFLs to give his pass rush opportunities to shine.

 I'm a Landman believer. But if 2025 was a magical season whose heights cannot be recaptured, opposing offenses will quickly put him under the microscope as the one Achilles' heel on the Rams' defense.

 

 
 

 San Francisco 49ers : WR Mike Evans 
 I loved the Evans signing. Getting Kyle Shanahan the type of receiver he had lacked since becoming the head coach of the 49ers -- a big, long, downfield ball-winner, short-yardage specialist and red zone mismatch -- opened new and exciting possibilities in the offense. Evans is also much better on the classic 49ers routes than he's given credit for. Among all receivers over the past two seasons, Evans is third in yards per route run (6.1) on deep, in-breaking routes. His 6-foot-5, 230-pound frame is hard to miss in the middle of the field.

 But Evans is 33 years old, so managing his snaps is important. Once Ricky Pearsall was ruled out for the season because of a right UCL tear, I was worried Evans would take too many snaps this season, especially coming off a hamstring injury in 2025. And then Evans started to miss time in camp: a quad strain in late July, then some talk about groin issues. Worrisome drumbeats for an older receiver in August.

 I still really like the blend of skills in a 49ers receivers room featuring Evans, rookie De'Zhaun Stribling , and veterans Deebo Samuel Sr . and Demarcus Robinson . But if Evans cannot stay on the field or is absent of twitch when he's on it, there's not enough downfield playmaking in the group (unless Stribling is the Offensive Rookie of the Year). The floor for any Shanahan-led offense is very high, but the ceiling this year is set by Evans.

 

 
 

 Seattle Seahawks : S  Ty Okada 
 The Seahawks' stars in the defensive backfield -- cornerback Devon Witherspoon and safeties Nick Emmanwori and Julian Love -- are well-known. The key departures of cornerback Riq Woolen (Eagles) and safety Coby Bryant (Bears) challenge their depth, especially when lighter personnel such as dime is needed. The plan was for their second-round pick, safety Bud Clark , to replace Bryant in the starting lineup, but Clark suffered a broken right ankle in the second preseason game and is out for the season.

 One of the young players who must rise to fill the accumulating voids is Okada, the fourth-year safety out of Montana State. An undrafted free agent who worked his way up the depth chart, Okada had to start multiple stretches last season when Love and Bryant went down because of injury. He proved effective at…
